title.zh: '''卷二百二十一上''' 列傳第一百四十六上 西域上

meta.sourceNote: Body created from Wikisource raw text because the ChineseNotes scrape produced a zero-byte file.

sentences.zh: ◎西域上泥婆羅泥婆羅，直吐蕃之西樂陵川。

translations.literal: Western Regions, upper section: Nipoluo. Nipoluo lies directly west of Tibet on the Leling River.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Regions, upper section: Nepal. Nepal lies directly west of Tibet on the Leling River.

sentences.zh: 土多赤銅、犛牛。

translations.literal: The land abounds in red copper and yaks.
translations.idiomatic: The country is rich in red copper and yaks.

sentences.zh: 俗翦發逮眉，穿耳，楦以筒若角，緩至肩者為姣好。

translations.literal: By custom they cut their hair to the eyebrows, pierce their ears, and stretch them with horn-like tubes; those that hang down to the shoulders are considered beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: The people cut their hair to eyebrow level, pierce their ears, and insert horn-shaped tubes to elongate the lobes; ornaments that reach the shoulders are regarded as a mark of beauty.

sentences.zh: 無匕箸，攫而食。

translations.literal: They have no spoons or chopsticks and eat by grabbing with their hands.
translations.idiomatic: They use neither spoons nor chopsticks, but eat with their hands.

sentences.zh: 其器皆用銅，其居版屋畫壁。

translations.literal: All their vessels are made of copper; their dwellings are plank houses with painted walls.
translations.idiomatic: They make all their utensils from copper and live in timber houses with painted walls.

sentences.zh: 俗不知牛耕，故少田作，習商賈。

translations.literal: By custom they do not know ox-plowing, hence they cultivate little land and are practiced in trade.
translations.idiomatic: Having no tradition of plowing with oxen, they do little farming and live mainly by commerce.

sentences.zh: 一幅布蔽身，日數盥浴。

translations.literal: A single bolt of cloth covers the body; they bathe several times a day.
translations.idiomatic: A single length of cloth suffices for dress, and they wash themselves several times daily.

sentences.zh: 重博戲，通推步歷術。

translations.literal: They value gambling games and are versed in divination and calendrical arts.
translations.idiomatic: Gambling is popular among them, and they are skilled in astronomy and calendrical calculation.

sentences.zh: 祀天神，鐫石為象，日浴之，烹羊以祭。

translations.literal: They worship the heavenly god, carving stone into an image, bathing it daily, and sacrificing boiled sheep.
translations.idiomatic: They worship a heavenly deity, carving his image in stone, bathing it each day, and offering boiled sheep in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 鑄銅為錢，面文人形，背牛馬形。

translations.literal: They cast copper into coins, with a human figure on the face and ox and horse figures on the reverse.
translations.idiomatic: Their currency is cast copper, bearing a human figure on one side and images of cattle and horses on the other.

sentences.zh: 其君服珠、頗黎、車渠、珊瑚、虎魄垂纓，耳金鉤玉珰，佩寶伏突，禦師子大床，燎香布花於堂，而大臣坐地不藉。

translations.literal: Their ruler wears pearls, glass, crystal, coral, and amber hanging from his headdress, gold hooks and jade earrings in his ears, and precious ornaments at his belt; he sits upon a large bed with a lion canopy, burns incense and spreads flowers in the hall, while his ministers sit on the bare ground without mats.
translations.idiomatic: The king adorns himself with pearls, glass, crystal, coral, and amber in his headdress, gold ear-hooks and jade pendants, and precious belt ornaments. He receives audiences from a lion-canopied couch, with incense burned and flowers strewn in the hall, while his ministers sit on the bare floor without cushions.

sentences.zh: 左右持兵，數百列侍。

translations.literal: Attendants on left and right hold weapons; several hundred stand in rows to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Armed attendants flank him on both sides, with hundreds standing in ranks to serve.

sentences.zh: 宮中有七重樓，覆銅瓦，楹極皆大琲雜寶，四隅置銅槽，下有金龍，口激水仰註槽中。

translations.literal: Within the palace is a seven-tiered tower roofed with copper tiles; pillars and beams are all inlaid with large pearls and assorted treasures. At the four corners are bronze troughs, beneath which golden dragons spout water upward into the troughs.
translations.idiomatic: The palace contains a seven-story tower roofed in copper tiles, with pillars and beams inlaid with large pearls and precious stones. At each corner stands a bronze trough fed by golden dragons whose mouths shoot water upward into it.

sentences.zh: 初，王那陵提婆之父為其叔所殺，提婆出奔，吐蕃納之，遂臣吐蕃。

translations.literal: At first, King Nalingtipo's father was killed by his uncle. Tipuo fled into exile; Tibet received him, and he thereupon became a subject of Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, King Nalingtipo's father had been murdered by his uncle. Tipuo fled into exile, was taken in by Tibet, and thereafter submitted to Tibetan rule.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，遣使者李義表到天竺，道其國，提婆大喜，延使者同觀阿耆婆爾池。

translations.literal: During the Zhenguan era, the envoy Li Yibiao was sent to Tianzhu and passed through their country. Tipuo was greatly pleased and invited the envoy to view Lake Aqipoer together.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign, when the envoy Li Yibiao was dispatched to India and passed through Nepal, Tipuo was delighted and invited him to visit Lake Aqipoer together.

sentences.zh: 池廣數十丈，水常溢沸，共傳旱潦未始耗溢。

translations.literal: The lake is several tens of zhang wide; its waters constantly bubble and overflow. It is commonly said that through drought and flood it never diminishes or rises excessively.
translations.idiomatic: The lake spans several tens of zhang; its waters perpetually bubble and overflow. Tradition holds that through drought and flood alike it neither dries up nor rises beyond its bounds.

sentences.zh: 或抵以物則生煙，釜其上，少選可熟。

translations.literal: If one touches it with an object, smoke arises; place a pot above it and food is cooked in no time.
translations.idiomatic: Touch an object to its surface and smoke rises; set a pot above it and food cooks in moments.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，遣使入獻波棱、酢菜、渾提蔥。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, they sent envoys to present boleng, pickled vegetables, and hunti scallions.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Zhenguan, they sent envoys bearing boleng spinach, pickled vegetables, and hunti scallions as tribute.

sentences.zh: 永徽時，其王屍利那連陀羅又遣使入貢。

translations.literal: During the Yonghui period, their king Shilinaliantuoluo again sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui reign, their king Shilinaliantuoluo again dispatched envoys to pay tribute.

sentences.zh: 党項，漢西羌別種，魏、晉後微甚。

translations.literal: Tangut. The Tangut were a separate branch of the Western Qiang of Han times; after Wei and Jin they declined greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut were a branch of the Western Qiang known in Han times; after the Wei and Jin dynasties they fell into sharp decline.

sentences.zh: 周滅宕昌、鄧至，而党項始強。

translations.literal: When Zhou destroyed Dangchang and Dengzhi, the Tangut first grew strong.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the Zhou dynasty destroyed Dangchang and Dengzhi did the Tangut begin to rise in power.

sentences.zh: 其地古析支也，東距松州，西葉護，南舂桑、迷桑等羌，北吐谷渾。

translations.literal: Their territory was ancient Qizhi. To the east it bordered Songzhou; to the west, Yehu; to the south, the Chunsang, Misang, and other Qiang peoples; to the north, Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands were the ancient territory of Qizhi, bounded on the east by Songzhou, on the west by Yehu, on the south by the Chunsang, Misang, and other Qiang tribes, and on the north by Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 處山谷崎嶇，大抵三千里。

translations.literal: They dwelt in rugged mountain valleys, roughly three thousand li in extent.
translations.idiomatic: They inhabited rugged mountain valleys covering roughly three thousand li.

sentences.zh: 以姓別為部，一姓又分為小部落，大者萬騎，小數千，不能相統，故有細封氏、費聽氏，往利氏、頗超氏、野辭氏、房當氏、米禽氏、拓拔氏、而拓拔最強。

translations.literal: They were divided into clans by surname; each surname was further split into small tribes, the large ones fielding ten thousand horsemen and the small ones several thousand. Unable to command one another, there arose the Xifeng, Feiting, Wangli, Pichao, Yeci, Fangdang, Miqin, and Tuoba clans, of which the Tuoba were strongest.
translations.idiomatic: They organized themselves into clans by surname, each surname further divided into smaller tribes numbering up to ten thousand horsemen or as few as several thousand. Lacking unified leadership, they formed such clans as the Xifeng, Feiting, Wangli, Pichao, Yeci, Fangdang, Miqin, and Tuoba, among whom the Tuoba were the most powerful.

sentences.zh: 土著，有棟宇，織犛尾、羊毛覆屋，歲一易。

translations.literal: They were settled inhabitants with permanent dwellings; they wove yak tails and sheep's wool to cover their houses, replacing them once a year.
translations.idiomatic: They were sedentary people who built permanent houses, roofing them with woven yak tails and sheep's wool, which they replaced once each year.

sentences.zh: 俗尚武，無法令、賦役。

translations.literal: By custom they valued martial prowess; they had no laws, statutes, or corvée levies.
translations.idiomatic: They were a martial people by custom, with no written laws or system of taxation and corvée.

sentences.zh: 人壽多過百歲，然好為盜，更相剽奪。

translations.literal: People's lifespans often exceeded a hundred years, yet they were fond of banditry and plundered one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: They commonly lived past a hundred years, yet they were given to robbery and raided one another ceaselessly.

sentences.zh: 尤重復讎，未得所欲者，蓬首垢顏，跣足草食，殺已乃復。

translations.literal: They especially valued blood vengeance. Those who had not yet achieved their desire went with disheveled hair and grimy faces, barefoot and eating wild plants, until they had killed their target and only then returned to normal life.
translations.idiomatic: Blood vengeance was paramount among them. Until a man had killed his enemy, he went about with unkempt hair and a filthy face, barefoot and eating only wild plants; only after the killing would he resume ordinary life.

sentences.zh: 男女衣裘褐，被氈。

translations.literal: Men and women wore fur and coarse cloth and wrapped themselves in felt.
translations.idiomatic: Both men and women dressed in furs and coarse woolens and wrapped themselves in felt.

sentences.zh: 畜犛牛、馬、驢、羊以食，不耕稼。

translations.literal: They raised yaks, horses, donkeys, and sheep for food and did not cultivate crops.
translations.idiomatic: They kept yaks, horses, donkeys, and sheep for sustenance and did not practice agriculture.

sentences.zh: 地寒，五月草生，八月霜降。

translations.literal: The land was cold; grass sprouted in the fifth month and frost fell in the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was harsh: grass did not appear until the fifth month, and frost came by the eighth.

sentences.zh: 無文字，候草木記歲。

translations.literal: They had no writing and reckoned the years by observing plants and trees.
translations.idiomatic: They had no written language and marked the passage of years by watching the growth and withering of plants.

sentences.zh: 三年一相聚，殺牛羊祭天，取麥他國以釀酒。

translations.literal: Once every three years they gathered together, slaughtered cattle and sheep to sacrifice to Heaven, and obtained grain from other states to brew wine.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years they assembled to sacrifice cattle and sheep to Heaven, importing grain from neighboring peoples to brew wine for the rite.

sentences.zh: 妻其庶母、伯叔母、兄嫂、子弟婦，惟不娶同姓。

translations.literal: A man might marry his stepmother, paternal uncle's wife, elder brother's widow, and younger brother's wife, but not one of the same surname.
translations.idiomatic: Men might take as wives their stepmothers, paternal uncles' widows, sisters-in-law, and brothers' wives, but marriage within the same clan was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 老而死，子孫不哭；

translations.literal: When the old died of natural causes, descendants did not weep.
translations.idiomatic: When an elder died of old age, his descendants did not mourn with tears.

sentences.zh: 少死，則曰夭枉，乃悲。

translations.literal: When the young died, they called it premature and wrongful death, and then they grieved.
translations.idiomatic: When the young died, they called it an untimely death and wept in grief.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，南會州都督鄭元璹鐫諭，其酋細封步賴舉部降。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan, Zheng Yuansui, military governor of Nanhui Prefecture, engraved and sent proclamations of instruction; their chieftain Xifeng Bulai led his entire tribe in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenguan, Zheng Yuansui, governor of Nanhui Prefecture, issued engraved proclamations urging submission, and the chieftain Xifeng Bulai led his entire tribe to surrender.

sentences.zh: 太宗璽詔慰撫，步賴因入朝，宴錫特異，以其地為軌州，即授刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong issued an imperial edict of consolation and reassurance. Bulai thereupon came to court, was feasted and rewarded with exceptional gifts, and his territory was made into Guizhou, with him appointed prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong issued an imperial edict of reassurance. Bulai then came to court, was entertained with exceptional honors, and his lands were organized as Guizhou, with Bulai appointed its prefect.

sentences.zh: 步賴請率兵討吐谷渾。

translations.literal: Bulai requested to lead troops to campaign against Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Bulai offered to lead his warriors against Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 其後諸酋長悉內屬，以其地為居、奉、嚴、遠四州，即首領拜刺史。

translations.literal: Thereafter all the chieftains submitted inward, and their territories were made into the four prefectures of Ju, Feng, Yan, and Yuan, with the chieftains appointed prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Subsequently all the chieftains submitted, and their lands were organized as the four prefectures of Ju, Feng, Yan, and Yuan, with each chieftain appointed prefect.

sentences.zh: 有拓拔赤辭者，初臣吐谷渾，慕容伏允待之厚，與結婚，諸羌已歸，獨不至。

translations.literal: There was one Tuoba Chici, who at first served Tuyuhun. Murong Fuyun treated him generously and formed a marriage alliance with him. When the other Qiang had submitted, he alone did not come.
translations.idiomatic: One Tuoba Chici had initially served Tuyuhun. Murong Fuyun treated him with great favor and sealed the bond with a marriage alliance. When the other Qiang tribes submitted, Chici alone held back.

sentences.zh: 李靖擊吐谷渾，赤辭屯狼道峽抗王師。

translations.literal: When Li Jing attacked Tuyuhun, Chici stationed troops at Langdao Gorge to resist the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing marched against Tuyuhun, Chici fortified Langdao Gorge to block the imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 廓州刺史久且洛生欲諭降之，辭曰：「渾主以腹心待我，不知其佗，若速去，且汙吾刀。」

translations.literal: Jiuqie Luosheng, prefect of Kuozhou, wished to persuade him to surrender. Chici replied: "The Tuyuhun lord treated me as a trusted confidant; I know no other loyalty. If you press me to leave, you will only stain my blade.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuqie Luosheng, prefect of Kuozhou, sought to persuade him to surrender. Chici replied: "The Tuyuhun ruler treated me as one of his inner circle; I owe loyalty to no other. Urge me to desert, and you will only force me to draw my sword.

sentences.zh: 洛生怒，引輕騎破之肅遠山，斬首數百級，虜雜畜六千。

translations.literal: Luosheng grew angry, led light cavalry, and defeated him at Suyuan Mountain, taking several hundred heads and six thousand mixed livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Luosheng led light cavalry and routed Chici at Mount Suyuan, taking several hundred heads and six thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 帝因其勝又令約降，赤辭從子思頭潛納款，其下拓拔細豆亦降。

translations.literal: The emperor, because of this victory, again ordered negotiations for surrender. Chici's nephew Sitou secretly pledged allegiance, and his subordinate Tuoba Xidou also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Following this victory, the emperor renewed overtures for surrender. Chici's nephew Sitou secretly submitted, and his subordinate Tuoba Xidou surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 赤辭知宗族攜沮，稍欲自歸，岷州都督劉師立復誘之，即與思頭俱內屬。

translations.literal: Chici, knowing his clansmen were divided and discouraged, gradually wished to submit of his own accord. Liu Shili, military governor of Minzhou, again enticed him, and he and Sitou both submitted inward.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his clansmen wavering, Chici gradually inclined toward surrender. Liu Shili, governor of Minzhou, renewed his overtures, and Chici and Sitou both submitted.

sentences.zh: 以其地為懿、嵯、麟、可三十二州，以松州為都督府，擢赤辭西戎州都督，賜氏李，貢職遂不絕。

translations.literal: Their territory was made into the thirty-two prefectures of Yi, Cuo, Lin, and Ke; Songzhou was made a military governorship; Chici was promoted to military governor of Xirong Prefecture and granted the surname Li; tribute duties thereafter never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands were organized as thirty-two prefectures including Yi, Cuo, Lin, and Ke, with Songzhou established as a military governorship. Chici was appointed military governor of Xirong Prefecture and granted the surname Li; tribute thereafter flowed without interruption.

sentences.zh: 於是自河首積石山而東，皆為中國地。

translations.literal: From this time, from the headwaters of the Yellow River at Jishi Mountain eastward, all became Chinese territory.
translations.idiomatic: From this point forward, all lands from the headwaters of the Yellow River at Jishi Mountain eastward fell within the Chinese domain.

sentences.zh: 後吐蕃浸盛，拓拔畏逼，請內徙，始詔慶州置靜邊等州處之。

translations.literal: Later, as Tibet gradually grew powerful, the Tuoba, fearing pressure, requested resettlement inward. An edict was first issued to establish Jingbian and other prefectures in Qingzhou to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Tibetan power grew, the Tuoba, fearing encroachment, petitioned to move inward. The court first ordered the establishment of Jingbian and other prefectures in Qingzhou to receive them.

sentences.zh: 地乃入吐蕃，其處者皆為吐蕃役屬，更號弭藥。

translations.literal: Their former lands then passed into Tibetan control; those who remained there all became subject to Tibetan service and were renamed Miyao.
translations.idiomatic: Their original territory then fell under Tibetan control, and those who remained there became Tibetan subjects, taking the name Miyao.

sentences.zh: 又有黑党項者，居赤水西。

translations.literal: There were also the Black Tangut, who dwelt west of Chishui.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the Black Tangut, who lived west of the Chishui River.

sentences.zh: 其長號敦善王，慕容伏允之走也依之。

translations.literal: Their leader was titled King Dunshan. When Murong Fuyun fled, he relied upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Their leader bore the title King Dunshan. When Murong Fuyun fled, he took refuge with them.

sentences.zh: 及吐谷渾款附，敦善王亦納貢。

translations.literal: When Tuyuhun sincerely submitted, King Dunshan also offered tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuyuhun submitted in good faith, King Dunshan also sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 居雪山者曰破醜氏。

translations.literal: Those who dwelt in the snow mountains were called the Pochou clan.
translations.idiomatic: Those who lived in the snow mountains were known as the Pochou clan.

sentences.zh: 又有白蘭羌，吐蕃謂之丁零，左屬党項，右與多彌接。

translations.literal: There were also the Bailan Qiang, whom the Tibetans called Dingling. To the left they were affiliated with the Tangut; to the right they bordered Duomi.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the Bailan Qiang, whom the Tibetans called the Dingling. On their left they were allied with the Tangut; on their right they bordered Duomi.

sentences.zh: 勝兵萬人，勇戰鬥，善作兵，俗與党項同。

translations.literal: Their effective fighting force numbered ten thousand men. They fought bravely and were skilled at making weapons; their customs were the same as the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: They could field ten thousand warriors, fought with courage, and were skilled armorers; their customs matched those of the Tangut.

sentences.zh: 武德六年，使者入朝。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wude, envoys came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Wude, they sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 明年，以其地為維、恭二州。

translations.literal: The following year, their territory was made into the two prefectures of Wei and Gong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, their lands were organized as the two prefectures of Wei and Gong.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年，與契數十萬內屬。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan, they and the Qi, numbering several hundred thousand, submitted inward.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenguan, they and the Qi people, numbering several hundred thousand, submitted to the court.

sentences.zh: 永徽時，特浪生羌卜樓大首領凍就率眾來屬，以其地為劍州。

translations.literal: During the Yonghui period, the great chieftain Dongjiu of the Telangsheng Qiang Bolou led his people to submit; their territory was made into Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui reign, Dongjiu, great chieftain of the Telangsheng Qiang Bolou, led his people to submit, and their lands were organized as Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 龍朔後，白蘭、舂桑及白狗羌為吐蕃所臣，籍其兵為前驅。

translations.literal: After the Longshuo era, the Bailan, Chunsang, and Baigou Qiang were made subjects by Tibet, and their troops were registered as vanguard forces.
translations.idiomatic: After the Longshuo era, the Bailan, Chunsang, and Baigou Qiang were subjugated by Tibet, whose armies conscripted them as front-line troops.

sentences.zh: 白狗與東會州接，勝兵才千人。

translations.literal: The Baigou bordered Donghuizhou; their effective fighting force was only a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The Baigou bordered Donghuizhou and could field only a thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 在西北者，天授中內附，戶凡二十萬，以其地為朝、吳、浮、歸十州，散居靈、夏間。

translations.literal: Those in the northwest submitted inward during the Tianshou era, with households totaling two hundred thousand. Their territory was made into the ten prefectures of Chao, Wu, Fu, and Gui, scattered between Ling and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: The northwestern Tangut submitted during the Tianshou era, numbering two hundred thousand households. Their lands were organized as ten prefectures including Chao, Wu, Fu, and Gui, and they were settled across the region between Ling and Xia.

sentences.zh: 至德末，為吐蕃所誘，使為鄉導鈔邊。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhide era, they were enticed by Tibet and made to serve as guides in raiding the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Zhide era, the Tibetans incited them to serve as guides in frontier raids.

sentences.zh: 俄悔悟，更來朝，願助靈州餉免。

translations.literal: Soon they repented, came again to court, and wished to assist in supplying Lingzhou in exchange for exemption from levies.
translations.idiomatic: They soon repented, returned to court, and offered to help supply Lingzhou in exchange for tax relief.

sentences.zh: 乾元間，中國數亂，因寇邠、寧二州，肅宗詔郭子儀都統朔方、邠寧、鄜坊節度事，以鄜州刺史杜冕、邠州刺史桑如圭分二隊出討。

translations.literal: During the Qianyuan era, China suffered repeated turmoil, and they therefore raided Bin and Ning prefectures. Emperor Suzong ordered Guo Ziyi to take overall command of the Shuofang, Binning, and Fufang frontier commands, with Du Mian, prefect of Fu Prefecture, and Sang Rugui, prefect of Bin Prefecture, leading two columns to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyuan era, as China was torn by repeated upheaval, the Tangut raided Bin and Ning prefectures. Emperor Suzong placed Guo Ziyi in overall command of the Shuofang, Binning, and Fufang commands and dispatched Du Mian of Fu Prefecture and Sang Rugui of Bin Prefecture with two columns to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 子儀至，党項潰去。

translations.literal: When Ziyi arrived, the Tangut broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Ziyi arrived, the Tangut forces broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 上元元年，在涇、隴部落十萬眾詣鳳翔節度使崔光遠降。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan, tribes in Jing and Long numbering one hundred thousand submitted to Cui Guangyuan, military governor of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shangyuan, Tangut tribes in Jing and Long numbering one hundred thousand submitted to Cui Guangyuan, military governor of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 二年，與渾、奴剌連和，寇寶雞，殺吏民，掠財珍，焚大散關，入鳳州，殺刺史蕭𢘽，節度使李鼎追擊走之。

translations.literal: In the second year, they allied with the Hun and Nula, raided Baoji, killed officials and commoners, plundered valuables, burned Dasan Pass, entered Feng Prefecture, and killed Prefect Xiao Kui. Military Governor Li Ding pursued and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, allied with the Hun and Nula tribes, they raided Baoji, slaughtered officials and civilians, plundered valuables, burned Dasan Pass, entered Feng Prefecture, and killed Prefect Xiao Kui before being driven off by Military Governor Li Ding.

sentences.zh: 明年，又攻梁州，刺史李勉走；

translations.literal: The following year, they again attacked Liang Prefecture, and Prefect Li Mian fled.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they attacked Liang Prefecture again, and Prefect Li Mian fled.

sentences.zh: 進寇奉天，大掠華原、同官去。

translations.literal: Advancing to raid Fengtian, they plundered heavily in Huayuan and Tongguan before departing.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on to raid Fengtian, looting Huayuan and Tongguan before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 詔臧希讓代勉為刺史，於是歸順、乾封、歸義、順化、和寧、和義、保善、寧定、羅雲、朝鳳凡十州部落詣希讓獻款，丐節印。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Zang Xirang to replace Mian as prefect. Thereupon tribes of the ten prefectures of Guishun, Qianfeng, Guiyi, Shunhua, He'ning, Heyi, Baoshan, Ningding, Luoyun, and Chaofeng came to Xirang to offer allegiance and begged for command seals and insignia.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Zang Xirang to replace Li Mian as prefect. Tribes from ten prefectures—Guishun, Qianfeng, Guiyi, Shunhua, He'ning, Heyi, Baoshan, Ningding, Luoyun, and Chaofeng—then came to Xirang to swear allegiance and petitioned for command seals and insignia.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict granted approval.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved their request.

sentences.zh: 仆固懷恩之叛，誘党項、渾、奴剌入寇，眾數萬，掠鳳翔、盩厔。

translations.literal: When Pugu Huai'en rebelled, he incited the Tangut, Hun, and Nula to raid inward; their forces numbered tens of thousands, and they plundered Fengxiang and Zhouzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Pugu Huai'en rebelled, he incited the Tangut, Hun, and Nula to join the invasion. Their combined forces numbered in the tens of thousands and ravaged Fengxiang and Zhouzhi.

sentences.zh: 大酋鄭廷、郝德入同州，刺史韋勝走，節度使周智光破之澄城。

translations.literal: Great chieftains Zheng Ting and Hao De entered Tong Prefecture; Prefect Wei Sheng fled, and Military Governor Zhou Zhiguang defeated them at Chengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Great chieftains Zheng Ting and Hao De entered Tong Prefecture. Prefect Wei Sheng fled, and Military Governor Zhou Zhiguang defeated them at Chengcheng.

sentences.zh: 閱月，又入同州，焚官私室廬，壁馬蘭山。

translations.literal: Within a month, they entered Tong Prefecture again, burned public and private buildings, and fortified themselves at Mount Malan.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month they invaded Tong Prefecture again, burning public and private buildings before fortifying themselves on Mount Malan.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀遣兵襲之，退保三堡，子儀遣慕容休明諭降廷、德。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi dispatched troops to attack them; they retreated to hold three fortresses. Ziyi sent Murong Xiuming to persuade Ting and De to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi sent troops to attack them; they fell back to three fortified positions. Ziyi then dispatched Murong Xiuming to negotiate the surrender of Ting and De.

sentences.zh: 子儀以党項、吐谷渾部落散處鹽、慶等州，其地與吐蕃濱近，易相脅，即表徙靜邊州都督、夏州、樂容等六府党項於銀州之北、夏州之東、寧朔州吐谷渾住夏西，以離沮之。

translations.literal: Ziyi, because Tangut and Tuyuhun tribes were scattered in Yan, Qing, and other prefectures, with lands close to Tibet where they could easily be coerced, submitted a memorial to relocate the military governor of Jingbian Prefecture, the Tangut of the six prefectures of Xia, Lerong, and others north of Yin Prefecture and east of Xia Prefecture, and the Tuyuhun of Ningshuo Prefecture west of Xia, in order to separate and discourage them.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi observed that Tangut and Tuyuhun tribes scattered across Yan, Qing, and neighboring prefectures lay too close to Tibet and were easily intimidated into collusion. He memorialized the throne to relocate the Jingbian military governor's Tangut subjects from six prefectures including Xia and Lerong to lands north of Yin Prefecture and east of Xia Prefecture, and the Ningshuo Tuyuhun to the west of Xia, so as to break up their alliance with Tibet.

sentences.zh: 召靜邊州大首領左羽林大將軍拓拔朝光等五刺史入朝，厚賜賫，使還綏其部。

translations.literal: The great chieftain of Jingbian Prefecture, Left Imperial Guard General Tuoba Chaoguang, and five prefects were summoned to court, richly rewarded, and sent back to pacify their tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Chaoguang, great chieftain of Jingbian Prefecture and Left Imperial Guard General, along with five prefects, were summoned to court, lavishly rewarded, and sent back to pacify their people.

sentences.zh: 先是，慶州有破醜氏族三、野利氏族五、把利氏族一，與吐蕃姻援，贊普悉王之，因是擾邊凡十年。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Qing Prefecture there were three Pochou clans, five Yeli clans, and one Bali clan, allied by marriage with Tibet. The Tibetan king made them all his subjects, and for this reason the frontier was disturbed for some ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Qing Prefecture had housed three Pochou clans, five Yeli clans, and one Bali clan, all linked to Tibet by marriage alliances. The Tibetan king brought them all under his rule, and for a decade they harassed the frontier.

sentences.zh: 子儀表工部尚書路嗣恭為朔方留後，將作少監梁進用為押党項部落使，置行慶州。

translations.literal: Ziyi submitted a memorial appointing Minister of Works Lu Sigong as acting commander of Shuofang and Assistant Director of Palace Construction Liang Jinyong as commissioner overseeing Tangut tribes, establishing a provisional Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi recommended Minister of Works Lu Sigong as acting commander of Shuofang and Assistant Director of Palace Construction Liang Jinyong as commissioner over Tangut tribes, with a provisional Qing Prefecture established.

sentences.zh: 且言：「党項陰結吐蕃為變，可遣使者招慰，芟其反謀，因令進用為慶州刺史，嚴邏以絕吐蕃往來道。」

translations.literal: He also stated: "The Tangut are secretly allied with Tibet and may rebel. Envoys may be dispatched to win them over and uproot their plot; Jinyong should then be made prefect of Qing Prefecture and patrols tightened to cut off the routes of Tibetan communication.
translations.idiomatic: He further argued: "The Tangut are secretly allied with Tibet and may rise in rebellion. Send envoys to win them over and uproot their conspiracy; then appoint Jinyong prefect of Qing Prefecture and tighten patrols to sever Tibetan lines of communication.

sentences.zh: 代宗然之。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 又表置靜邊、芳池、相興王州都督、長史，永平、旭定、清寧、寧保、忠順、靜塞、萬吉等七州都督府。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial to establish military governors and chief administrators for Jingbian, Fangchi, and Xiangxing Prefectures, and military governorships for the seven prefectures of Yongping, Xuding, Qingning, Ningbao, Zhongshun, Jingsai, and Wanji.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned to establish military governors and chief administrators for Jingbian, Fangchi, and Xiangxing prefectures, and military governorships for Yongping, Xuding, Qingning, Ningbao, Zhongshun, Jingsai, and Wanji.

sentences.zh: 於是破醜、野利、把利三部及思樂州刺史拓拔乞梅等皆入朝，宜定州刺史折磨布落、芳池州野利部並徙綏、延州。

translations.literal: Thereupon the three tribes of Pochou, Yeli, and Bali, along with Tuoba Qimei, prefect of Sile Prefecture, and others all came to court. Mozhaboluo, prefect of Yiding Prefecture, and the Yeli tribe of Fangchi Prefecture were both relocated to Sui and Yan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Pochou, Yeli, and Bali tribes, along with Tuoba Qimei, prefect of Sile Prefecture, and others all came to court. Mozhaboluo of Yiding Prefecture and the Yeli tribe of Fangchi Prefecture were both resettled in Sui and Yan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 大歷末，野利禿羅都與吐蕃叛，招餘族不應，子儀擊之，斬禿羅都，而野利景庭、野利剛以其部數千人入附雞子川。

translations.literal: At the end of the Dali era, Yeli Tuluodu rebelled with Tibet and summoned the remaining clans, but they did not respond. Ziyi attacked, beheaded Tuluodu, and Yeli Jingting and Yeli Gang led several thousand of their tribesmen to submit at Jizichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Dali era, Yeli Tuluodu rebelled alongside Tibet and called upon the remaining clans to join him, but they refused. Guo Ziyi attacked, executed Tuluodu, and Yeli Jingting and Yeli Gang led several thousand of their people to submit at Jizichuan.

sentences.zh: 六州部落，曰：野利越詩、野利龍兒、野利厥律、兒黃、野海、野窣等；

translations.literal: The tribes of the six prefectures were: Yeli Yueshi, Yeli Long'er, Yeli Juelü, Erhuang, Yehai, Yesu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: The six-prefecture tribes included the Yeli Yueshi, Yeli Long'er, Yeli Juelü, Erhuang, Yehai, Yesu, and others.

sentences.zh: 居慶州者號東山部，夏州者號平夏部。

translations.literal: Those dwelling in Qing Prefecture were called the Eastern Mountain Division; those in Xia Prefecture were called the Pingxia Division.
translations.idiomatic: Those settled in Qing Prefecture were known as the Eastern Mountain Division; those in Xia Prefecture as the Pingxia Division.

sentences.zh: 永泰後稍徙石州，後為永安將阿史那思柬賦索無極，遂亡走河西。

translations.literal: After the Yongtai era they gradually moved to Shi Prefecture. Later, because General Yong'an Ashina Sijian's tax demands were boundless, they fled to Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongtai era they gradually resettled in Shi Prefecture. Later, driven to flight by the exorbitant tax demands of General Yong'an Ashina Sijian, they fled west to Hexi.

sentences.zh: 元和時復置宥州，護党項。

translations.literal: During the Yuanhe era, You Prefecture was re-established to protect the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe reign, You Prefecture was re-established to oversee the Tangut.

sentences.zh: 至大和中寢強，數寇掠。

translations.literal: By the Dahe era they had gradually grown strong and repeatedly raided and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: By the Dahe reign they had grown steadily stronger and launched repeated raids.

sentences.zh: 然器械鈍苦，畏唐兵精，則以善馬購鎧，善羊貿弓矢。

translations.literal: Yet their weapons were crude and poor; fearing the excellence of Tang troops, they traded fine horses for armor and fine sheep for bows and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Their own weapons were crude, and fearing Tang military prowess, they traded their best horses for armor and their finest sheep for bows and arrows.

sentences.zh: 鄜坊道軍糧使李石表禁商人不得以旗幟、甲胄、五兵入部落，告者，舉罪人財畀之。

translations.literal: Li Shi, grain commissioner of the Fufang Circuit, submitted a memorial forbidding merchants from bringing banners, armor, or the five weapons into the tribes. Informants would receive the entire property of the guilty party as reward.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi, grain commissioner of the Fufang Circuit, petitioned to ban merchants from supplying banners, armor, or weapons to the tribes, offering informants the full property of offenders as reward.

sentences.zh: 至開成末，種落愈繁，富賈人賫繒寶鬻羊馬，藩鎮乘其利，強市之，或不得直，部人怨，相率為亂，至靈、鹽道不通。

translations.literal: By the end of the Kaicheng era, the tribes had grown ever more numerous. Wealthy merchants brought silk and treasures to trade for sheep and horses; the military governors seized the profit, forcing purchases and sometimes paying no fair price. The tribesmen grew resentful and rose in rebellion together, until the roads through Ling and Yan were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Kaicheng reign the tribes had multiplied. Wealthy merchants brought silk and treasures to trade for livestock, but military governors exploited the commerce, forcing sales at unfair prices. Resentment spread, the tribes rose in rebellion, and traffic through Ling and Yan prefectures was severed.

sentences.zh: 武宗以侍御史為使招定，分三印，以邠、寧、延屬崔彥曾，鹽、夏、長澤屬李雩鄠，靈武、麟、勝屬鄭賀，皆緋衣銀魚，而功不克。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong appointed censorial commissioners as envoys to win them over and pacify them, dividing three seals of authority: Bin, Ning, and Yan under Cui Yanzeng; Yan, Xia, Chang, and Ze under Li Yu'e; Lingwu, Lin, and Sheng under Zheng He—all wearing crimson robes and silver fish insignia—but success was not achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong dispatched censorial commissioners to pacify them, dividing authority among three envoys: Cui Yanzeng over Bin, Ning, and Yan; Li Yu'e over Yan, Xia, Chang, and Ze; and Zheng He over Lingwu, Lin, and Sheng—all vested with crimson robes and silver fish insignia—but the effort failed.

sentences.zh: 宣宗大中四年，內掠邠、寧，詔鳳翔李業、河東李拭合節度兵討之，宰相白敏中為都統。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dazhong of Emperor Xuanzong, they raided inward into Bin and Ning. An edict ordered Li Ye of Fengxiang and Li Shi of Hedong to combine their frontier troops to campaign against them, with Chief Minister Bai Minzhong as overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dazhong, the Tangut raided Bin and Ning prefectures. The court ordered Li Ye of Fengxiang and Li Shi of Hedong to combine frontier forces against them, with Chief Minister Bai Minzhong as supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 帝出近苑，或以竹一個植舍外，見才尺許，遠且百步，帝屬二矢曰：「黨羌窮寇，仍歲暴吾鄙，今我約：射竹中則彼當自亡，不中，我且索天下兵翦之，終不以此賊遺子孫。」

translations.literal: The emperor went out to the nearby imperial park. Someone planted a single bamboo stalk outside the lodge; it was only about a chi tall and stood a hundred paces away. The emperor handed two arrows to an attendant and said: "The Tangut bandits are cornered foes who year after year ravage our borders. Here is my wager: if I hit the bamboo, they shall perish of themselves; if I miss, I shall mobilize the empire's armies to exterminate them—I will not bequeath these bandits to my descendants.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited the nearby imperial park, where a single bamboo stalk about a chi tall had been planted a hundred paces from the lodge. Handing two arrows to an attendant, he declared: "These Tangut bandits are desperate raiders who year after year ravage our borders. Here is my wager: if I hit that bamboo, they will destroy themselves; if I miss, I will mobilize the empire's armies to wipe them out—I will not leave this scourge to my descendants.

sentences.zh: 左右註目，帝一發竹分，矢徹諸外，左右呼萬歲。

translations.literal: Those around him watched intently. With a single shot the emperor split the bamboo, the arrow passing clean through. Those around him shouted "Ten thousand years!".
translations.idiomatic: All eyes were fixed upon him. With a single shot he split the bamboo, the arrow passing clean through. The courtiers erupted in cries of "Long live the emperor!".

sentences.zh: 不閱月，羌果破殄，餘種竄南山。

translations.literal: Within less than a month, the Qiang were indeed destroyed; the surviving remnants fled into the southern mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Within the month the Tangut were indeed crushed, and the survivors fled into the southern mountains.

sentences.zh: 始，天寶末，平夏部有戰功，擢容州刺史、天柱軍使。

translations.literal: At the beginning, at the end of the Tianbao era, the Pingxia Division had rendered military service and was promoted: one was made prefect of Rong Prefecture and commissioner of the Tianzhu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at the end of the Tianbao era, a warrior of the Pingxia Division distinguished himself in battle and was promoted to prefect of Rong Prefecture and commissioner of the Tianzhu Army.

sentences.zh: 其裔孫拓拔思恭，咸通末竊據宥州，稱刺史。

translations.literal: His descendant Tuoba Sigong, at the end of the Xiantong era, seized You Prefecture by stealth and styled himself prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His descendant Tuoba Sigong, in the closing years of Xiantong, seized control of You Prefecture and styled himself prefect.

sentences.zh: 黃巢入長安，與鄜州李孝昌壇而坎牲，誓討賊，僖宗賢之，以為左武衛將軍，權知夏綏銀節度事。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao entered Chang'an, he and Li Xiaochang of Fu Prefecture built an altar and buried a sacrificial victim, swearing to campaign against the bandits. Emperor Xizong admired him and appointed him Left Martial Guard General with provisional authority over the Xia-Sui-Yin frontier command.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao seized Chang'an, Sigong and Li Xiaochang of Fu Prefecture erected an altar, buried a sacrificial victim, and swore to destroy the rebels. Emperor Xizong was impressed and appointed him Left Martial Guard General with provisional authority over the Xia-Sui-Yin frontier command.

sentences.zh: 次王橋，為巢所敗，更與鄭畋四節度盟，屯渭橋，

translations.literal: At Wang Bridge he was defeated by Huang Chao's forces; he then allied with Zheng Tian and four frontier commanders and encamped at Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated by Huang Chao at Wang Bridge, he then joined Zheng Tian and four military governors in alliance and encamped at Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 詔為京城西面都統、檢校司空、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him supreme commander of the western capital, Acting Minister of Works, and co-equal with the chancellors of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed supreme commander of the western capital, Acting Minister of Works, and Chancellor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 俄進四面都統，權知京兆尹。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to supreme commander on all four sides and given provisional authority as prefect of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to supreme commander on all four sides and granted provisional authority as prefect of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 賊平，兼太子太傅，封夏國公，賜姓李。

translations.literal: When the bandits were suppressed, he was additionally made Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed as Duke of Xia, and granted the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were crushed, he was also made Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed as Duke of Xia, and granted the imperial surname Li.

sentences.zh: 嗣襄王煴之亂，詔思恭討賊，兵不出，卒。

translations.literal: During the uprising of the Heir Apparent Xiang Wang Yun, an edict ordered Sigong to campaign against the rebels, but his troops did not march forth; he then died.
translations.idiomatic: When the Heir Apparent Xiang Wang Yun rebelled, the court ordered Sigong to suppress the uprising, but he never marched. He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 以弟思諫代為定難節度使，思孝為保大節度、鄜坊凡翟等州觀察使，並檢校司徒、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: His younger brother Sijian was appointed in his stead as military governor of Dingnan; Sixiao was made military governor of Baoda and observation commissioner of Fu-Fang and other prefectures including Fan and Zhai; both were Acting Ministers of Education and co-equal with the chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Sijian succeeded him as military governor of Dingnan; Sixiao was appointed military governor of Baoda and observation commissioner of Fu, Fang, Fan, Zhai, and neighboring prefectures. Both were made Acting Ministers of Education and chancellors.

sentences.zh: 王行瑜反，以思孝為北面招討使，思諫東北面招討使。

translations.literal: When Wang Xingyu rebelled, Sixiao was made northern campaign commander and Sijian northeastern campaign commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xingyu rebelled, Sixiao was appointed northern campaign commander and Sijian northeastern campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 思孝亦因亂取鄜州，遂為節度使，累兼侍中。

translations.literal: Sixiao also seized Fu Prefecture amid the turmoil and thus became military governor, eventually serving concurrently as Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Sixiao also seized Fu Prefecture during the upheaval and became its military governor, eventually rising to Vice Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 以老薦弟思敬為保大軍兵馬留後，俄為節度使。

translations.literal: Because of old age he recommended his younger brother Sijing as acting commander of the Baoda Army; Sijing soon became military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing in years, he recommended his younger brother Sijing as acting commander of the Baoda Army; Sijing soon became military governor.

sentences.zh: 東女東女，亦曰蘇伐剌挐瞿咀羅，羌別種也，西海亦有女自王，故稱「東」別之。

translations.literal: Eastern Women Kingdom. The Eastern Women Kingdom, also called Sufalianijuluo, was a branch of the Qiang. There were also women who ruled themselves in the Western Sea region, hence the designation "Eastern" to distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Women Kingdom. Also known as Sufalianijuluo, this was a Qiang offshoot. Since women also ruled in kingdoms west of the sea, the designation "Eastern" served to distinguish this one.

sentences.zh: 東與吐蕃、党項、茂州接，西屬三波訶，北距於闐，東南屬雅州羅女蠻、白狼夷。

translations.literal: To the east it bordered Tibet, the Tangut, and Maozhou; to the west it was subject to Sanbohe; to the north it faced Khotan; to the southeast it was subject to the Luonü barbarians and Bailang Yi of Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: It bordered Tibet, the Tangut, and Maozhou on the east; owed allegiance to Sanbohe on the west; faced Khotan on the north; and was linked to the Luonü barbarians and Bailang Yi of Yazhou on the southeast.

sentences.zh: 東西行盡九日，南北行盡二十日。

translations.literal: Traveling east to west took nine days; traveling north to south took twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: It measured nine days' travel from east to west and twenty days from north to south.

sentences.zh: 有八十城。

translations.literal: It had eighty walled cities.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom contained eighty walled cities.

sentences.zh: 以女為君，居康延川，巖險四繚，有弱水南流，縫革為船。

translations.literal: A woman served as ruler; the capital lay in Kangyanchuan, surrounded by steep cliffs on all sides. Weak Water flowed southward, and they sewed leather to make boats.
translations.idiomatic: A woman held the throne, with the capital at Kangyanchuan, ringed by precipitous cliffs. Weak Water flowed southward, and boats were fashioned from sewn leather.

sentences.zh: 戶四萬，勝兵萬人。

translations.literal: Households numbered forty thousand; effective fighting forces ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: It had forty thousand households and could field ten thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 王號賓就，官曰高霸黎，猶言宰相也。

translations.literal: The queen was titled Binjiu; officials were called Gaobali, equivalent to prime ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The queen bore the title Binjiu; officials were titled Gaobali, meaning prime minister.

sentences.zh: 官在外者，率男子為之。

translations.literal: For offices outside the court, men were generally appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Men generally held offices based outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 凡號令，女官自內傳，男官受而行。

translations.literal: For all orders, female officials transmitted them from within, and male officials received and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: All royal commands were issued by female officials from within the palace and executed by male officials outside.

sentences.zh: 王侍女數百，五日一聽政。

translations.literal: The queen had several hundred attendant maidens and held audience every five days.
translations.idiomatic: The queen was attended by several hundred maidens and held court every five days.

sentences.zh: 王死，國人以金錢數萬納王族，求淑女二立之。

translations.literal: When the queen died, the people of the state paid tens of thousands in gold and silver to the royal clan and sought two virtuous women to establish as rulers.
translations.idiomatic: Upon the queen's death, the people offered tens of thousands in gold and silver to the royal clan and selected two virtuous women to succeed her.

sentences.zh: 次為小王，王死，因以為嗣，或姑死婦繼，無篡奪。

translations.literal: The younger served as lesser queen; when the queen died, she succeeded accordingly. Sometimes an aunt died and a niece succeeded; there was no usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: The younger woman served as vice-queen and succeeded upon the queen's death. Sometimes a niece succeeded an aunt; the throne was never seized by force.

sentences.zh: 所居皆重屋，王九層，國人六層。

translations.literal: Their dwellings were all multi-storied buildings; the queen's had nine tiers, those of common people six.
translations.idiomatic: All dwellings were multi-storied: the queen's palace rose nine stories, common dwellings six.

sentences.zh: 王服青毛綾裙，被青袍，袖委於地，冬羔裘，飾以文錦。

translations.literal: The queen wore a green woolen skirt, a green robe with sleeves trailing to the ground, and in winter a lamb-fur coat adorned with brocade.
translations.idiomatic: The queen wore a green woolen skirt and green robe with sleeves trailing to the ground; in winter she donned a lamb-fur coat trimmed with brocade.

sentences.zh: 為小鬟髻，耳垂珰。

translations.literal: She wore her hair in small loops; pearl pendants hung from her ears.
translations.idiomatic: She wore her hair in small topknots with pearl earrings.

sentences.zh: 足曳索。

translations.literal: On her feet she dragged suo.
translations.idiomatic: On her feet she wore suo.

sentences.zh: 索，履也。

translations.literal: Suo means footwear.
translations.idiomatic: Suo means shoes.

sentences.zh: 俗輕男子，女貴者咸有侍男，被發，以青塗面，惟務戰與耕而已。

translations.literal: By custom men were held in low regard; noblewomen all had attendant men with loose hair and faces painted blue, who devoted themselves only to fighting and farming.
translations.idiomatic: Men were held in low esteem by custom. Noble women kept attendant men with loose hair and blue-painted faces who devoted themselves solely to warfare and farming.

sentences.zh: 子從母姓。

translations.literal: Children took their mother's surname.
translations.idiomatic: Children inherited their mother's surname.

sentences.zh: 地寒宜麥，畜羊馬，出黃金。

translations.literal: The land was cold and suited to wheat; they raised sheep and horses and produced gold.
translations.idiomatic: The cold climate favored wheat; they raised sheep and horses and mined gold.

sentences.zh: 風俗大抵與天竺同。

translations.literal: Customs were largely the same as in Tianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs were largely those of India.

sentences.zh: 以十一月為正。

translations.literal: They took the eleventh month as the start of the year.
translations.idiomatic: The eleventh month marked the beginning of their year.

sentences.zh: 巫者以十月詣山中，布糟麥，咒呼群鳥。

translations.literal: In the tenth month shamans went into the mountains, spread fermented grain and wheat, and invoked the flocks of birds with incantations.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month shamans entered the mountains, scattered fermented grain and wheat, and summoned flocks of birds with incantations.

sentences.zh: 俄有鳥來如雞狀，剖視之，有谷者歲豐，否即有災，名曰鳥卜。

translations.literal: Soon a bird would come shaped like a chicken; they dissected it, and if grain was found within, the year would be abundant; otherwise disaster would follow. This was called bird divination.
translations.idiomatic: A bird resembling a chicken would appear; they opened it and read the omen—grain within meant a bountiful harvest, its absence foretold disaster. This practice was called bird divination.

sentences.zh: 居喪三年，不易服，不櫛沐。

translations.literal: Mourning lasted three years; they did not change garments and did not comb their hair or bathe.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning lasted three years without changing garments, combing hair, or bathing.

sentences.zh: 貴人死，剝藏其皮，內骨甕中，糅金屑瘞之。

translations.literal: When a noble died, they flayed and preserved the skin, placed the bones in an urn, and buried it mixed with gold dust.
translations.idiomatic: When a noble died, the skin was preserved, the bones placed in an urn, and the urn buried mixed with gold dust.

sentences.zh: 王之葬，殉死至數十人。

translations.literal: At the queen's burial, dozens were buried alive to accompany her in death.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens were entombed alive to accompany the queen at her burial.

sentences.zh: 武德時，王湯滂氏始遣使入貢。

translations.literal: During the Wude era, Queen Tangpangshi first sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude reign, Queen Tangpangshi first sent envoys to pay tribute.

sentences.zh: 高祖厚報，為突厥所掠不得通。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu responded generously, but they were plundered by the Turks and could not get through.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu responded with lavish gifts, but the envoys were intercepted by the Turks and never reached the court.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，使復至，太宗璽制慰撫。

translations.literal: During the Zhenguan era, envoys came again, and Emperor Taizong issued an imperial edict of consolation and reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign, envoys returned, and Emperor Taizong issued an imperial edict of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 顯慶初，遣使高霸黎文與王子三廬來朝，授右監門中郎將。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xianqing era, envoys Gaobali Wen and Prince Sanlu came to court and were appointed Right Gate Guard Lieutenant General.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xianqing reign, the envoy Gaobali Wen and Prince Sanlu came to court; both were appointed Right Gate Guard Lieutenant Generals.

sentences.zh: 其王斂臂使大臣來請官號，武後冊拜斂臂左玉鈐衛員外將軍，賜瑞錦服。

translations.literal: Their queen Lianbi sent a minister to request an official title; Empress Wu enfeoffed Lianbi as External General of the Left Jade Bell Guard and bestowed brocade robes of honor.
translations.idiomatic: Queen Lianbi dispatched a minister to request an official title. Empress Wu appointed Lianbi External General of the Left Jade Bell Guard and granted her brocade robes of honor.

sentences.zh: 天授、開元間，王及子再來朝，詔與宰相宴曲江，封王曳夫為歸昌王、左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Between the Tianshou and Kaiyuan eras, the queen and her son came to court again; an edict summoned them to banquet with the chancellor at Qujiang; the queen Yefu was enfeoffed as King of Guichang and made Left Golden Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Tianshou and Kaiyuan reigns, the queen and her son visited court again and were entertained at Qujiang with the chancellor. Queen Yefu was enfeoffed as King of Guichang and appointed Left Golden Guard General.

sentences.zh: 後乃以男子為王，

translations.literal: Later a man was made king.
translations.idiomatic: Later the throne passed to a man.

sentences.zh: 其王湯立悉與白狗君及哥鄰君董臥庭、逋租君鄧吉知、南水君薛尚悉曩、弱水君董避和、悉董君湯息贊、清遠君蘇唐磨、咄霸君董藐蓬皆詣劍南韋臯求內附。

translations.literal: Their king Tanglixi, together with the lord of Baigou and the lords Tangwoting of Geling, Dengjizhi of Chongzu, Xue Shangxinang of Nanshui, Dongbihe of Ruoshui, Tangxizan of Xidong, Sutangmo of Qingyuan, and Dongmiaopeng of Duoba, all came to Wei Gao in Jiannan seeking to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: King Tanglixi, together with the lord of Baigou and the chieftains Tangwoting of Geling, Dengjizhi of Chongzu, Xue Shangxinang of Nanshui, Dongbihe of Ruoshui, Tangxizan of Xidong, Sutangmo of Qingyuan, and Dongmiaopeng of Duoba, all sought out Wei Gao in Jiannan to submit to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 其種散居西山、弱水，雖自謂王，蓋小小部落耳。

translations.literal: Their tribes were scattered in the western mountains and along Weak Water; though they styled themselves kings, they were but tiny tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Scattered across the western mountains and Weak Water, they styled themselves kings but were in truth little more than small tribes.

sentences.zh: 自失河、隴，悉為吐蕃羈屬，部數千戶，輒置令，歲督絲絮。

translations.literal: Since the loss of the He and Long regions, all became bound subjects of Tibet; tribes of several thousand households each had officials appointed who collected silk floss annually.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tang lost the He and Long regions, all fell under Tibetan control. Tribes of several thousand households each had officials imposed upon them to collect silk floss as tribute every year.

sentences.zh: 至是猶上天寶所賜詔書。

translations.literal: Even now they still presented the edicts bestowed during the Tianbao era.
translations.idiomatic: Even then they still presented the edicts the court had granted them during the Tianbao reign.

sentences.zh: 臯處其眾於維、霸等州，賜牛、糧，治生業。

translations.literal: Gao settled their people in Wei, Ba, and other prefectures, granting cattle and grain to establish livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Gao resettled them in Wei, Ba, and neighboring prefectures, providing cattle and grain to establish new livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 立悉等入朝，差賜官祿。

translations.literal: Tanglixi and others came to court and were variously granted official salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Tanglixi and the others came to court and received graded appointments and stipends.

sentences.zh: 於是松州羌二萬口相踵入附。

translations.literal: Thereupon twenty thousand Tangut of Song Prefecture submitted in continuous succession.
translations.idiomatic: Then twenty thousand Tangut of Song Prefecture submitted in a steady stream.

sentences.zh: 立悉等官刺史，皆得世襲，然陰附吐蕃，故謂「兩面羌」。

translations.literal: Tanglixi and others were appointed prefects, all inheritable offices; yet they secretly allied with Tibet, hence they were called "double-faced Qiang."
translations.idiomatic: Tanglixi and the others were appointed hereditary prefects, yet they secretly sided with Tibet and were therefore called the "double-faced Qiang."

sentences.zh: 高昌高昌，直京師西四千里而贏，其橫八百里，縱五百里，凡二十一城。

translations.literal: Gaochang. Gaochang lay four thousand li west of the capital with surplus; it measured eight hundred li across and five hundred li north to south, with twenty-one cities in all.
translations.idiomatic: Gaochang. Gaochang lay some four thousand li west of the capital, measuring eight hundred li east to west and five hundred li north to south, with twenty-one cities in all.

sentences.zh: 王都交河城，漢車師前王廷也。

translations.literal: The royal capital was Jiaohe City, the former court of the Former Kingdom of Cheshi in Han times.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was Jiaohe City, seat of the Former Kingdom of Cheshi in Han times.

sentences.zh: 田地城，戊己校尉所治也。

translations.literal: Tiandi City was where the Wuji Colonel was stationed.
translations.idiomatic: Tiandi City was the seat of the Wuji Colonel.

sentences.zh: 勝兵萬人。

translations.literal: Effective fighting forces numbered ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: It could field ten thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 土沃，麥、禾皆再熟。

translations.literal: The soil was fertile; wheat and grain both ripened twice.
translations.idiomatic: The land was fertile, with wheat and grain yielding two harvests a year.

sentences.zh: 有草名白疊，擷花可織為布。

translations.literal: There was a plant called baidie; its flowers could be picked and woven into cloth.
translations.idiomatic: A plant called baidie grew there; its flowers could be harvested and woven into cloth.

sentences.zh: 俗辮髻垂後。

translations.literal: By custom they wore braided topknots hanging behind.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they wore braided topknots hanging down the back.

sentences.zh: 其王曲伯雅，隋時嘗妻以戚屬宇文氏女，號華容公主。

translations.literal: Their king Qu Boya had in Sui times been given a daughter of the imperial Yuwen clan in marriage, titled Princess Huarong.
translations.idiomatic: Their king Qu Boya had married a daughter of the imperial Yuwen clan during the Sui dynasty, who was titled Princess Huarong.

sentences.zh: 武德初，伯雅死，子文泰立，遣使來告，高祖命使者臨吊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, Boya died and his son Wentai succeeded; envoys came to announce it, and Emperor Gaozu ordered envoys to attend the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wude, Boya died and his son Wentai succeeded. Envoys came to announce the death, and Emperor Gaozu dispatched representatives to pay condolences.

sentences.zh: 後五年，獻狗高六寸，長尺，能曳馬銜燭，雲出拂菻，中國始有拂菻狗。

translations.literal: Five years later they presented a dog six cun tall and one chi long, able to drag a horse bridle and carry a candle, said to come from Fulin; China first had Fulin dogs then.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later they presented a dog six cun tall and one chi long, capable of pulling a bridle and carrying a candle—said to come from Fulin—the first such dog known in China.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，獻玄狐裘，帝賜妻宇文華钅奠一具，宇文亦上玉盤。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong ascended the throne, they presented a dark fox fur coat; the emperor bestowed upon his wife Yuwen a set of floral gold inlay ornaments, and Yuwen also presented a jade dish.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong ascended the throne, they presented a dark fox fur coat. The emperor granted Princess Yuwen a set of floral gold inlay ornaments, and she in turn presented a jade dish.

sentences.zh: 凡諸國施為輒以聞。

translations.literal: For all measures taken among the various states, they invariably reported to the court.
translations.idiomatic: They reported all major undertakings to the Tang court.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年，文泰遂來朝，禮賜厚甚。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan, Wentai came to court; the rites and rewards were exceedingly generous.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenguan, Wentai came to court and was received with exceptional honors and gifts.

sentences.zh: 宇文求預宗籍，有詔賜氏李，更封常樂公主。

translations.literal: Yuwen requested enrollment in the imperial clan register; an edict granted her the surname Li and re-enfeoffed her as Princess Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen petitioned for enrollment in the imperial clan register; the court granted her the surname Li and re-enfeoffed her as Princess Changle.

sentences.zh: 久之，文泰與西突厥通，凡西域朝貢道其國，鹹見壅掠。

translations.literal: After a long time, Wentai communicated with the Western Turks; all Western Regions tribute missions passing through his state were blocked and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Wentai allied with the Western Turks and plundered every Western Regions tribute mission passing through his territory.

sentences.zh: 伊吾嘗臣西突厥，至是內屬，文泰與葉護共擊之。

translations.literal: Yiwu had once served the Western Turks; at this time it submitted inward, and Wentai and Yehu jointly attacked it.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwu, formerly a Western Turk vassal, had now submitted to the Tang. Wentai and Yehu joined forces to attack it.

sentences.zh: 帝下詔讓其反覆，召大臣冠軍阿史那矩計事，文泰不遣，使長史曲雍來謝罪。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict reproaching his flip-flopping, summoned his minister Champion Ashina Ju to discuss matters, but Wentai did not send him; instead he sent Chief Administrator Qu Yong to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict rebuking Wentai's duplicity and summoned his minister Champion Ashina Ju for consultation, but Wentai refused to send him, dispatching Chief Administrator Qu Yong to apologize instead.

sentences.zh: 初，大業末，華民多奔突厥，及頡利敗，有逃入高昌者，有詔護送，文泰苛留之。

translations.literal: At first, at the end of Daye, Chinese commoners fled in great numbers to the Turks; when Jieli was defeated, some escaped into Gaochang; an edict ordered their escort home, but Wentai harshly detained them.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye reign, many Chinese had fled to the Turks. After Jieli's defeat, some escaped into Gaochang. The court ordered their repatriation, but Wentai forcibly detained them.

sentences.zh: 又與西突厥乙毗設破焉耆三城，虜其人，焉耆王訴諸朝。

translations.literal: He also joined with the Western Turk Yipishi to destroy three cities of Yanqi and capture their people; the King of Yanqi complained to the court.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined the Western Turk Yipishi in sacking three Yanqi cities and capturing their people, prompting the King of Yanqi to petition the Tang court.

sentences.zh: 帝遣虞部郎中李道裕問狀，復遣使謝。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched Li Daoyu of the Palace Revisions Bureau to investigate, and Wentai again sent envoys to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Li Daoyu of the Palace Revisions Bureau to investigate; Wentai again sent envoys to apologize.

sentences.zh: 帝引責曰：「而主數年朝貢不入，無藩臣禮，擅置官，擬效百僚。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned and reproached him, saying: "Your lord for several years has sent no tribute and shown no ritual of a vassal state, has arbitrarily established offices and mimicked the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him and rebuked him: "Your lord has sent no tribute for years, shown no deference befitting a vassal, and arbitrarily established offices imitating the imperial bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 今歲首萬君長悉來，而主不至。

translations.literal: At this New Year every tribal chieftain has come, yet your lord has not come.
translations.idiomatic: At this New Year every tribal chieftain has come to court, yet your lord has not appeared.

sentences.zh: 日我使人往，文泰猥曰：『鷹飛於天，雉竄於蒿，貓遊於堂，鼠安於穴，各得其所，豈不快邪！』

translations.literal: When I previously sent envoys, Wentai rudely said: 'The hawk flies in the sky, the pheasant hides in the weeds, the cat roams the hall, the rat rests in its hole—each in its place. Is that not satisfactory!
translations.idiomatic: When I sent envoys before, Wentai insolently replied: 'The hawk soars in the sky, the pheasant hides in the weeds, the cat roams the hall, the rat rests in its hole—each in its own place. What fault is there in that?

sentences.zh: 西域使者入貢，而主悉拘梗之。

translations.literal: Western Regions envoys coming to offer tribute—your lord has detained and obstructed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from the Western Regions bringing tribute—your lord has detained and obstructed them all.

sentences.zh: 又諗薛延陀曰：『既自為可汗，與唐天子等，何事拜謁其使？』

translations.literal: He also incited the Xueyantuo, saying: 'Since you have made yourself khan, you are equal to the Son of Heaven of Tang—why bother to pay respects to his envoys?
translations.idiomatic: He also goaded the Xueyantuo, saying: 'You have made yourself khan and are equal to the Tang emperor—why demean yourself by paying respects to his envoys?

sentences.zh: 明年我當發兵虜而國，歸謂而君善自圖。」

translations.literal: Next year I shall dispatch troops to capture your state. Return and tell your lord to plan accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Next year I shall send troops to destroy your kingdom. Return and tell your lord to prepare accordingly.

sentences.zh: 時薛延陀可汗請為軍向導，故民部尚書唐儉至延陀堅約。

translations.literal: At that time the Xueyantuo khan offered to serve as military guide, so Minister of Revenue Tang Jian went to Xueyantuo to cement the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: The Xueyantuo khan had offered to guide the Tang army, so Minister of Revenue Tang Jian went to Xueyantuo to finalize the alliance.

sentences.zh: 帝復下璽書示文泰禍福，促使入朝，文泰遂稱疾不至。

translations.literal: The emperor again issued an imperial edict showing Wentai the consequences of fortune and misfortune, urging him to come to court; Wentai then claimed illness and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent an imperial edict setting out the consequences of obedience and defiance, urging Wentai to come to court. Wentai pleaded illness and refused.

sentences.zh: 乃拜侯君集為交河道大總管，左屯衛大將軍薛萬均、薩孤吳仁副之，契何力為蔥山道副大總管，武衛將軍牛進達為行軍總管，率突厥、契騎數萬討之。

translations.literal: Hou Junji was appointed Grand Commander of the Jiaohe Circuit; Left Encampment Guard General Xue Wanjun and Sagou Wuren served as his deputies; Qibi Heli as deputy grand commander of the Congshan Circuit; Martial Guard General Niu Jinda as campaign commander; they led tens of thousands of Turk and Qi cavalry to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Junji was appointed Grand Commander of the Jiaohe Circuit, with Left Encampment Guard General Xue Wanjun and Sagou Wuren as deputies, Qibi Heli as deputy commander of the Congshan Route, and Martial Guard General Niu Jinda as campaign commander. They led tens of thousands of Turk and Qi cavalry against Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 群臣諫以行萬里兵難得誌，且天界絕域，雖得之，不可守。

translations.literal: The ministers remonstrated that marching ten thousand li, troops would be hard to sustain, and besides it was a heaven-bounded remote region that even if taken could not be held.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers warned that an army marching ten thousand li could not be sustained, and that even if conquered, this remote frontier land could not be held.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor overruled them.

sentences.zh: 文泰謂左右曰：「曩吾入朝，見秦、隴北城邑蕭條，非有隋比。

translations.literal: Wentai said to those around him: "When I previously came to court, I saw the cities and towns north of Qin and Long desolate and empty—they were nothing compared to Sui times.
translations.idiomatic: Wentai told his advisors: "When I last visited court, the cities north of Qin and Long were desolate—nothing like the Sui era.

sentences.zh: 今伐我，兵多則糧付不逮；

translations.literal: Now if they campaign against me, if their troops are many, their grain supplies will not reach them.
translations.idiomatic: If they invade now, too large an army will outrun its supplies.

sentences.zh: 若下三萬，我能制之。

translations.literal: If fewer than thirty thousand, I can subdue them.
translations.idiomatic: If they send fewer than thirty thousand, I can defeat them.

sentences.zh: 度磧疲鈍，以逸待勞，臥收其弊耳。」

translations.literal: Crossing the desert they will be worn and dull; I shall wait rested for their exhaustion and easily reap their defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the desert will wear them down. I need only wait rested for their exhaustion and reap the victory.

sentences.zh: 十四年，聞王師至磧口，悸駭無它計，發病死，子智盛立。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, hearing the imperial army had reached the desert crossing, he was seized with terror and had no other plan; he fell ill and died of fright; his son Zhicheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, hearing the imperial army had reached the desert crossing, he was gripped by terror and had no recourse. He died of fright; his son Zhicheng succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 君集奄攻田地城，契何力以前軍鏖戰。

translations.literal: Junji suddenly attacked Tiandi City; Qibi Heli fought fiercely with the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Junji launched a surprise assault on Tiandi City, with Qibi Heli fighting fiercely at the head of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 是夜星墜城中，明日拔其城，虜七千餘人。

translations.literal: That night a star fell within the city; the next day they took the city and captured more than seven thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: That night a star fell inside the city. The next day the Tang forces took it, capturing more than seven thousand men.

sentences.zh: 中郎將辛獠兒以勁騎夜逼其都。

translations.literal: Lieutenant General Xin Liaor led crack cavalry in a night approach on the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Lieutenant General Xin Liaor led elite cavalry in a night approach on the capital.

sentences.zh: 智盛以書遺君集曰：「得罪於天子者，先王也，咎深譴積，震墜厥命。

translations.literal: Zhicheng sent a letter to Junji saying: "The one who offended the Son of Heaven was my late father; his crimes were deep and his punishment long accumulated, and he fell from his mandated fate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicheng wrote to Junji: "It was my late father who offended the Son of Heaven. His crimes were grave and his punishment long overdue, and Heaven struck him down.

sentences.zh: 智盛嗣位未幾，公其見赦。」

translations.literal: Zhicheng has succeeded to the throne only recently—please show forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: I have reigned only briefly—I beg your mercy.

sentences.zh: 君集曰：「能悔禍者，當面縛軍門。」

translations.literal: Junji said: "If you can repent your misfortune, come bound to the camp gate."
translations.idiomatic: Junji replied: "If you wish to repent, come bound to the camp gate."

sentences.zh: 智盛不答。

translations.literal: Zhicheng did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicheng made no reply.

sentences.zh: 軍進，填隍引沖車，飛石如雨，城中大震。

translations.literal: The army advanced, filled the moat and deployed battering rams; flying stones fell like rain; the city was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced, filled the moat, and deployed siege engines. Stones rained down and the city shook in terror.

sentences.zh: 智盛令大將曲士義居守，身與綰曹曲德俊謁軍門，請改事天子。

translations.literal: Zhicheng ordered General Qu Shiyi to hold the defense; he himself, with Secretariat Officer Qu Dejun, visited the camp gate and requested to transfer allegiance to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicheng left General Qu Shiyi to defend the city and went with Secretariat Officer Qu Dejun to the camp gate to surrender to the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 君集諭使降，辭示屈，薛萬均勃然起曰：「當先取城，小兒何與語！」

translations.literal: Junji urged him to surrender; his words showed submission. Xue Wanjun rose angrily and said: "We should first take the city—why talk with this boy!
translations.idiomatic: Junji urged him to surrender, and Zhicheng's words showed submission. Xue Wanjun rose angrily: "Take the city first—why parley with this boy!

sentences.zh: 麾而進，智盛流汗伏地曰：「唯公命！」

translations.literal: He signaled the advance; Zhicheng, sweating, prostrated himself and said: "I obey your command alone!"
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the advance. Zhicheng, sweating, prostrated himself and cried: "I obey your command alone!"

sentences.zh: 乃降。

translations.literal: He thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 君集分兵略定，凡三州、五縣、二十二城，戶八千，口三萬，馬四千。

translations.literal: Junji divided his forces to pacify the region, taking in all three prefectures, five counties, and twenty-two cities, with eight thousand households, thirty thousand persons, and four thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Junji divided his forces to pacify the region, securing three prefectures, five counties, and twenty-two cities—eight thousand households, thirty thousand people, and four thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 先是，其國人謠曰：「高昌兵，如霜雪；

translations.literal: Earlier, the people of the state had a song that said: "Gaochang's soldiers are like frost and snow;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the people had sung: "Gaochang's soldiers are like frost and snow;

sentences.zh: 唐家兵，如日月。

translations.literal: Tang soldiers are like sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: Tang soldiers are like sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 日月照霜雪，幾何自殄滅。」

translations.literal: When sun and moon shine upon frost and snow, how long before it melts away?"
translations.idiomatic: When sun and moon shine upon frost and snow, how long before it melts away?

sentences.zh: 文泰捕謠所發，不能得也。

translations.literal: Wentai arrested those who spread the song but could not find them.
translations.idiomatic: Wentai arrested those who spread the song but could not find the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 捷書聞，天子大悅，宴群臣，班賜策功，赦高昌所部，披其地皆州縣之，號西昌州。

translations.literal: When news of victory arrived, the Son of Heaven was greatly pleased, feasted the ministers, distributed rewards according to merit, pardoned the people of Gaochang, organized their lands into prefectures and counties, and named the region Xichang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, the emperor was delighted. He feasted his ministers, distributed rewards by merit, pardoned the people of Gaochang, organized their lands into prefectures and counties, and named the region Xichang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 特進魏徵諫曰：「陛下即位，高昌最先朝謁。

translations.literal: Special Advance Wei Zheng remonstrated, saying: "Since Your Majesty's accession, Gaochang was the first to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Special Advance Wei Zheng remonstrated: "Since Your Majesty's accession, Gaochang was the first to pay court.

sentences.zh: 俄以掠商胡，遏貢獻，故王誅加焉。

translations.literal: Soon, for plundering merchant envoys and obstructing tribute, the king was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, for plundering merchants and obstructing tribute, the king was punished.

sentences.zh: 文泰死，罪止矣。

translations.literal: Wentai is dead—the crime ends there.
translations.idiomatic: Wentai is dead—the crime ends with him.

sentences.zh: 撫其人，立其子，伐罪吊民，道也。

translations.literal: To comfort the people and establish his son, punishing guilt and consoling the people—this is the Way.
translations.idiomatic: To comfort the people and install his son—punishing the guilty and consoling the innocent—is the proper way.

sentences.zh: 今利其土，屯守常千人，屯士數年一易，辦裝資，離親戚，不十年隴右且空。

translations.literal: Now if you seize their land and garrison it with a thousand men permanently, with garrison troops rotated every few years at the cost of equipment and supplies, separated from kin—for less than ten years Longyou will be emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Now, seizing their land requires a permanent garrison of a thousand men, rotated every few years at the cost of equipment and supplies, torn from their families—for less than ten years Longyou will be drained empty.

sentences.zh: 陛下終不得高昌圭粒咫帛助中國費，所謂散有用事無用。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty will ultimately receive not a grain or inch of silk from Gaochang to aid China's expenses—this is what is called scattering the useful for the useless."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty will never receive so much as a grain or inch of silk from Gaochang to offset the empire's costs—this is to squander the useful on the useless.

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: The advice was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept the advice.

sentences.zh: 改西昌州曰西州，更置安西都護府，歲調千兵，謫罪人以戍。

translations.literal: Xichang Prefecture was renamed Xizhou, and the Anxi Protectorate was newly established, with a thousand soldiers levied annually and convicts exiled to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Xichang Prefecture was renamed Xizhou, the Anxi Protectorate was established, a thousand soldiers were levied annually, and convicts were exiled to garrison the frontier.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎褚遂良諫曰：「古者先函夏，後夷狄，務廣德化，不爭荒逖。

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Vice Director Chu Suiliang remonstrated, saying: "In antiquity one first secured the Central Plains, then dealt with the barbarians, striving to extend virtue and transformation rather than contesting remote wastes.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Vice Director Chu Suiliang remonstrated: "In antiquity the sage kings secured the Central Plains first and dealt with barbarians afterward, extending virtue rather than contesting remote wastes.

sentences.zh: 今高昌誅滅，威動四夷，然自王師始征，河西供役，飛米轉芻，十室九匱，五年未可復。

translations.literal: Now that Gaochang is destroyed, your prestige shakes the four quarters—yet from the moment the imperial army marched, the Hexi region supplied labor, flying grain and hauling fodder until nine of ten households were impoverished; five years will not restore them.
translations.idiomatic: Though Gaochang's destruction shakes the four quarters, from the moment the imperial army marched the Hexi region has supplied labor, flying grain and hauling fodder until nine of ten households are ruined—five years will not restore them.

sentences.zh: 今又歲遣屯戍，行李萬里，去者資裝使自營辦，賣菽粟，傾機杼，道路死亡尚不計。

translations.literal: Now you additionally dispatch annual garrison troops ten thousand li away; those who depart must provision themselves, selling beans and grain and exhausting their looms—and deaths along the road are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Now you dispatch annual garrison troops ten thousand li away; those who depart must provision themselves, selling grain and exhausting their looms—and deaths along the road are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 罪人始於犯法，終於惰業，無益於行。

translations.literal: Convicts begin by breaking the law and end in idleness—this benefits nothing in practice.
translations.idiomatic: Convicts begin as lawbreakers and end as idlers—this serves no practical purpose.

sentences.zh: 所遣復有亡命，官司捕逮，株蔓相牽。

translations.literal: Among those dispatched are also fugitives whom officials pursue, with families implicated in chains.
translations.idiomatic: Among those dispatched are fugitives whom officials pursue, dragging entire families into the net.

sentences.zh: 有如張掖、酒泉塵飛烽舉，豈得高昌一乘一卒及事乎？
