translations.literal: If dust rises and beacon fires blaze at Zhangye and Jiuquan, would a single rider or soldier from Gaochang be of any use?
translations.idiomatic: If dust rises and beacon fires blaze at Zhangye and Jiuquan, would a single rider or soldier from Gaochang be of any use?

sentences.zh: 必發隴右、河西耳。

translations.literal: Troops would have to be drawn from Longyou and Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Troops would have to be drawn from Longyou and Hexi.

sentences.zh: 然則河西為我腹心，高昌，他人手足也，何必耗中華，事無用？

translations.literal: Thus Hexi is our heart and belly, while Gaochang is another's hand and foot—why exhaust the Central Plains for something useless?
translations.idiomatic: Hexi is our heart and belly; Gaochang is another's hand and foot. Why exhaust the Central Plains for something useless?

sentences.zh: 昔陛下平頡利、吐谷渾，皆為立君，蓋罪而誅之，伏而立之，百蠻所以畏威慕德也。

translations.literal: Formerly when Your Majesty pacified Jieli and Tuyuhun, you established rulers for each—punishing guilt by execution and establishing submission by enthronement. This is why the hundred barbarians fear your might and admire your virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty pacified Jieli and Tuyuhun, you established rulers for each—executing the guilty and enthroning the submissive. This is why the hundred barbarians fear your might and admire your virtue.

sentences.zh: 今宜擇高昌可立者立之，召首領悉還本土，長為藩翰，中國不擾。」

translations.literal: Now you should choose someone suitable from Gaochang to establish as ruler, summon all the chieftains back to their native lands, and let them long serve as frontier bulwarks without disturbing China.
translations.idiomatic: Choose a suitable ruler from Gaochang, summon all chieftains back to their native lands, and let them serve as frontier bulwarks without disturbing the empire.

sentences.zh: 書聞不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was received but not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received but ignored.

sentences.zh: 初，文泰以金厚餉西突厥欲谷設，約有急為表裏；

translations.literal: At first, Wentai had bribed the Western Turk Yugu She heavily with gold, agreeing that in an emergency they would act as mutual support;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wentai had bribed the Western Turk Yugu She heavily with gold, agreeing to mutual support in an emergency;

sentences.zh: 使葉護屯可汗浮圖城。

translations.literal: he had Yehu station troops at Khan Futu City.
translations.idiomatic: he had Yehu station troops at Khan Futu City.

sentences.zh: 及君集至，懼不敢發，遂來降，以其地為庭州。

translations.literal: When Junji arrived, Yehu feared to act and came to surrender; his territory was made into Ting Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Junji arrived, Yehu feared to act and surrendered; his territory was organized as Ting Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 焉耆請歸高昌所奪五城，留兵以守。

translations.literal: Yanqi requested the return of five cities seized by Gaochang and that troops be left to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqi requested the return of five cities seized by Gaochang and that troops be left to garrison them.

sentences.zh: 君集勒石紀功，凱而旋，俘智盛君臣獻觀德殿。

translations.literal: Junji inscribed a stone to record the achievement, returned in triumph, and presented the captive Zhicheng, his ministers, and officials at Guande Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Junji inscribed a stone to record the victory, returned in triumph, and presented the captive Zhicheng and his court at Guande Hall.

sentences.zh: 行飲至禮，酺三日。

translations.literal: A victory banquet was held and revelry lasted three days.
translations.idiomatic: A victory banquet was held and revelry lasted three days.

sentences.zh: 徙高昌豪桀於中國，智盛拜左武衛將軍、金城郡公，弟智湛右武衛中郎將、天山郡公。

translations.literal: The leading families of Gaochang were relocated to China; Zhicheng was appointed Left Martial Guard General and Duke of Jincheng; his younger brother Zhizhan was made Right Martial Guard Lieutenant General and Duke of Tianshan.
translations.idiomatic: Gaochang's leading families were relocated to China. Zhicheng was appointed Left Martial Guard General and Duke of Jincheng; his younger brother Zhizhan was made Right Martial Guard Lieutenant General and Duke of Tianshan.

sentences.zh: 曲氏傳國九世，百三十四年而亡。

translations.literal: The Qu clan had ruled for nine generations over one hundred thirty-four years before perishing.
translations.idiomatic: The Qu clan had ruled for nine generations over one hundred thirty-four years before the kingdom fell.

sentences.zh: 智湛，麟德中以左驍衛大將軍為西州刺史，卒，贈涼州都督。

translations.literal: Zhizhan, in the Longde era, served as Left Piaoqi Guard General and prefect of Xizhou; he died and was posthumously made military governor of Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhan served as Left Piaoqi Guard General and prefect of Xizhou during the Longde era; upon his death he was posthumously made military governor of Liang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 有子昭，好學。

translations.literal: He had a son Zhao who loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Zhao who loved learning.

sentences.zh: 有鬻異書者，母顧笥中金嘆曰：「何愛此，不使子有異聞乎？」

translations.literal: When someone was selling unusual books, his mother, glancing at the gold in the chest, sighed: "Why cherish this and not let my son hear unusual things?
translations.idiomatic: When a peddler offered unusual books, his mother glanced at the gold in her chest and sighed: "Why hoard this and deny my son uncommon learning?

sentences.zh: 盡持易之。

translations.literal: She took it all to exchange for the books.
translations.idiomatic: She spent it all to buy the books.

sentences.zh: 昭歷司膳卿，頗能辭章。

translations.literal: Zhao served as Director of Palace Provisions and was quite skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao served as Director of Palace Provisions and was accomplished in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 弟崇裕有武藝，永徽中為右武衛翊府中郎將，封交河郡王，邑至三千戶。

translations.literal: His younger brother Chongyu had martial talent; in the Yonghui era he was Right Martial Guard Lieutenant General of the Palace Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Jiaohe with a fief of up to three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Chongyu was skilled in arms; during the Yonghui reign he served as Right Martial Guard Lieutenant General of the Palace Guard and was enfeoffed as Prince of Jiaohe with a fief of three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 終鎮軍大將軍，武後為舉哀，襚以美錦，賻賜甚厚，封爵絕。

translations.literal: He ended as General of Garrison Forces; Empress Wu held mourning rites for him, bestowing fine brocade for the shroud and lavish funeral gifts; the enfeoffment then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as General of Garrison Forces. Empress Wu held mourning rites for him, bestowing fine brocade for the shroud and lavish funeral gifts; the line of enfeoffment then ended.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾居甘松山之陽，洮水之西，南抵白蘭，地數千里。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun dwelt on the southern slopes of Mount Gansong, west of the Tao River, reaching south to Bailan, their territory spanning several thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun. The Tuyuhun lived on the southern slopes of Mount Gansong, west of the Tao River, extending south to Bailan across several thousand li.

sentences.zh: 有城郭，不居也。

translations.literal: They had walled cities but did not dwell in them.
translations.idiomatic: They had walled cities but did not live in them.

sentences.zh: 隨水草，帳室、肉糧。

translations.literal: They followed water and pasture, living in tents and eating meat.
translations.idiomatic: They followed water and pasture, living in tents on meat and dairy.

sentences.zh: 其官有長史、司馬、將軍、王、公、僕射、尚書、郎中，蓋慕諸華為之。

translations.literal: Their offices included chief administrator, marshal, generals, kings, dukes, vice directors, ministers, and bureau directors—titles apparently modeled on the Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Their offices included chief administrator, marshal, generals, kings, dukes, vice directors, ministers, and bureau directors—titles apparently modeled on Chinese practice.

sentences.zh: 俗識文字，其王椎髻黑冒，妻錦袍織裙，金花飾首。

translations.literal: By custom they knew writing; their king wore a topknot with a black cap, his wife a brocade robe and woven skirt with golden flower ornaments in her hair.
translations.idiomatic: They knew writing by custom. The king wore a topknot with a black cap; his wife wore brocade robes and woven skirts with golden flower ornaments in her hair.

sentences.zh: 男子服長裙繒冒，或冠瀍。

translations.literal: Men wore long skirts and silk caps, or caps of chan.
translations.idiomatic: Men wore long skirts and silk caps, or caps of chan.

sentences.zh: 婦人辮發縈後，綴珠貝。

translations.literal: Women braided their hair behind and adorned it with pearls and shells.
translations.idiomatic: Women braided their hair behind and adorned it with pearls and shells.

sentences.zh: 婚禮，富家厚納聘，貧者竊妻去。

translations.literal: For marriage, the wealthy paid heavy bride-price; the poor stole wives away.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy families paid heavy bride-prices; the poor eloped with their brides.

sentences.zh: 父死妻庶母，兄死妻嫂。

translations.literal: When a father died, a son married his stepmother; when an elder brother died, he married his sister-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: When a father died, a son might marry his stepmother; when an elder brother died, he might marry his sister-in-law.

sentences.zh: 喪有服，葬已即除。

translations.literal: Mourning garments were worn for funerals and removed immediately after burial.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning garments were worn for funerals and removed as soon as burial was complete.

sentences.zh: 民無常稅，用不足，乃斂富室商人，足而止。

translations.literal: The people paid no fixed taxes; when revenue was insufficient, they levied the wealthy and merchants until needs were met.
translations.idiomatic: There were no fixed taxes; when revenue fell short, the wealthy and merchants were levied until needs were met.

sentences.zh: 凡殺人若盜馬者死，它罪贖以物。

translations.literal: Murderers and horse thieves were put to death; other crimes were redeemed with goods.
translations.idiomatic: Murderers and horse thieves were executed; other crimes were redeemed with goods.

sentences.zh: 地多寒，宜麥、菽、粟、蕪菁，出小馬、犛牛、銅、鐵、丹砂。

translations.literal: The land was mostly cold, suited to wheat, beans, millet, and turnips; it produced small horses, yaks, copper, iron, and cinnabar.
translations.idiomatic: The land was mostly cold, suited to wheat, beans, millet, and turnips; it produced small horses, yaks, copper, iron, and cinnabar.

sentences.zh: 有青海者，周八九百里，中有山，須冰合，遊牝馬其上，明年生駒，號龍種。

translations.literal: There was Qinghai Lake, eight or nine hundred li in circumference, with a mountain in its midst; when ice had fully formed, mares were driven onto it to mate, and the foals born the next year were called dragon seed.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghai Lake measured eight or nine hundred li around, with a mountain at its center. When ice fully formed, mares were driven onto it to mate; foals born the next year were called dragon seed.

sentences.zh: 嘗得波斯馬，牧於海，生驄駒，日步千里，故世稱「青海驄」。

translations.literal: They once obtained Persian horses and pastured them by the lake; the foals born were dappled grays that could travel a thousand li in a day, hence the world called them Qinghai dappled grays.
translations.idiomatic: They once obtained Persian horses and pastured them by the lake; the foals born were dappled grays traveling a thousand li in a day, hence the world called them Qinghai dappled grays.

sentences.zh: 西北有流沙數百里，夏有熱風，傷行人。

translations.literal: To the northwest were drifting sands extending several hundred li; in summer hot winds injured travelers.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest lay drifting sands extending several hundred li; in summer hot winds injured travelers.

sentences.zh: 風將發，老駝引項鳴，埋鼻沙中，人候之，以氈蔽鼻口乃無恙。

translations.literal: When the wind was about to rise, old camels would stretch their necks and cry, burying their noses in the sand; people watched for this and covered nose and mouth with felt to escape harm.
translations.idiomatic: When the wind was about to rise, old camels stretched their necks and cried, burying their noses in the sand; people watched for this sign and covered nose and mouth with felt to escape harm.

sentences.zh: 隋時，其王慕容伏允號步薩缽，嘗寇邊。

translations.literal: During the Sui dynasty, their king Murong Fuyun, titled Busabo, frequently raided the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui dynasty, their king Murong Fuyun, titled Busabo, frequently raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 煬帝遣鐵勒敗之，壁西平；

translations.literal: Emperor Yang dispatched the Tiele to defeat him, and he fortified himself at Xiping;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang dispatched the Tiele to defeat him, and he fortified himself at Xiping;

sentences.zh: 復命觀王雄破其眾。

translations.literal: he then ordered Prince Guan to break his forces.
translations.idiomatic: he then ordered Prince Guan to rout his forces.

sentences.zh: 伏允以數十騎入泥嶺，亡去，仙頭王率男女十餘萬降。

translations.literal: Fuyun fled with several dozen horsemen into Mount Ni; King Xiantou led more than one hundred thousand men and women in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyun fled with several dozen horsemen into Mount Ni; King Xiantou led more than one hundred thousand men and women in surrender.

sentences.zh: 置郡縣鎮戍，以長子順為質，因王之，統餘眾，俄追還。

translations.literal: Prefectures, counties, and garrison posts were established; his eldest son Shun was kept as hostage and installed as king to rule the remaining people, but he was soon recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures, counties, and garrison posts were established; his eldest son Shun was kept as hostage and installed as king over the remaining people, but was soon recalled.

sentences.zh: 伏允客党項，隋亂，因得復故地。

translations.literal: Fuyun took refuge with the Tangut; amid the Sui turmoil he recovered his former territory.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyun took refuge with the Tangut; amid the Sui turmoil he recovered his former territory.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，順自江都還長安，於時李軌據涼州，帝乃約伏允和，令擊軌自效，當護送順。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the Mandate, Shun returned from Jiangdu to Chang'an; at that time Li Gui held Liang Prefecture, so the emperor made a pact with Fuyun for peace, ordering him to attack Gui to prove his loyalty, whereupon Shun would be escorted home.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, Shun returned from Jiangdu to Chang'an. Li Gui then held Liang Prefecture, so the emperor made peace with Fuyun, ordering him to attack Li Gui to prove his loyalty in exchange for Shun's return.

sentences.zh: 伏允喜，引兵與軌戰庫門，交綏止，即遣使請順，帝遣之。

translations.literal: Fuyun was pleased, led troops to battle Li Gui at Kumen, fought to a standstill, and immediately sent envoys requesting Shun; the emperor dispatched him.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyun was pleased, led troops against Li Gui at Kumen, fought to a standstill, and immediately requested Shun's return; the emperor sent him.

sentences.zh: 順至，號為大寧王。

translations.literal: When Shun arrived, he was titled King of Daning.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun arrived, he was titled King of Daning.

sentences.zh: 太宗時，伏允遣使者入朝，未還，即寇鄯州。

translations.literal: During Emperor Taizong's reign, Fuyun sent envoys to court; before they returned he raided Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Taizong's reign, Fuyun sent envoys to court; before they returned he raided Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使者讓，且召伏允；

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to reproach him and summoned Fuyun;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to reproach him and summoned Fuyun;

sentences.zh: 以疾為解，而為子求婚，驗帝意。

translations.literal: he pleaded illness as excuse, but sought a marriage alliance for his son to test the emperor's intentions.
translations.idiomatic: he pleaded illness, but sought a marriage alliance for his son to test the emperor's intentions.

sentences.zh: 帝召子親迎，亦稱疾。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the son to come in person for the marriage, but he too claimed illness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned the son to come in person for the marriage, but he too claimed illness.

sentences.zh: 有詔止婚，遣中郎將康處真臨諭。

translations.literal: An edict halted the marriage and dispatched Lieutenant General Kang Chuzhen to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict halted the marriage and dispatched Lieutenant General Kang Chuzhen to instruct him.

sentences.zh: 又掠岷州，都督李道彥擊走之，執名王二，斬級七百。

translations.literal: He again raided Min Prefecture; Military Governor Li Daoyan drove him off, capturing two titled kings and taking seven hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: He again raided Min Prefecture; Military Governor Li Daoyan drove him off, capturing two titled kings and seven hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 連歲遣名王朝。

translations.literal: Year after year he sent titled princes to court.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year he sent titled princes to court.

sentences.zh: 俄寇涼州，鄯州刺史李玄運表吐谷渾牧馬青海，輕兵掩之，可盡致。

translations.literal: Soon he raided Liang Prefecture; Prefect Li Xuanyun memorialized that Tuyuhun horses were pastured at Qinghai and could be taken entirely by a light strike.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he raided Liang Prefecture; Prefect Li Xuanyun memorialized that Tuyuhun horses pastured at Qinghai could be seized entirely by a light strike.

sentences.zh: 乃命左驍衛大將軍段誌玄、左驍衛將軍梁洛仁率契、党項兵擊之，未至三十里，誌玄等不欲戰，壁而留。

translations.literal: Left Piaoqi Guard General Duan Zhixuan and Left Piaoqi Guard Commander Liang Luoren were ordered to lead Qi and Tangut troops against them; within thirty li they did not wish to fight and encamped to wait.
translations.idiomatic: Left Piaoqi Guard General Duan Zhixuan and Left Piaoqi Guard Commander Liang Luoren were ordered to lead Qi and Tangut troops against them; within thirty li they halted and encamped without fighting.

sentences.zh: 虜知之，驅牧馬走。

translations.literal: The barbarians detected this and drove their herds away.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians detected this and drove their herds away.

sentences.zh: 副將李君羨率精騎尾襲懸水上，得牛羊二萬還。

translations.literal: Deputy Commander Li Junxian led elite cavalry in pursuit along the Xuanshui River, returning with twenty thousand cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Commander Li Junxian led elite cavalry in pursuit along the Xuanshui River, returning with twenty thousand cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 是時，伏允耄不能事，其相天柱王用事，拘天子行人鴻臚丞趙德楷。

translations.literal: At this time Fuyun was aged and unable to govern; his minister Tianzhu Wang held power and detained the court's envoy, Director of Ceremonies Zhao Dekai.
translations.idiomatic: By then Fuyun was aged and unable to govern; his minister Tianzhu Wang held power and detained the court's envoy, Director of Ceremonies Zhao Dekai.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使曉敕，十返，無悛言。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys with imperial instructions ten times; there was no word of repentance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys with imperial instructions ten times; there was no word of repentance.

sentences.zh: 貞觀九年，詔李靖為西海道行軍大總管，侯君集積石道，任城王道宗鄯善道，李道彥赤水道，李大亮且末道，高甑生鹽澤道，並為行軍總管，率突厥、契兵擊之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenguan, an edict appointed Li Jing as Grand Campaign Commander of the Xihai Circuit, Hou Junji of the Jishi Circuit, Prince of Rencheng Li Daozong of the Shanshan Circuit, Li Daoyan of the Chishui Circuit, Li Daliang of the Qimo Circuit, and Gao Zangsheng of the Yanze Circuit—all as campaign commanders leading Turk and Qi troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhenguan, Li Jing was appointed Grand Campaign Commander of the Xihai Route, Hou Junji of the Jishi Route, Prince of Rencheng Li Daozong of the Shanshan Route, Li Daoyan of the Chishui Route, Li Daliang of the Qimo Route, and Gao Zangsheng of the Yanze Route—all leading Turk and Qi troops against Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 党項內屬羌及洮州羌，皆殺刺史歸伏允。

translations.literal: The Tangut who had submitted inward and the Tao Prefecture Tangut all killed their prefects and submitted to Fuyun.
translations.idiomatic: The submitted Tangut and the Tao Prefecture Tangut all killed their prefects and submitted to Fuyun.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，道宗破伏允於庫山，俘斬四百。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, Daozong defeated Fuyun at Mount Ku, capturing and killing four hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, Daozong defeated Fuyun at Mount Ku, capturing and killing four hundred.

sentences.zh: 伏允謀入磧疲唐兵，燒野草，故靖馬多饑。

translations.literal: Fuyun planned to enter the desert to wear down the Tang army and burn the wild grasses, so Jing's horses mostly went hungry.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyun planned to enter the desert to wear down the Tang army and burn the wild grasses, leaving Jing's horses mostly hungry.

sentences.zh: 道宗曰：「柏海近河源，古未有至者。

translations.literal: Daozong said: "Bohai is near the source of the Yellow River; in antiquity none had ever reached it.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong said: "Bohai lies near the source of the Yellow River; in antiquity none had ever reached it.

sentences.zh: 伏允西走，未知其在，方馬臒糧乏，難遠入，不如按軍鄯州，須馬壯更圖之。」

translations.literal: Fuyun has fled westward and we do not know where he is; our horses are thin and grain is scarce—it is hard to go far. Better to hold the army at Shan Prefecture and wait until the horses are strong before planning further."
translations.idiomatic: Fuyun has fled westward to parts unknown; our horses are thin and grain scarce—it is hard to go far. Better to hold at Shan Prefecture until the horses recover before planning further.

sentences.zh: 君集曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Junji said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Junji replied: "Not so.

sentences.zh: 向者段誌玄至鄯州，吐谷渾兵輒傅城，彼國方完，逆眾用命也。

translations.literal: Formerly when Duan Zhixuan reached Shan Prefecture, Tuyuhun troops pressed against the walls—their state was intact and the rebels fought with full loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Zhixuan reached Shan Prefecture, Tuyuhun troops pressed against the walls—their state was intact and they fought with full loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今虜大敗，斥候無在，君臣相失，我乘其困，可以得誌。

translations.literal: Now the barbarians are greatly defeated, scouts are nowhere to be found, ruler and ministers are separated—we should seize their distress and achieve our aim.
translations.idiomatic: Now the barbarians are crushed, scouts are nowhere, ruler and ministers are separated—we should seize their distress and finish the task.

sentences.zh: 柏海雖遠，可鼓而至也。」

translations.literal: Though Bohai is far, we can drum our way there."
translations.idiomatic: Though Bohai is far, we can drum our way there."

sentences.zh: 靖曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Jing said: "Well said."
translations.idiomatic: Jing said: "Well said."

sentences.zh: 分二軍：靖與大亮、薛萬均以一軍趣北，出其右；

translations.literal: The army was divided in two: Jing with Daliang and Xue Wanjun took one column northward to emerge on their right;
translations.idiomatic: The army divided in two: Jing with Daliang and Xue Wanjun took one column north to emerge on their right;

sentences.zh: 君集、道宗以一軍趣南，出其左。

translations.literal: Junji and Daozong took one column southward to emerge on their left.
translations.idiomatic: Junji and Daozong took one column south to emerge on their left.

sentences.zh: 靖將薩孤吳仁以輕騎戰曼都山，斬名王，獲五百級。

translations.literal: Jing had Sagou Wuren fight with light cavalry at Mount Mandu, beheading a titled king and taking five hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had Sagou Wuren fight with light cavalry at Mount Mandu, beheading a titled king and taking five hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 諸將戰牛心堆、赤水源，獲虜將南昌王慕容孝俊，收雜畜數萬。

translations.literal: The generals fought at Mount Niuxin and Chishui Source, capturing the barbarian general Nanchang Wang Murong Xiaojun and seizing tens of thousands of mixed livestock.
translations.idiomatic: The generals fought at Mount Niuxin and Chishui Source, capturing the barbarian general Nanchang Wang Murong Xiaojun and tens of thousands of head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 君集、道宗登漢哭山，戰烏海，獲名王梁屈蔥。

translations.literal: Junji and Daozong ascended Mount Hanku and fought at Wuhai, capturing the titled king Liang Qucong.
translations.idiomatic: Junji and Daozong ascended Mount Hanku and fought at Wuhai, capturing the titled king Liang Qucong.

sentences.zh: 靖破天柱部落於赤海，收雜畜二十萬。

translations.literal: Jing destroyed the Tianzhu tribe at Chihai, seizing two hundred thousand mixed livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Jing destroyed the Tianzhu tribe at Chihai, seizing two hundred thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 大亮俘名王二十，雜畜五萬，次且末之西。

translations.literal: Daliang captured twenty titled kings and fifty thousand mixed livestock, halting west of Qimo.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang captured twenty titled kings and fifty thousand head of livestock, halting west of Qimo.

sentences.zh: 伏允走圖倫磧，將托於闐，萬均督銳騎追亡數百里，又破之。

translations.literal: Fuyun fled to the Tulun desert, intending to take refuge with Khotan; Wanjun led crack cavalry in pursuit for several hundred li and defeated him again.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyun fled to the Tulun desert, intending to take refuge with Khotan; Wanjun led crack cavalry in pursuit for several hundred li and defeated him again.

sentences.zh: 士乏水，刺馬飲血。

translations.literal: The soldiers lacked water and pierced their horses to drink the blood.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers lacked water and pierced their horses to drink the blood.

sentences.zh: 君集、道宗行空荒二千里，盛夏降霜，乏水草，士糜冰，馬秣雪。

translations.literal: Junji and Daozong marched two thousand li through empty wilderness; in midsummer frost fell, water and fodder were lacking, soldiers ate ice, and horses fed on snow.
translations.idiomatic: Junji and Daozong marched two thousand li through empty wilderness. In midsummer frost fell; water and fodder ran out, soldiers ate ice, and horses fed on snow.

sentences.zh: 閱月，次星宿川，達柏海上，望積石山，覽觀河源。

translations.literal: Within a month they reached Xingsu River, arrived at Bohai Lake, gazed upon Jishi Mountain, and viewed the source of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month they reached Xingsu River and Bohai Lake, gazing upon Jishi Mountain and the source of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 執失思力馳破虜車重。

translations.literal: Zhishisili charged and broke the barbarians' baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishisili charged and smashed the barbarians' baggage train.

sentences.zh: 兩軍會於大非川、破邏真谷。

translations.literal: The two armies joined at Dafeichuan and Poluozheng Valley.
translations.idiomatic: The two armies joined at Dafeichuan and Poluozheng Valley.

sentences.zh: 順之質隋，為金紫光祿大夫、伏允立其弟為太子。

translations.literal: Shun had been a hostage in Sui and was made Gold Purple Light Grand Master; Fuyun established his younger brother as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Shun had been a hostage in Sui and was made Gold Purple Light Grand Master; Fuyun established his younger brother as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 順歸，常鞅鞅，自以失位，欲以功自結天子，乃斬天柱王，舉國降。

translations.literal: When Shun returned he was often discontented, feeling he had lost his position; wishing to win the Son of Heaven's favor through merit, he beheaded Tianzhu Wang and led the entire state in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun returned he was often discontented, feeling displaced. Seeking to win the emperor's favor through merit, he beheaded Tianzhu Wang and led the entire kingdom in surrender.

sentences.zh: 伏允懼，引千餘騎遁磧中，眾稍亡，從者才百騎，窮無聊，即自經死。

translations.literal: Fuyun was terrified, fled with more than a thousand horsemen into the desert; his followers gradually deserted until only a hundred horsemen remained; in utter destitution he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyun fled in terror with a thousand horsemen into the desert. His followers gradually deserted until only a hundred remained; in utter destitution he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 國人立順為君，稱臣內附，詔封四平郡王，號越胡呂烏甘豆可汗。

translations.literal: The people of the state established Shun as ruler; he declared himself a subject and submitted inward. An edict enfeoffed him as Prince of Siping and titled him Khan Yuehulugandou.
translations.idiomatic: The people established Shun as ruler. He submitted to the Tang and was enfeoffed as Prince of Siping with the title Khan Yuehulugandou.

sentences.zh: 帝恐未能定其國，遣李大亮率精兵鎮援。

translations.literal: The emperor feared the state might not yet be settled and dispatched Li Daliang with elite troops to garrison and support it.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the kingdom was not yet settled, the emperor dispatched Li Daliang with elite troops to garrison and support it.

sentences.zh: 順久質華，國人不附，卒為下所殺，立其子燕王諾曷缽。

translations.literal: Shun had long been a hostage in China and was not accepted by his people; he was eventually killed by his subordinates, who established his son, Prince of Yan Nuohebo.
translations.idiomatic: Shun had long been a hostage in China and was not accepted by his people; his subordinates killed him and established his son, Prince of Yan Nuohebo.

sentences.zh: 諾曷缽幼，大臣爭權。

translations.literal: Nuohebo was young and ministers contended for power.
translations.idiomatic: Nuohebo was young, and ministers contended for power.

sentences.zh: 帝詔侯君集就經紀之，始請頒歷及子弟入侍。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Hou Junji to administer the state; they first requested the issuance of the calendar and that princes enter court as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Hou Junji to administer the state; they first requested the Tang calendar and that princes enter court as hostages.

sentences.zh: 詔封諾曷缽河源郡王，號為地也拔勒豆可汗，遣淮陽郡王道明持節冊命，賜鼓纛。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed Nuohebo as Prince of Heyuan and titled him Khan Diyebledou; Prince of Huaiyang Li Daoming was dispatched with credentials to invest him and bestow drums and banners.
translations.idiomatic: Nuohebo was enfeoffed as Prince of Heyuan with the title Khan Diyebledou. Prince of Huaiyang Li Daoming was dispatched to invest him and bestow drums and banners.

sentences.zh: 諾曷缽身入謝，遂請婚，獻馬牛羊萬。

translations.literal: Nuohebo came in person to give thanks and then requested a marriage alliance, presenting ten thousand horses, cattle, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Nuohebo came in person to give thanks, then requested a marriage alliance and presented ten thousand horses, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 比年入朝，乃以宗室女為弘化公主妻之，詔道明及右武衛將軍慕容寶持節送公主。

translations.literal: In succeeding years he came to court; an imperial clanswoman was made Princess Honghua and given to him in marriage; Daoming and Right Martial Guard General Murong Bao were ordered to escort the princess.
translations.idiomatic: In succeeding years he came to court. An imperial clanswoman was made Princess Honghua and given to him in marriage; Daoming and Right Martial Guard General Murong Bao escorted the princess.

sentences.zh: 其相宣王跋扈，謀作亂，欲襲公主，劫諾曷缽奔吐蕃。

translations.literal: His minister Xuan Wang was overbearing and plotted rebellion, intending to seize the princess and abduct Nuohebo to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: His minister Xuan Wang was overbearing and plotted rebellion, intending to seize the princess and abduct Nuohebo to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 諾曷缽知之，引輕騎走鄯城，威信王以兵迎之。

translations.literal: Nuohebo learned of this and fled with light cavalry to Shancheng; Prince of Weixin welcomed him with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of the plot, Nuohebo fled with light cavalry to Shancheng, where Prince of Weixin welcomed him with troops.

sentences.zh: 果毅都尉席君買率兵與威信王共討，斬其兄弟三人，國大擾。

translations.literal: Fruit-and-Courage Commandant Xi Junmai led troops with Prince of Weixin to suppress them, beheading three of Xuan Wang's brothers; the state was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Fruit-and-Courage Commandant Xi Junmai joined Prince of Weixin in suppressing them, beheading three of Xuan Wang's brothers and throwing the kingdom into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 帝又詔民部尚書唐儉、中書舍人馬周持節撫慰。

translations.literal: The emperor again ordered Minister of Revenue Tang Jian and Secretariat Draftsman Ma Zhou to go with credentials to console and reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again ordered Minister of Revenue Tang Jian and Secretariat Draftsman Ma Zhou to console and reassure them.

sentences.zh: 高宗立，以主故，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, because of the princess Nuohebo was made Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, Nuohebo was made Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant because of the princess.

sentences.zh: 又獻名馬，帝問馬種性，使者曰：「國之最良者。」

translations.literal: He again presented famous horses; the emperor inquired about the breed and nature of the horses, and the envoy said: "They are the finest in the state.
translations.idiomatic: He again presented famous horses. When the emperor inquired about the breed, the envoy replied: "They are the finest in our kingdom.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「良馬人所愛。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Fine horses are beloved by men."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Fine horses are beloved by all men."

sentences.zh: 詔還其馬。

translations.literal: An edict returned the horses.
translations.idiomatic: An edict returned the horses.

sentences.zh: 公主表請入朝，遣左驍衛將軍鮮于匡濟迎之。

translations.literal: The princess petitioned to come to court; Left Piaoqi Guard General Xianyu Kuangji was dispatched to escort her.
translations.idiomatic: The princess petitioned to come to court; Left Piaoqi Guard General Xianyu Kuangji was dispatched to escort her.

sentences.zh: 十一月，及諾曷缽至京師，帝又以宗室女金城縣主妻其長子蘇度摸末，拜左領軍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Nuohebo and the princess arrived at the capital; the emperor also gave an imperial clanswoman, County Princess of Jincheng, to his eldest son Sumomomo and appointed him Left Vanguard Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Nuohebo and the princess arrived at the capital. The emperor also gave County Princess of Jincheng to his eldest son Sumomomo and appointed him Left Vanguard Guard General.

sentences.zh: 久之，摸末死，主與次子右武衛大將軍梁漢王闥盧摸末來請婚，帝以宗室女金明縣主妻之。

translations.literal: After a time Momo died; the princess and the second son, Right Martial Guard General Prince of Lianghan Tulumomo, came to request a marriage; the emperor gave County Princess of Jinming to Tulumomo.
translations.idiomatic: After a time Momo died. The princess and the second son, Right Martial Guard General Prince of Lianghan Tulumomo, came to request a marriage; the emperor gave County Princess of Jinming to Tulumomo.

sentences.zh: 既而與吐蕃相攻，上書相曲直，並來請師，天子兩不許。

translations.literal: Thereafter they fought with Tibet; both sides petitioned the court with their grievances and requested troops; the Son of Heaven refused both.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they fought with Tibet. Both sides petitioned the court with their grievances and requested troops; the emperor refused both.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾大臣素和貴奔吐蕃，言其情，吐蕃出兵搗虛，破其眾黃河上。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun minister Suhe Gui fled to Tibet and revealed their situation; Tibet dispatched troops to strike at a weak point and broke their forces on the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun minister Suhe Gui fled to Tibet and revealed their situation. Tibet dispatched troops to strike at a weak point and broke their forces on the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 諾曷缽不支，與公主引數千帳走涼州。

translations.literal: Nuohebo could not hold out; with the princess he led several thousand tents to flee to Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to hold out, Nuohebo fled with the princess and several thousand tents to Liang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 帝遣左武衛大將軍蘇定方為安集大使，平兩國怨。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched Left Martial Guard General Su Dingfang as Pacification Commissioner to settle the grievances between the two states.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Left Martial Guard General Su Dingfang as Pacification Commissioner to settle the grievances between the two kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃遂有其地。

translations.literal: Tibet thereupon took their territory.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet thereupon seized their territory.

sentences.zh: 諾曷缽請內徙。

translations.literal: Nuohebo requested resettlement inward.
translations.idiomatic: Nuohebo requested resettlement within Tang territory.

sentences.zh: 乾封初，更封青海國王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianfeng, he was again enfeoffed as King of Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qianfeng he was again enfeoffed as King of Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 帝欲徙其部於涼州之南山，群臣議不同，帝難之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to relocate their tribe to the southern mountains of Liang Prefecture; ministers debated and disagreed, and the emperor found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to relocate their tribe to the southern mountains of Liang Prefecture; ministers debated without agreement, and the emperor hesitated.

sentences.zh: 咸亨元年，乃以右威衛大將軍薛仁貴為邏娑道行軍大總管，左衛員外大將軍阿史那道真、左衛將軍郭待封副之，總兵五萬討吐蕃，且納諾曷缽於故廷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianheng, Right Martial Guard General Xue Rengui was made Grand Campaign Commander of the Luosuo Circuit, with Left Guard External Grand General Ashina Daozhen and Left Guard General Guo Daifeng as deputies, leading fifty thousand troops against Tibet and to restore Nuohebo to his former court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianheng, Right Martial Guard General Xue Rengui was made Grand Campaign Commander of the Luosuo Route, with Ashina Daozhen and Guo Daifeng as deputies, leading fifty thousand troops against Tibet to restore Nuohebo to his former court.

sentences.zh: 王師敗於大非川，舉吐谷渾地皆陷，諾曷缽與親近數千帳才免。

translations.literal: The imperial army was defeated at Dafeichuan; all Tuyuhun territory fell; Nuohebo and several thousand tents of kin barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army was defeated at Dafeichuan. All Tuyuhun territory fell; Nuohebo and several thousand tents of kin barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 三年，乃徙浩水南。

translations.literal: In the third year they were relocated south of the Hao River.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year they were relocated south of the Hao River.

sentences.zh: 諾曷缽以吐蕃盛，勢不抗，而鄯州地狹，又徙靈州，帝為置安樂州，即拜刺史，欲其安且樂雲。

translations.literal: Nuohebo, seeing Tibetan power and unable to resist, and finding Shan Prefecture too narrow, was again relocated to Ling Prefecture; the emperor established Anle Prefecture for them and appointed him prefect, wishing them peace and contentment.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Tibetan power and unable to resist, and finding Shan Prefecture too narrow, Nuohebo was relocated to Ling Prefecture. The emperor established Anle Prefecture and appointed him prefect, wishing them peace and contentment.

sentences.zh: 諾曷缽死，子忠立。

translations.literal: Nuohebo died and his son Zhong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Nuohebo died; his son Zhong succeeded.

sentences.zh: 忠死，子宣超立，聖歷三年，拜左豹韜員外大將軍，襲故可汗號，餘部詣涼、甘、肅、瓜、沙等州降。

translations.literal: When Zhong died his son Xuanchao succeeded; in the third year of Shengli, Xuanchao was appointed External Grand General of the Left Leopard Bow Guard and inherited the former khan title; the remaining tribes submitted to Liang, Gan, Su, Gua, Sha, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong died his son Xuanchao succeeded. In the third year of Shengli, Xuanchao inherited the former khan title; the remaining tribes submitted to Liang, Gan, Su, Gua, Sha, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 宰相張錫與右武衛大將軍唐休璟議徙其人於秦、隴、豐、靈間，令不得畔去。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Xi and Right Martial Guard General Tang Xiujing debated relocating the people among Qin, Long, Feng, and Ling, so they could not rebel and flee.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Xi and Right Martial Guard General Tang Xiujing debated relocating the people among Qin, Long, Feng, and Ling to prevent rebellion and flight.

sentences.zh: 涼州都督郭元振以為：「吐谷渾近秦、隴，則與監牧雜處；

translations.literal: Liang Prefecture Military Governor Guo Yuanzhen argued: "If Tuyuhun are placed near Qin and Long, they will mix with the imperial stud farms;
translations.idiomatic: Liang Prefecture Military Governor Guo Yuanzhen argued: "Placing Tuyuhun near Qin and Long would mix them with the imperial stud farms;

sentences.zh: 置豐、靈，又邇默啜；

translations.literal: if placed at Feng and Ling, they will again be close to Mohe;
translations.idiomatic: placing them at Feng and Ling would put them close to Mohe again;

sentences.zh: 假在諸華，亦不遽移其性也。

translations.literal: even if placed among the Chinese, their nature would not quickly change.
translations.idiomatic: even among the Chinese, their nature would not quickly change.

sentences.zh: 前日王孝傑自河源軍徙耽爾乙句貴置靈州，既其叛，乃入牧坊掠群馬，瘢夷州縣，是則遷中土無益之成驗。

translations.literal: Formerly Wang Xiaojie relocated Danier Yijugui from Heyuan Army to Ling Prefecture; when he rebelled he entered the stud farms to plunder herds and ravaged the prefectures and counties—this is proven evidence that relocation to the interior is useless.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Wang Xiaojie relocated Danier Yijugui from Heyuan Army to Ling Prefecture; when he rebelled he plundered the stud farms and ravaged the prefectures—proof that relocation to the interior is useless.

sentences.zh: 往素和貴叛去，於我無損，但失吐谷渾數十部，豈與句貴比邪？

translations.literal: When Suhe Gui rebelled and fled, we lost nothing—but we did lose several dozen Tuyuhun tribes. Can that compare with Yijugui?
translations.idiomatic: When Suhe Gui rebelled and fled, we lost nothing but several dozen Tuyuhun tribes. Can that compare with Yijugui?

sentences.zh: 今降虜非強服，皆突矢刃，棄吐蕃而來，宜當循其情，為之制也。

translations.literal: The present submitters are not forcibly subdued; all braved blades and abandoned Tibet to come. Their sentiments should be followed and institutions made for them.
translations.idiomatic: The present submitters came willingly, braving blades to abandon Tibet. Their sentiments should be respected and institutions tailored to them.

sentences.zh: 當甘、肅、瓜、沙降者，即其所置之。

translations.literal: Those who submitted at Gan, Su, Gua, and Sha should be settled where they submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Those who submitted at Gan, Su, Gua, and Sha should be settled where they submitted.

sentences.zh: 因所投而居，情易安，磔數州則勢自分。

translations.literal: Settling them where they chose makes them easy to pacify; splitting them across several prefectures divides their power.
translations.idiomatic: Settling them where they chose eases their minds; splitting them across prefectures divides their power.

sentences.zh: 順其情，分其勢，不擾於人，可謂善奪戎心者也。

translations.literal: Following their sentiments and dividing their power without disturbing the people—this may be called skillfully winning barbarian hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Following their sentiments and dividing their power without disturbing the people is skillfully winning barbarian hearts.

sentences.zh: 歲遣鎮遏使者與宣超兄弟撫護之，無令相侵奪，生業固矣。

translations.literal: Each year dispatch pacification commissioners with Xuanchao and his brothers to protect them and prevent mutual encroachment, and their livelihoods will be secure.
translations.idiomatic: Each year dispatch pacification commissioners with Xuanchao and his brothers to protect them from mutual encroachment, and their livelihoods will be secure.

sentences.zh: 有如叛去，無損中國。」

translations.literal: If they rebel and flee, China loses nothing.
translations.idiomatic: If they rebel and flee, the empire loses nothing.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 宣超死，子曦皓立。

translations.literal: When Xuanchao died his son Xihao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanchao died his son Xihao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 曦皓死，子兆立。

translations.literal: When Xihao died his son Zhao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Xihao died his son Zhao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃復取安樂州，而殘部徙朔方、河東，語謬為「退渾」。

translations.literal: Tibet again took Anle Prefecture, and the remnant tribes were relocated to Shuofang and Hedong; their speech was corrupted to "Tuihun."
translations.idiomatic: Tibet again took Anle Prefecture, and the remnant tribes were relocated to Shuofang and Hedong; their name was corrupted in speech to "Tuihun."

sentences.zh: 貞元十四年，以朔方節度副使、左金吾衛大將軍慕容復為長樂都督、青海國王，襲可汗號。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan, Shuofang Frontier Deputy Military Governor and Left Golden Guard General Murong Fu was made Military Governor of Changle and King of Qinghai, inheriting the khan title.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan, Shuofang Frontier Deputy Military Governor Murong Fu was made Military Governor of Changle and King of Qinghai, inheriting the khan title.

sentences.zh: 復死，停襲。

translations.literal: When Fu died the inheritance ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu died the line of inheritance ceased.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾自晉永嘉時有國，至龍朔三年吐蕃取其地，凡三百五十年，及此封嗣絕矣。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun had had a state since the Yongjia era of Jin; in the third year of Longshuo Tibet took their land—three hundred fifty years in all—and with this enfeoffment the succession ended.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun had ruled since the Yongjia era of Jin; in the third year of Longshuo Tibet seized their lands—three hundred fifty years in all—and with this the succession ended.

sentences.zh: 焉耆國直京師西七千里而贏，橫六百里，縱四百里。

translations.literal: Yanqi Kingdom. Yanqi lay seven thousand li west of the capital with surplus, measuring six hundred li across and four hundred li north to south.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqi lay some seven thousand li west of the capital, measuring six hundred li east to west and four hundred li north to south.

sentences.zh: 東高昌，西龜茲，南尉犁，北烏孫。

translations.literal: To the east was Gaochang; to the west Kucha; to the south Weili; to the north Wusun.
translations.idiomatic: It bordered Gaochang on the east, Kucha on the west, Weili on the south, and Wusun on the north.

sentences.zh: 逗渠溉田，土宜黍、蒲陶，有魚鹽利。

translations.literal: Canals irrigated the fields; the soil was suited to millet and grapes, and there was profit in fish and salt.
translations.idiomatic: Canals irrigated the fields; the soil suited millet and grapes, and fish and salt brought profit.

sentences.zh: 俗祝髮氈衣。

translations.literal: By custom they shaved their heads and wore felt garments.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they shaved their heads and wore felt garments.

sentences.zh: 戶四千，勝兵二千，常役屬西突厥。

translations.literal: Households numbered four thousand; effective fighting forces two thousand; they were regularly subject to the Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: There were four thousand households and two thousand warriors; they were regularly subject to the Western Turks.

sentences.zh: 俗尚娛遨，二月朏出野祀，四月望日遊林，七月七日祀生祖，十月望日王始出遊，至歲盡止。

translations.literal: By custom they valued amusement; on the second day of the second month they went out to the wilds for sacrifice; on the fifteenth of the fourth month they roamed the forests; on the seventh day of the seventh month they sacrificed to the birth ancestor; on the fifteenth of the tenth month the king first went out touring, continuing until year's end.
translations.idiomatic: They valued amusement by custom: on the second day of the second month they sacrificed in the wilds; on the fifteenth of the fourth month they roamed the forests; on the seventh day of the seventh month they sacrificed to the birth ancestor; from the fifteenth of the tenth month the king toured until year's end.

sentences.zh: 太原貞觀六年，其王龍突騎支始遣使來朝。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan of the Taiyuan era, their king Long Tuqizhi first sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenguan, their king Long Tuqizhi first sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 自隋亂，磧路閉，故西域朝貢皆道高昌。

translations.literal: Since the Sui turmoil the desert route was closed, so Western Regions tribute missions all passed through Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Sui turmoil the desert route was closed, and Western Regions tribute missions all passed through Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 突騎支請開大磧道以便行人，帝許之。

translations.literal: Tuqizhi requested opening the great desert route to ease travelers; the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Tuqizhi requested opening the great desert route for travelers; the emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 高昌怒，大掠其邊。

translations.literal: Gaochang was enraged and raided their frontier heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Gaochang was enraged and launched heavy raids on their frontier.

sentences.zh: 西突厥莫賀設與咄陸弩失畢作難，來奔，咄陸弩失畢復攻之，遣使言狀，並貢名馬。

translations.literal: The Western Turk Moheshe and Dulunushibi made trouble and came to submit; Dulunushibi again attacked them; they sent envoys reporting the situation and presenting famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Turk Moheshe and Dulunushibi made trouble and came to submit; Dulunushibi again attacked them. They sent envoys reporting the situation and presenting famous horses.

sentences.zh: 咥利失可汗立，素善焉耆，故倚為援。

translations.literal: When Khan Xielishi was established, he was naturally friendly with Yanqi and relied on it as support.
translations.idiomatic: When Khan Xielishi was established, he was naturally friendly with Yanqi and relied on it as support.

sentences.zh: 十二年，處月、處蜜與高昌攻陷其五城，掠千五百人，焚廬舍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Chuyue and Chumi together with Gaochang attacked and took five of its cities, capturing fifteen hundred people and burning dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, Chuyue and Chumi together with Gaochang attacked and took five cities, capturing fifteen hundred people and burning dwellings.

sentences.zh: 侯君集討高昌，遣使與相聞，突騎支喜，引兵佐唐。

translations.literal: When Hou Junji campaigned against Gaochang he sent envoys to communicate; Tuqizhi was pleased and led troops to assist Tang.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Junji campaigned against Gaochang he sent envoys to communicate; Tuqizhi was pleased and led troops to assist the Tang.

sentences.zh: 高昌破，歸向所俘及城，遣使者入謝。

translations.literal: When Gaochang fell, the captives and cities taken were returned; envoys were sent to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaochang fell, captives and seized cities were returned; envoys came to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 西突厥臣屈利啜為弟娶突騎支女，遂相約為輔車勢，不朝貢。

translations.literal: The Western Turk subject Quili Chuo had his brother marry Tuqizhi's daughter and they agreed to mutual support, ceasing tribute to the court.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Turk subject Quili Chuo had his brother marry Tuqizhi's daughter; they agreed to mutual support and ceased tribute to the court.

sentences.zh: 安西都護郭孝恪請討之。

translations.literal: Anxi Protector Guo Xiaoge requested a campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Anxi Protector Guo Xiaoge requested a campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 會王弟頡鼻、栗婆準葉護等三人來降，帝即命孝恪為西州道總管，率兵出銀山道，以栗婆準等為向導。

translations.literal: At this time the king's younger brothers Xiebi, Lipozhun Yehu, and three others came to surrender; the emperor immediately appointed Xiaoge as campaign commander of the Xizhou Route, leading troops out the Yinshan Route with Lipozhun and others as guides.
translations.idiomatic: The king's younger brothers Xiebi, Lipozhun Yehu, and three others came to surrender. The emperor appointed Xiaoge campaign commander of the Xizhou Route, leading troops out the Yinshan Route with Lipozhun and others as guides.

sentences.zh: 初，焉耆所都周三十里，四面大山，海水繚其外，故恃不為虞。

translations.literal: At first Yanqi's capital measured thirty li around, surrounded by great mountains on all four sides with seawater encircling it outside, so they relied on this and were unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqi's capital measured thirty li around, ringed by mountains with seawater encircling it; relying on this, they were unprepared.

sentences.zh: 孝恪倍道絕水，夜傅堞，遲曙噪而登，鼓角轟哄，唐兵縱，國人擾敗，斬千餘級，執突騎支，更以栗婆準攝國事。

translations.literal: Xiaoge marched at double speed, crossed water by night, scaled the walls at dawn with drums and horns thundering; Tang troops charged, the people were thrown into defeat, more than a thousand were beheaded, Tuqizhi was captured, and Lipozhun was left to administer state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoge marched at double speed, crossed water by night, and scaled the walls at dawn amid thundering drums and horns. Tang troops charged; more than a thousand were beheaded, Tuqizhi was captured, and Lipozhun was left to administer affairs.

sentences.zh: 始，帝語近臣曰：「孝恪以八月十一日詣焉耆，閱二旬可至，當以二十二日破之，使者今至矣！」

translations.literal: At first the emperor told close ministers: "Xiaoge will reach Yanqi on the eleventh of the eighth month; within twenty days he should arrive and break them on the twenty-second—the envoy should arrive now!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told close ministers: "Xiaoge will reach Yanqi on the eleventh of the eighth month and break them within twenty days on the twenty-second—the messenger should arrive now!

sentences.zh: 俄而遽人以捷布聞。

translations.literal: Soon a swift messenger arrived with news of victory.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a swift messenger arrived with news of victory.

sentences.zh: 囚突騎支及妻子送洛陽，有詔赦罪。

translations.literal: Tuqizhi and his wife and children were imprisoned and sent to Luoyang; an edict pardoned their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Tuqizhi and his wife and children were sent to Luoyang; an edict pardoned their crimes.

sentences.zh: 屈利啜以兵救焉耆，而孝恪還三日矣。

translations.literal: Quili Chuo came with troops to rescue Yanqi, but Xiaoge had already returned three days earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Quili Chuo came with troops to rescue Yanqi, but Xiaoge had already returned three days earlier.

sentences.zh: 屈利啜囚栗婆準，更使吐屯攝王，遣使以告。

translations.literal: Quili Chuo imprisoned Lipozhun and installed Tutun as regent king, sending envoys to report this.
translations.idiomatic: Quili Chuo imprisoned Lipozhun and installed Tutun as regent king, sending envoys to report this.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「焉耆我所下，爾乃王之邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Yanqi is territory I conquered—yet you would make yourself its king?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Yanqi is territory I conquered—yet you would make yourself its king?

sentences.zh: 吐屯懼，不敢王。

translations.literal: Tutun feared and dared not claim kingship.
translations.idiomatic: Tutun feared and dared not claim kingship.

sentences.zh: 焉耆立栗婆準，而從兄薛婆阿那支自為王，號瞎幹，執栗婆準獻龜茲，殺之。

translations.literal: Yanqi established Lipozhun, but his cousin Xiepo Anazhi made himself king, styled Xiaqian, seized Lipozhun, and presented him to Kucha, where he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqi established Lipozhun, but his cousin Xiepo Anazhi made himself king, styled Xiaqian, seized Lipozhun, and presented him to Kucha, where he was killed.

sentences.zh: 阿史那社爾討龜茲，阿那支奔之，壁東境抗王師，為社爾所禽，數其罪，斬以徇。

translations.literal: Ashina She'er campaigned against Kucha; Anazhi fled to him and fortified the eastern border against the imperial army; he was captured by She'er, his crimes enumerated, and he was beheaded as warning.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina She'er campaigned against Kucha; Anazhi fled to him and fortified the eastern border. She'er captured him, enumerated his crimes, and beheaded him as warning.

sentences.zh: 立突騎支弟婆伽利為王，以其地為焉耆都督府。

translations.literal: Tuqizhi's younger brother Pojiali was established as king, and the territory was made the Yanqi Military Governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Tuqizhi's younger brother Pojiali was established as king, and the territory was organized as the Yanqi Military Governorship.

sentences.zh: 婆伽利死，國人請還前王突騎支，高宗許之，拜左衛大將軍，歸國。

translations.literal: When Pojiali died the people requested the former king Tuqizhi be restored; Emperor Gaozong granted it, appointing him Left Guard Grand General and sending him home.
translations.idiomatic: When Pojiali died the people requested Tuqizhi's restoration; Emperor Gaozong granted it, appointing him Left Guard Grand General and sending him home.

sentences.zh: 死，龍嫩突立。

translations.literal: He died and Long Nentu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died; Long Nentu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 武後長安時，以其國小人寡，過使客不堪其勞，詔四鎮經略使禁止傔使私馬、無品者肉食。

translations.literal: During Empress Wu's Chang'an era, because the state was small and the people few and passing envoys could not bear the labor, an edict ordered the Four Garrisons Frontier Commissioner to forbid private horses of attendants and meat for those without rank.
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Wu's Chang'an era, because the kingdom was small and passing envoys overburdened the people, an edict ordered the Four Garrisons Frontier Commissioner to forbid attendants' private horses and meat for those without rank.

sentences.zh: 開元七年，龍嫩突死，焉吐拂延立。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kaiyuan, Long Nentu died and Long Tufuyan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Kaiyuan, Long Nentu died and Long Tufuyan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 於是十姓可汗請居碎葉，安西節度使湯嘉惠表以焉耆備四鎮。

translations.literal: Then the Ten Surname Khan requested to reside at Suyab; Anxi Military Governor Tang Jiahui memorialized that Yanqi should supplement the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Ten Surname Khan requested residence at Suyab; Anxi Military Governor Tang Jiahui memorialized that Yanqi should supplement the Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 詔焉耆、龜茲、疏勒、於闐征西域賈，各食其征，由北道者輪臺征之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yanqi, Kucha, Kashgar, and Khotan to levy Western Regions merchants, each taking its share of the levy; those on the northern route were levied at Luntai.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yanqi, Kucha, Kashgar, and Khotan to levy Western Regions merchants, each taking its share; those on the northern route were levied at Luntai.

sentences.zh: 訖天寶常朝賀。

translations.literal: Until the Tianbao era they regularly came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Until the Tianbao era they regularly came to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 龜茲龜茲，一曰丘茲，一曰屈茲，東距京師七千里而贏，自焉耆西南步二百里，度小山，經大河二，又步七百里乃至。

translations.literal: Kucha. Kucha, also called Qiuci or Quzi, lay seven thousand li east of the capital with surplus; from Yanqi one walked southwest two hundred li, crossed two small mountains and a great river, then walked seven hundred li more to reach it.
translations.idiomatic: Kucha. Also called Qiuci or Quzi, it lay seven thousand li east of the capital. From Yanqi one walked southwest two hundred li, crossed two small mountains and a great river, then seven hundred li more to reach it.

sentences.zh: 橫千里，縱六百里。

translations.literal: It measured a thousand li across and six hundred li north to south.
translations.idiomatic: It measured a thousand li east to west and six hundred li north to south.

sentences.zh: 土宜麻、麥、粳稻、蒲陶，出黃金。

translations.literal: The soil was suited to hemp, wheat, rice, and grapes; it produced gold.
translations.idiomatic: The soil suited hemp, wheat, rice, and grapes; it produced gold.

sentences.zh: 俗善歌樂，旁行書，貴浮圖法。

translations.literal: By custom they were skilled in song and music, wrote horizontally, and honored the Buddhist law.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they were skilled in song and music, wrote horizontally, and honored Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 產子以木壓首。

translations.literal: When giving birth they press the head with wood.
translations.idiomatic: At childbirth they pressed the infant's head with wood.

sentences.zh: 俗斷髮齊頂，惟君不翦發。

translations.literal: By custom they cut their hair level with the crown; only the king did not cut his hair.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they cut their hair level with the crown; only the king kept his hair uncut.

sentences.zh: 姓白氏。

translations.literal: Their surname was Bai.
translations.idiomatic: They bore the surname Bai.

sentences.zh: 居伊邏廬城，北倚河羯田山，亦曰白山，常有火。

translations.literal: They dwelt in Yilu City, leaning north on Mount Hetian, also called Mount Bai, which constantly had fire.
translations.idiomatic: They dwelt in Yilu City, north of Mount Hetian, also called White Mountain, which perpetually burned with fire.

sentences.zh: 王以錦冒頂，錦袍、寶帶。

translations.literal: The king wore a brocade cap, brocade robe, and jeweled belt.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore a brocade cap, brocade robe, and jeweled belt.

sentences.zh: 歲朔，鬥羊馬橐它七日，觀勝負以卜歲盈耗雲。

translations.literal: At the New Year they matched sheep, horses, and camels for seven days, observing victory and defeat to divine the year's abundance or shortage.
translations.idiomatic: At the New Year they matched sheep, horses, and camels for seven days, reading victory and defeat as omens of the year's harvest.

sentences.zh: 蔥嶺以東俗喜淫，龜茲、於闐置女肆，征其錢。

translations.literal: East of the Congling Pass the custom favored licentiousness; Kucha and Khotan established women's markets and levied fees.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Congling Pass customs favored licentiousness; Kucha and Khotan established women's markets and levied fees.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，王蘇伐勃駃遣使入朝。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the Mandate, King Subo Bodi sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, King Subo Bodi sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 會死，子蘇伐疊立，號時健莫賀俟利發。

translations.literal: He soon died and his son Subo Die succeeded, styled Shijian Mohe Sili Fa.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died and his son Subo Die succeeded, styled Shijian Mohe Sili Fa.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年獻馬，太宗賜璽書，撫慰加等。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan they presented horses; Emperor Taizong bestowed an imperial edict of consolation and raised their rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenguan they presented horses; Emperor Taizong bestowed an imperial edict of consolation and raised their rank.

sentences.zh: 後臣西突厥。

translations.literal: Later they became subjects of the Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Later they became subjects of the Western Turks.

sentences.zh: 郭孝恪伐焉耆，乃遣兵與焉耆影援，自是不朝貢。

translations.literal: When Guo Xiaoge campaigned against Yanqi, they sent troops to assist Yanqi in secret, and from then on did not come to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Xiaoge campaigned against Yanqi, they secretly sent troops to assist Yanqi and thereafter ceased tribute to the court.

sentences.zh: 蘇伐疊死，弟訶黎布失畢立。

translations.literal: When Subo Die died his younger brother Heli Bushibi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Subo Die died his younger brother Heli Bushibi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，兩遣使朝貢，然帝怒其佐焉耆叛，議討之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year they sent envoys to court twice, yet the emperor was angry that they had aided Yanqi's rebellion and debated campaigning against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year they sent envoys twice, yet the emperor was angry they had aided Yanqi's rebellion and debated attacking them.

sentences.zh: 是夜月食昴，詔曰：「月陰精，用刑兆也；

translations.literal: That night the moon eclipsed the Pleiades; an edict said: "The moon is yin essence and an omen of punishment;
translations.idiomatic: That night the moon eclipsed the Pleiades. An edict declared: "The moon is yin essence and an omen of punishment;

sentences.zh: 星胡分，數且終。」

translations.literal: the stars are the Hu constellation—its number is nearly at an end.
translations.idiomatic: the stars mark the Hu constellation—its number is nearly exhausted.

sentences.zh: 乃以阿史那社爾為昆丘道行軍大總管，契何力副之，率安西都護郭孝恪、司農卿楊弘禮、左武衛將軍李海岸等發鐵勒十三部兵十萬討之。

translations.literal: Ashina She'er was made Grand Campaign Commander of the Kunqiu Circuit with Qibi Heli as deputy, leading Anxi Protector Guo Xiaoge, Minister of Agriculture Yang Hongli, Left Martial Guard General Li Haian, and others with one hundred thousand troops from the thirteen Tiele tribes against them.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina She'er was made Grand Campaign Commander of the Kunqiu Route with Qibi Heli as deputy, leading Guo Xiaoge, Yang Hongli, Li Haian, and one hundred thousand Tiele troops against Kucha.

sentences.zh: 社爾分五軍掠其北，執焉耆王阿那支。

translations.literal: She'er divided five armies to raid the north and captured the Yanqi king Anazhi.
translations.idiomatic: She'er divided five armies to raid the north and captured the Yanqi king Anazhi.

sentences.zh: 龜茲大恐，酋長皆棄城走。

translations.literal: Kucha was greatly terrified and chieftains all abandoned their cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Kucha was terrified; chieftains abandoned their cities and fled.

sentences.zh: 社爾次磧石，去王城三百里。

translations.literal: She'er halted at Qishi, three hundred li from the royal city.
translations.idiomatic: She'er halted at Qishi, three hundred li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 先遣伊州刺史韓威以千騎居前，右驍衛將軍曹繼叔次之。

translations.literal: He first dispatched Yizhou Prefect Han Wei with a thousand horsemen in advance, followed by Right Piaoqi Guard General Cao Jishu.
translations.idiomatic: He first dispatched Yizhou Prefect Han Wei with a thousand horsemen, followed by Right Piaoqi Guard General Cao Jishu.

sentences.zh: 至多褐，與王遇，其將羯獵顛兵五萬合戰。

translations.literal: At Duoe they encountered the king; his general Jieliedian with fifty thousand troops joined battle.
translations.idiomatic: At Duoe they encountered the king; his general Jieliedian joined battle with fifty thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 威偽北，王見威兵少，麾而進，威退與繼叔合，還戰，大破之，追奔八十里。

translations.literal: Wei feigned retreat; the king, seeing Wei's troops were few, waved them forward. Wei withdrew and joined Jishu, turned and fought, routing them utterly and pursuing eighty li.
translations.idiomatic: Wei feigned retreat. Seeing his small force, the king pressed the attack. Wei rejoined Jishu, counterattacked, routed the enemy, and pursued eighty li.

sentences.zh: 王嬰城，社爾將圍之，王引突騎西走，城遂拔，孝恪居守。

translations.literal: The king held the city; She'er was about to besiege it when the king fled west with crack cavalry and the city was taken; Xiaoge remained to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: The king held the city. As She'er prepared to besiege it, the king fled west with crack cavalry; the city fell and Xiaoge remained to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 沙州刺史蘇海政、行軍長史薛萬備以精騎窮躡六百里。

translations.literal: Shazhou Prefect Su Haizheng and Campaign Chief Administrator Xue Wanbei led elite cavalry in pursuit for six hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Shazhou Prefect Su Haizheng and Campaign Chief Administrator Xue Wanbei led elite cavalry in pursuit for six hundred li.

sentences.zh: 王計窮，保撥換城，社爾圍之。

translations.literal: The king, at his wit's end, held Boluan City; She'er besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: At his wit's end, the king held Boluan City; She'er besieged it.

sentences.zh: 閱月，執王及羯獵顛。

translations.literal: Within a month the king and Jieliedian were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the king and Jieliedian were captured.

sentences.zh: 其相那利夜逸，以西突厥並國人萬餘來戰，孝恪及子死之。

translations.literal: The minister Nali escaped by night, joined the Western Turks and more than ten thousand countrymen in battle; Xiaoge and his son were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Nali escaped by night, joined the Western Turks and more than ten thousand countrymen in battle; Xiaoge and his son were killed.

sentences.zh: 王師擾，倉部郎中崔義起募兵戰城中，繼叔、威助擊之，斬首三千級。

translations.literal: The imperial army was thrown into disorder; Treasury Section Director Cui Yiqi recruited troops to fight in the city; Jishu and Wei assisted the attack, taking three thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army was thrown into disorder. Treasury Section Director Cui Yiqi recruited troops to fight in the city; Jishu and Wei assisted, taking three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 那利敗，裒亡散復振，還襲王師，繼叔乘之，斬八千級。

translations.literal: Nali was defeated, gathered the scattered and rallied again, and returned to attack the imperial army; Jishu struck them, beheading eight thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Nali rallied the scattered and attacked again; Jishu struck them, beheading eight thousand.

sentences.zh: 那利走，或執以詣軍。

translations.literal: Nali fled and was sometimes captured and brought to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Nali fled and was captured and brought to the army.

sentences.zh: 社爾凡破五大城，男女數萬，遣使者諭降小城七百餘，西域震懼，西突厥、安兩國歸軍餉焉。

translations.literal: She'er in all broke five great cities and tens of thousands of men and women; envoys were sent to persuade more than seven hundred small cities to surrender; the Western Regions trembled in fear, and the Western Turks and An submitted provisions to the army.
translations.idiomatic: She'er captured five great cities and tens of thousands of people; envoys persuaded more than seven hundred small cities to surrender. The Western Regions trembled; the Western Turks and An submitted provisions.

sentences.zh: 社爾立王弟葉護王其國，勒石紀功。

translations.literal: She'er established the king's younger brother Yehu as ruler of the state and inscribed a stone to record the achievement.
translations.idiomatic: She'er established the king's younger brother Yehu as ruler and inscribed a stone to record the victory.

sentences.zh: 書聞，帝喜，見群臣從容曰：「夫樂有幾，朕嘗言之：土城竹馬，童兒樂也；

translations.literal: When the report arrived the emperor was pleased and told the ministers at leisure: "How many kinds of joy are there? I have spoken of them: earthen cities and bamboo horses are the joy of children;
translations.idiomatic: When the report arrived the emperor was pleased and told his ministers: "How many kinds of joy exist? Earthen cities and bamboo horses are the joy of children;

sentences.zh: 飭金翠羅紈，婦人樂也；

translations.literal: adornment in gold, green, silk, and brocade is the joy of women;
translations.idiomatic: adornment in gold, green, silk, and brocade is the joy of women;

sentences.zh: 貿遷有無，商賈樂也；

translations.literal: trading what one has for what one lacks is the joy of merchants;
translations.idiomatic: trading what one has for what one lacks is the joy of merchants;

sentences.zh: 高官厚秩，士大夫樂也；

translations.literal: high office and rich stipends are the joy of scholar-officials;
translations.idiomatic: high office and rich stipends are the joy of scholar-officials;

sentences.zh: 戰無前敵，將帥樂也；

translations.literal: fighting with no enemy ahead is the joy of generals;
translations.idiomatic: fighting with no enemy ahead is the joy of generals;

sentences.zh: 四海寧一，帝王樂也。

translations.literal: when the four seas are pacified and unified, that is the joy of an emperor.
translations.idiomatic: when the four seas are pacified, that is the joy of an emperor.

sentences.zh: 朕今樂矣！」

translations.literal: I am joyful now!
translations.idiomatic: I am joyful now!

sentences.zh: 遂遍觴之。

translations.literal: He then passed cups to all.
translations.idiomatic: He then passed cups to all.

sentences.zh: 初，孝恪之擊焉耆也，龜茲有浮屠善數，嘆曰：「唐家終有西域，不數年吾國亦亡。」

translations.literal: At first, when Xiaoge attacked Yanqi, a Kuchan Buddhist skilled in divination sighed: "The Tang will ultimately hold the Western Regions; within a few years our state too will perish.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaoge attacked Yanqi, a Kuchan Buddhist skilled in divination sighed: "The Tang will hold the Western Regions; within a few years our kingdom too will perish.

sentences.zh: 社爾執訶黎布失畢、那利、羯獵顛獻太廟，帝受俘紫微殿。

translations.literal: She'er presented Heli Bushibi, Nali, and Jieliedian at the Imperial Ancestral Temple; the emperor received the captives at Ziwei Hall.
translations.idiomatic: She'er presented Heli Bushibi, Nali, and Jieliedian at the Imperial Ancestral Temple; the emperor received the captives at Ziwei Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝責謂，君臣皆頓首伏。

translations.literal: The emperor reproached them; ruler and ministers all prostrated themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reproached them; ruler and ministers prostrated themselves.

sentences.zh: 詔赦罪，改館鴻臚寺，拜布失畢左武衛中朗將。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned their crimes, lodged them at the Court of Ceremonies, and appointed Bushibi Left Martial Guard Lieutenant General.
translations.idiomatic: An edict pardoned their crimes, lodged them at the Court of Ceremonies, and appointed Bushibi Left Martial Guard Lieutenant General.

sentences.zh: 始徙安西都護於其都，統於闐、碎葉、疏勒，號「四鎮。」

translations.literal: The Anxi Protectorate was first relocated to their capital, governing Khotan, Suyab, and Kashgar—called the "Four Garrisons."
translations.idiomatic: The Anxi Protectorate was relocated to their capital, governing Khotan, Suyab, and Kashgar—the "Four Garrisons."

sentences.zh: 高宗復封訶黎布失畢為龜茲王，與那利、羯獵顛還國。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong again enfeoffed Heli Bushibi as King of Kucha and returned Nali and Jieliedian to their country.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong again enfeoffed Heli Bushibi as King of Kucha and returned Nali and Jieliedian to their kingdom.

sentences.zh: 久之，王來朝。

translations.literal: After a long time the king came to court.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time the king came to court.

sentences.zh: 那利烝其妻阿史那，王不能禁，左右請殺之，由是更猜忌。

translations.literal: Nali violated his wife Ashina; the king could not restrain him; his attendants requested he be killed, and from this suspicion deepened.
translations.idiomatic: Nali violated the king's wife Ashina; the king could not restrain him. Attendants urged his execution, deepening mutual suspicion.

sentences.zh: 使者言狀，帝並召至京師，囚那利，護遣王還。

translations.literal: Envoys reported the situation; the emperor summoned both to the capital, imprisoned Nali, and escorted the king back.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys reported the situation; the emperor summoned both to the capital, imprisoned Nali, and escorted the king home.

sentences.zh: 羯獵顛拒不內，遣使降賀魯，王不敢進，悒悒死。

translations.literal: Jieliedian refused to admit him and sent envoys to surrender to Helu; the king dared not advance and died in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Jieliedian refused to admit him and sent envoys to surrender to Helu; the king dared not advance and died of grief.

sentences.zh: 詔左屯衛大將軍楊胄發兵禽羯獵顛，窮誅部黨，以其地為龜茲都督府，更立子素稽為王，授右驍衛大將軍，為都督。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Left Encampment Guard General Yang Zhou to dispatch troops, capture Jieliedian, and exterminate his faction; the territory was made the Kucha Military Governorship; his son Suji was newly established as king and appointed Right Piaoqi Guard General and military governor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yang Zhou to capture Jieliedian and exterminate his faction. The territory became the Kucha Military Governorship; his son Suji was established as king and appointed Right Piaoqi Guard General and military governor.

sentences.zh: 是歲，徙安西都護府於其國，以故安西為西州都督府，即拜左驍衛大將軍兼安西都護曲智湛為都督。

translations.literal: That year the Anxi Protectorate was relocated to Kucha; the former Anxi became the Xizhou Military Governorship; Left Piaoqi Guard General and Anxi Protector Qu Zhizhan was appointed military governor.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Anxi Protectorate moved to Kucha; former Anxi became the Xizhou Military Governorship. Qu Zhizhan was appointed military governor.

sentences.zh: 西域平。

translations.literal: The Western Regions were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Regions were pacified.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使者分行諸國風俗物產，詔許敬宗與史官撰《西域圖志》。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched envoys to survey the customs and products of the various states and ordered Xu Jingzong and the historiographers to compile the Record of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched envoys to survey the customs and products of the various states and ordered Xu Jingzong and the historiographers to compile the Record of the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 上元中，素稽獻銀頗羅、名馬，

translations.literal: During the Shangyuan era Suji presented silver poluo and famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shangyuan era Suji presented silver poluo and famous horses.

sentences.zh: 王延田跌來朝。

translations.literal: King Yantian Die came to court.
translations.idiomatic: King Yantian Die came to court.

sentences.zh: 始，儀鳳時，吐蕃攻焉耆以西，四鎮皆沒。

translations.literal: At first, during the Yifeng era, Tibet attacked west of Yanqi and all Four Garrisons fell.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yifeng era, Tibet attacked west of Yanqi and all Four Garrisons fell.

sentences.zh: 長壽元年，武威道總管王孝傑破吐蕃，復四鎮地，置安西都護府於龜茲，以兵三萬鎮守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changshou, Campaign Commander of the Wuwei Circuit Wang Xiaojie defeated Tibet and recovered the Four Garrisons, establishing the Anxi Protectorate at Kucha with thirty thousand troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changshou, Wang Xiaojie defeated Tibet, recovered the Four Garrisons, and established the Anxi Protectorate at Kucha with thirty thousand garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 於是沙磧荒絕，民供貲糧苦甚，議者請棄之，武後不聽。

translations.literal: The desert wastes were desolate and remote; the people suffered greatly supplying provisions; debaters requested abandonment, but Empress Wu refused.
translations.idiomatic: The desert wastes were desolate; the people suffered supplying provisions. Critics urged abandonment, but Empress Wu refused.

sentences.zh: 都護以政勣稱華狄者，田揚名、郭元振、張孝嵩、杜暹雲，

translations.literal: Protectors renowned for governing both Chinese and barbarians included Tian Yangming, Guo Yuanzhen, Zhang Xiaosong, and Du Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Protectors renowned for governing Chinese and barbarians alike included Tian Yangming, Guo Yuanzhen, Zhang Xiaosong, and Du Xian.

sentences.zh: 王白莫死，子多幣立，改名孝節。

translations.literal: King Baimo died and his son Duobi succeeded, changing his name to Xiaojie.
translations.idiomatic: King Baimo died; his son Duobi succeeded, changing his name to Xiaojie.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遣弟孝義來朝。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year his younger brother Xiaoyi came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year his younger brother Xiaoyi came to court.

sentences.zh: 自龜茲贏六百里，窬小沙磧，有跋祿迦，小國也，一曰亟墨，即漢姑墨國，橫六百里，縱三百里。

translations.literal: Six hundred li beyond Kucha's surplus, crossing a small desert, was Baluka, a small state also called Jimo—the Han Kingdom of Gumo—measuring six hundred li across and three hundred li north to south.
translations.idiomatic: Six hundred li beyond Kucha, crossing a small desert, lay Baluka, also called Jimo—the Han Kingdom of Gumo—measuring six hundred by three hundred li.

sentences.zh: 風俗文字與龜茲同，言語少異。

translations.literal: Customs and writing were the same as Kucha's; the language differed slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Customs and writing matched Kucha's; the language differed slightly.

sentences.zh: 出細氈褐。

translations.literal: It produced fine felt and coarse wool.
translations.idiomatic: It produced fine felt and coarse wool.

sentences.zh: 西三百里度石磧至淩山，蔥嶺北原也，水東流，春夏山谷積雪。

translations.literal: Three hundred li west one crossed stony desert to Mount Ling, the northern plain of the Congling Pass, where water flowed eastward and snow accumulated in valleys in spring and summer.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred li west lay stony desert leading to Mount Ling, the northern Congling plain, where water flowed eastward and snow accumulated in the valleys through spring and summer.

sentences.zh: 西北五百里至素葉水城，比國商胡雜居。

translations.literal: Five hundred li northwest was Suyab Water City, where merchants of many states lived mixed together.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred li northwest was Suyab Water City, where merchants of many states lived together.

sentences.zh: 素葉以西數十城，皆立君長，役頟屬突厥。

translations.literal: Several dozen cities west of Suyab each had rulers and chieftains, all subject to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of cities west of Suyab each had rulers subject to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 自素葉水城至羯霜那國，衣氈褐皮氎，以繒繚。

translations.literal: From Suyab Water City to the Kingdom of Jieshuangna, people wore felt, coarse wool, and leather, trimmed with silk.
translations.idiomatic: From Suyab Water City to Jieshuangna, people wore felt, coarse wool, and leather trimmed with silk.

sentences.zh: 素葉城西四百里至千泉，地贏二百里，南雪山，三垂平陸，多泉池，因名之，突厥可汗歲避暑其中。
