translations.literal: Four hundred li west of Suyab was Qianquan, a fertile region two hundred li across with the southern Snow Mountains and level land on three sides, rich in springs and pools, hence the name; the Turk khan summered there each year.
translations.idiomatic: Four hundred li west of Suyab was Qianquan, a fertile two-hundred-li region named for its many springs; the Turk khan summered there annually.

sentences.zh: 群鹿飾鈴镮，可狎也。

translations.literal: Herds of deer wore bell collars and could be approached.
translations.idiomatic: Herds of deer wore bell collars and could be approached freely.

sentences.zh: 西贏百里至呾邏私城，亦比國商胡雜居。

translations.literal: One hundred li west was Tuluosi City, where merchants of many states also lived mixed together.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred li west was Tuluosi City, where merchants of many states also lived together.

sentences.zh: 有小城，三百，本華人，為突厥所掠，群保此，尚華語。

translations.literal: There was a small city of three hundred people, originally Chinese captured by the Turks, who preserved themselves here and still spoke Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: A small city of three hundred people, originally Chinese captured by the Turks, preserved themselves here and still spoke Chinese.

sentences.zh: 西南贏二百里至白水城，原隰膏腴。

translations.literal: Two hundred li southwest was Baishui City, with fertile lowlands.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred li southwest was Baishui City, with fertile lowlands.

sentences.zh: 南五十里有笯赤建國，廣千里，地沃宜稼，多蒲陶。

translations.literal: Fifty li south was the Kingdom of Nuchijian, a thousand li across with rich soil suited to crops and many grapes.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty li south was Nuchijian, a thousand li across with rich soil and many grapes.

sentences.zh: 又二百里即石國。

translations.literal: Two hundred li farther was the Kingdom of Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred li farther was the Kingdom of Shi.

sentences.zh: 疏勒疏勒，一曰佉沙，環五千里，距京師九千里而贏。

translations.literal: Kashgar. Kashgar, also called Qiasha, encompassed five thousand li, nine thousand li from the capital with surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Kashgar. Also called Qiasha, it encompassed five thousand li, some nine thousand li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 多沙磧，少壤土。

translations.literal: There was much desert sand and little arable soil.
translations.idiomatic: Desert sand predominated; arable soil was scarce.

sentences.zh: 俗尚詭詐，生子亦夾頭取褊，其人文身碧瞳。

translations.literal: By custom they valued deceit; at birth they also compressed the head to flatten it; their people tattooed their bodies and had green eyes.
translations.idiomatic: They valued deceit by custom; at birth they compressed the head to flatten it. Their people tattooed their bodies and had green eyes.

sentences.zh: 王姓裴氏，自號「阿摩支」，居迦師城，突厥以女妻之。

translations.literal: The king bore the surname Pei, styled himself "Amozhi," dwelt in Jiashi City, and the Turks gave him a woman in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The king bore the surname Pei, styled himself Amozhi, dwelt in Jiashi City, and the Turks gave him a wife.

sentences.zh: 勝兵二千人。

translations.literal: Effective fighting forces numbered two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: It could field two thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 俗祠祅神。

translations.literal: By custom they worshipped the Zoroastrian god.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they worshipped the Zoroastrian god.

sentences.zh: 貞觀九年，遣使者獻名馬，又四年，與朱俱波、甘棠貢方物。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenguan envoys presented famous horses; four years later they presented local products together with Zhujubo and Gantang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhenguan envoys presented famous horses; four years later they presented local products with Zhujubo and Gantang.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂房玄齡等曰：「曩之一天下，克勝四夷，惟秦皇、漢武耳。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong told Fang Xuanling and others: "In unifying the empire and conquering the four barbarians, only Emperor Qin and Emperor Han compare.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong told Fang Xuanling and others: "In unifying the empire and conquering the four quarters, only the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han compare.

sentences.zh: 朕提三尺劍定四海，遠夷率服，不減二君者。

translations.literal: I drew a three-foot sword and pacified the four seas; distant barbarians all submitted—no less than those two rulers.
translations.idiomatic: I drew a three-foot sword and pacified the four seas; distant peoples submitted—no less than those two emperors.

sentences.zh: 然彼末路不自保，公等宜相輔弼，毋進諛言，置朕於危亡也。」

translations.literal: Yet they could not preserve themselves at the end; you should assist and support me—do not offer flattery and place me in danger and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they could not preserve themselves in the end. Assist me faithfully—do not flatter me into danger and ruin.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳時，吐蕃破其國。

translations.literal: During the Yifeng era Tibet destroyed their state.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yifeng era Tibet destroyed their kingdom.

sentences.zh: 開元十六年，始遣大理正喬夢松攝鴻臚少卿，冊其君安定為疏勒王。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan, Grand Justice Qiao Mengsong was first dispatched as acting Director of Ceremonies to invest their lord Anding as King of Kashgar.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan, Grand Justice Qiao Mengsong was dispatched to invest Lord Anding as King of Kashgar.

sentences.zh: 天寶十二載，首領裴國良來朝，授折沖都尉，賜紫袍、金魚。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Tianbao chieftain Pei Guoliang came to court and was appointed Irregular Cavalry Commander, granted a purple robe and golden fish insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Tianbao chieftain Pei Guoliang came to court, was appointed Irregular Cavalry Commander, and granted a purple robe and golden fish insignia.

sentences.zh: 朱俱波亦名朱俱槃，漢子合國也。

translations.literal: Zhujubo was also called Zhujupan—the Han Kingdom of Zihe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhujubo. Also called Zhujupan, this was the Han Kingdom of Zihe.

sentences.zh: 並有西夜、蒲犁、依耐、得若四種地，直於闐西千里，蔥嶺北三百里，西距喝盤陀，北九百里屬疏勒，南三千里女國也。

translations.literal: Together with Xiye, Puli, Yinai, and Deruo it had four kinds of territory, a thousand li directly west of Khotan, three hundred li north of the Congling Pass, four hundred li west to Hepantuo, nine hundred li north belonging to Kashgar, and three thousand li south to the Women Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Xiye, Puli, Yinai, and Deruo it held four territories: a thousand li west of Khotan, three hundred li north of the Congling Pass, four hundred li west to Hepantuo, nine hundred li north to Kashgar, and three thousand li south to the Women Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 勝兵二千人。

translations.literal: Effective fighting forces numbered two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: It could field two thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 尚浮屠法，文字同婆羅門。

translations.literal: They honored the Buddhist law; their writing was the same as Brahmin script.
translations.idiomatic: They honored Buddhism; their writing matched Brahmin script.

sentences.zh: 甘棠甘棠，在海南，昆侖人也。

translations.literal: Gantang. Gantang lay south of the sea; its people were Kunlun.
translations.idiomatic: Gantang lay south of the sea; its people were Kunlun.

sentences.zh: 喝盤陀喝盤陀，或曰漢陀，曰渴館檀，亦謂渴羅陀，由疏勒西南入劍末谷、不忍領六百里，其國也。

translations.literal: Hepantuo, also called Handuo or Kehandan, also called Keluoduo, reached its country by entering the Jianmo Valley southwest from Kashgar and crossing Burnin Ridge for six hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Hepantuo, also called Handuo, Kehandan, or Keluoduo, was reached by entering the Jianmo Valley southwest from Kashgar and crossing Burnin Ridge for six hundred li.

sentences.zh: 距瓜州四千五百里，直朱俱波西，南距懸度山，北抵疏勒，西護密，西北判汗國也。

translations.literal: It lay four thousand five hundred li from Guazhou, directly west of Zhujubo, south of the Suspended Crossing Mountains, north to Kashgar, west to Wumi, and northwest to the Pihan Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: It lay four thousand five hundred li from Guazhou, west of Zhujubo, south of the Suspended Crossing Mountains, north to Kashgar, west to Wumi, and northwest to Pihan.

sentences.zh: 治蔥嶺中，都城負徙多河。

translations.literal: It was governed amid the Congling Pass; the capital leaned on the Tuoduo River.
translations.idiomatic: It was governed amid the Congling Pass; the capital stood on the Tuoduo River.

sentences.zh: 勝兵千人。

translations.literal: Effective fighting forces numbered a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: It could field a thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 其王本疏勒人，世相承為之。

translations.literal: Their king was originally a Kashgar man, succeeding generation after generation.
translations.idiomatic: Their king was originally from Kashgar, succeeding generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 西南即頭痛山也。

translations.literal: To the southwest was Mount Toutong.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest lay Mount Toutong.

sentences.zh: 蔥嶺俗號極嶷山，環其國。

translations.literal: The Congling Pass was popularly called Mount Jiyi, encircling their state.
translations.idiomatic: The Congling Pass, popularly called Mount Jiyi, encircled their kingdom.

sentences.zh: 人勁悍，貌、言如於闐。

translations.literal: The people were fierce and strong; their appearance and speech resembled those of Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: The people were fierce; their appearance and speech resembled those of Khotan.

sentences.zh: 其法，殺人剽劫者死，餘得贖。

translations.literal: By their law, murderers and robbers were put to death; other crimes could be redeemed.
translations.idiomatic: By their law murderers and robbers were executed; other crimes could be redeemed.

sentences.zh: 賦必輸服飾，王坐人床。

translations.literal: Tribute had to be paid in garments; the king sat on a human bed.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute was paid in garments; the king sat on a human bed.

sentences.zh: 後魏太延中，始通中國。

translations.literal: In the Taiyan era of Later Wei they first communicated with China.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiyan era of Later Wei they first communicated with China.

sentences.zh: 貞觀九年，遣使者來朝。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenguan they sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhenguan they sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 開元中破平其國，置蔥嶺守捉，安西極邊戍也。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era their state was conquered and pacified; the Congling Garrison was established as the extreme frontier post of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era their kingdom was conquered and the Congling Garrison established as Anxi's extreme frontier post.

sentences.zh: 於闐於闐，或曰瞿薩旦那，亦曰渙那，曰屈丹，北狄曰於遁，諸胡曰豁旦。

translations.literal: Khotan. Khotan, also called Qusadanna, also called Huanna, Quzhan, Yudun among the northern barbarians, and Huodan among the various Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Khotan. Also called Qusadanna, Huanna, Quzhan, Yudun among northern peoples, and Huodan among the Hu.

sentences.zh: 距京師九千七百里，瓜州贏四千里，並有漢戎廬、桿彌、渠勒、皮山五國故地。

translations.literal: It lay nine thousand seven hundred li from the capital, four thousand li beyond Guazhou, and included the former territories of the five Han states of Hanronglu, Ganmi, Qule, and Pishan.
translations.idiomatic: It lay nine thousand seven hundred li from the capital, four thousand li beyond Guazhou, encompassing the former Han territories of Hanronglu, Ganmi, Qule, and Pishan.

sentences.zh: 其居曰西山城，勝兵四千人。

translations.literal: Their capital was called Xishan City; effective fighting forces numbered four thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Their capital was Xishan City; they could field four thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 有玉河，國人夜視月光盛處必得美玉。

translations.literal: There was a Jade River; the people watched where moonlight was brightest at night and always found fine jade there.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Jade River; by night the people watched where moonlight shone brightest and always found fine jade.

sentences.zh: 王居繪室。

translations.literal: The king dwelt in a painted hall.
translations.idiomatic: The king dwelt in a painted hall.

sentences.zh: 俗機巧，言迂大，喜事祅神、浮屠法，然貌恭謹，相見皆跪。

translations.literal: By custom they were skilled and clever, spoke in grand circumlocutions, honored the Zoroastrian god and the Buddhist law, yet their appearance was respectful and cautious; when meeting they all knelt.
translations.idiomatic: They were skilled and clever by custom, spoke grandly, honored Zoroastrian and Buddhist faiths, yet appeared respectful; all knelt when meeting.

sentences.zh: 以木為筆，玉為印，凡得問遺書，戴於首乃發之。

translations.literal: They used wood for pens and jade for seals; whenever they received a letter of inquiry or gift, they placed it on their heads before opening it.
translations.idiomatic: They used wood for pens and jade for seals; letters of inquiry or gift were placed on the head before opening.

sentences.zh: 自漢武帝以來，中國詔書符節，其王傳以相授。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Wu of Han, Chinese edicts, credentials, and tokens had been transmitted from king to king.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Wu of Han, Chinese edicts and credentials had passed from king to king.

sentences.zh: 人喜歌舞，工紡勣。

translations.literal: The people loved song and dance and were skilled at weaving.
translations.idiomatic: The people loved song and dance and were skilled weavers.

sentences.zh: 西有沙磧，鼠大如猬，色類金，出入群鼠為從。

translations.literal: To the west was desert sand; rats large as hedgehogs, colored like gold, moved in groups with attendant rats.
translations.idiomatic: To the west lay desert sands where rats large as hedgehogs, colored like gold, moved in attendant groups.

sentences.zh: 初無桑蠶，丐鄰國，不肯出，其王即求婚，許之。

translations.literal: At first they had no mulberry or silkworms; they begged from a neighboring state, which refused; their king then sought marriage and was granted it.
translations.idiomatic: At first they had no mulberry or silkworms; a neighbor refused their request, so their king sought marriage and was granted it.

sentences.zh: 將迎，乃告曰：「國無帛，可持蠶自為衣。」

translations.literal: When she was to be escorted home, he said: "Our state has no silk; you may bring silkworms and raise them for clothing yourself.
translations.idiomatic: When she was escorted home, he said: "Our state has no silk; bring silkworms and raise them for clothing.

sentences.zh: 女聞，置蠶帽絮中，關守不敢驗，自是始有蠶。

translations.literal: The woman heard this, placed silkworms in cotton in her hat, and the border guards dared not inspect; from this silkworms first came to the state.
translations.idiomatic: She placed silkworms in cotton in her hat; border guards dared not inspect, and silkworms first entered the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 女刻石約無殺蠶，蛾飛盡得治繭。

translations.literal: The woman carved a stone covenant forbidding the killing of silkworms; when moths flew away the cocoons could be processed.
translations.idiomatic: She carved a stone covenant forbidding silkworm killing; when moths flew away the cocoons could be processed.

sentences.zh: 王姓尉遲氏，名屋密，本臣突厥，，遣使者入獻。

translations.literal: The king bore the surname Yuchi, named Wumi; he originally served the Turks and sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: King Yuchi Wumi originally served the Turks and sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 後三年，遣子入侍。

translations.literal: Three years later he sent his son to serve at court.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he sent his son to serve at court.

sentences.zh: 阿史那社爾之平龜茲也，其王伏阇信大懼，使子獻橐它三百。

translations.literal: When Ashina She'er pacified Kucha, King Fuxinxin was greatly terrified and sent his son presenting three hundred camels.
translations.idiomatic: When Ashina She'er pacified Kucha, King Fuxinxin was terrified and sent his son with three hundred camels.

sentences.zh: 長史薛萬備謂社爾曰：「公破龜茲，西域皆震恐，願假輕騎羈於闐王獻京師。」

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Xue Wanbei told She'er: "You have broken Kucha and all the Western Regions tremble in fear; I wish to borrow light cavalry to bring the Khotan king to the capital as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Wanbei told She'er: "You have broken Kucha and the Western Regions tremble; lend me light cavalry to bring the Khotan king to court.

sentences.zh: 社爾許之。

translations.literal: She'er granted it.
translations.idiomatic: She'er granted it.

sentences.zh: 至於闐，陳唐威靈，勸入見天子，伏阇信乃隨使者來。

translations.literal: Arriving at Khotan, he displayed Tang might and urged audience with the Son of Heaven; Fuxinxin then followed the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: At Khotan he displayed Tang might and urged audience with the emperor; Fuxinxin followed the envoy.

sentences.zh: 會高宗立，授右衛大將軍，子葉護玷為右驍衛將軍，賜袍帶，布帛六千段，第一區，留數月遣之，請以子弟宿衛。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, he was appointed Right Guard Grand General; his son Yehu Dian was made Right Piaoqi Guard General; robes, belts, and six thousand bolts of silk and cloth were bestowed along with a first-class district; after several months he was sent home and requested that his sons and younger brothers remain as guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong ascended, Fuxinxin was appointed Right Guard Grand General; his son Yehu Dian was made Right Piaoqi Guard General and granted robes, belts, and six thousand bolts of silk. After several months he was sent home, requesting sons and brothers remain as guards.

sentences.zh: 上元初，身率子弟酋領七十人來朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shangyuan he personally led seventy sons, younger brothers, and chieftains to court.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shangyuan he led seventy sons, brothers, and chieftains to court.

sentences.zh: 擊吐蕃有功，帝以其地為毗沙都督府，析十州，授伏阇雄都督。

translations.literal: For fighting Tibet he was rewarded; the emperor made his territory the Bisha Military Governorship, dividing ten prefectures and appointing Fuxiong military governor.
translations.idiomatic: For fighting Tibet he was rewarded; his territory became the Bisha Military Governorship of ten prefectures, with Fuxiong as military governor.

sentences.zh: 死，武後立其子敬。

translations.literal: When he died Empress Wu established his son Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When he died Empress Wu established his son Jing.

sentences.zh: 開元時獻馬、駝、豽。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era they presented horses, camels, and leopards.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era they presented horses, camels, and leopards.

sentences.zh: 敬死，復立尉遲伏師戰為王。

translations.literal: When Jing died they again established Yuchi Fushizhan as king.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing died Yuchi Fushizhan was again established as king.

sentences.zh: 死，伏阇達嗣，並冊其妻執失為妃。

translations.literal: When he died Fuxinda succeeded; his wife Zhishi was also enfeoffed as consort.
translations.idiomatic: When he died Fuxinda succeeded; his wife Zhishi was enfeoffed as consort.

sentences.zh: 死，尉遲圭嗣，妻馬為妃。

translations.literal: When he died Yuchi Gui succeeded; his wife Ma was enfeoffed as consort.
translations.idiomatic: When he died Yuchi Gui succeeded; his wife Ma was enfeoffed as consort.

sentences.zh: 圭死，子勝立。

translations.literal: When Gui died his son Sheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui died his son Sheng succeeded.

sentences.zh: 至德初，以兵赴難，因請留宿衛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide he came with troops to aid the court in crisis and requested to remain as palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhide he came with troops to aid the court and requested to remain as palace guard.

sentences.zh: 乾元三年，以其弟左監門衛率葉護曜為大仆員外卿、同四鎮節度副使，權知本國事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianyuan his younger brother Left Gate Guard Rate Yehu Yao was made External Director of the Palace Stud and deputy military governor of the Four Garrisons with provisional authority over state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qianyuan his brother Yehu Yao was made External Director of the Palace Stud and deputy military governor of the Four Garrisons with provisional authority over state affairs.

sentences.zh: 勝自有傳。

translations.literal: Sheng has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 於闐東三百里有建德力河，七百里有精絕國；

translations.literal: Three hundred li east of Khotan was the Jiandele River; seven hundred li farther was the Kingdom of Jingjue.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred li east of Khotan was the Jiandele River; seven hundred li farther was Jingjue.

sentences.zh: 河之東有汗彌，居達德力城，亦曰拘彌城，即寧彌故城。

translations.literal: East of the river was Hanmi, dwelling at Dadeli City, also called Jumi City—the former city of Ningmi.
translations.idiomatic: East of the river was Hanmi at Dadeli City, also called Jumi City—the former Ningmi.

sentences.zh: 皆小國也。

translations.literal: All were small states.
translations.idiomatic: All were small states.

sentences.zh: 初，德宗即位，遣內給事朱如玉之安西，求玉於於闐，得圭一，珂佩五，枕一，帶胯三百，簪四十，奩三十，釧十，杵三，瑟瑟百斤，並它寶等。

translations.literal: At first, when Emperor Dezong ascended the throne, he dispatched Inner Attendant Zhu Ruyu to Anxi to seek jade from Khotan, obtaining one gui, five ke pendants, one pillow, three hundred belt plaques, forty hairpins, thirty cosmetic cases, ten bracelets, three pestles, a hundred jin of sese, and other treasures.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong ascended, Inner Attendant Zhu Ruyu was dispatched to Anxi to seek jade from Khotan, obtaining one gui, five ke pendants, one pillow, three hundred belt plaques, and other treasures.

sentences.zh: 及還，詐言假道回紇為所奪。

translations.literal: On returning he falsely claimed the Uyghurs seized them while he passed through their territory.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he falsely claimed the Uyghurs seized them en route.

sentences.zh: 久之事泄，得所市，流死恩州。

translations.literal: After a long time the matter was exposed; the purchased goods were recovered and he was exiled to En Prefecture to die.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was eventually exposed; the goods were recovered and he was exiled to En Prefecture to die.

sentences.zh: 天竺國，漢身毒國也，或曰摩伽陀，曰婆羅門。

translations.literal: India was the Han Kingdom of Shendu, also called Magadha or Brahmana.
translations.idiomatic: India. The Han Kingdom of Shendu, also called Magadha or Brahmana.

sentences.zh: 去京師九千六百里，都護治所二千八百里。

translations.literal: It lay nine thousand six hundred li from the capital, two thousand eight hundred li from the protectorate seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay nine thousand six hundred li from the capital, two thousand eight hundred li from the protectorate seat.

sentences.zh: 居葱嶺南，幅圓三萬里，分東、西、南、北、中五天竺，皆城邑數百。

translations.literal: It lay south of the Congling Pass, three thousand li in circumference, divided into East, West, South, North, and Central India, each with several hundred walled cities.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Congling Pass, it spanned three thousand li, divided into East, West, South, North, and Central India, each with hundreds of walled cities.

sentences.zh: 南天竺瀕海，出師子、豹、𤟤、橐它、犀、象、火齊、琅玕、石蜜、黑鹽。

translations.literal: South India bordered the sea, producing lions, leopards, rhinoceroses, camels, rhinoceros horn, elephants, fire crystal, carnelian, rock sugar, and black salt.
translations.idiomatic: South India bordered the sea, producing lions, leopards, rhinoceroses, camels, ivory, elephants, fire crystal, carnelian, rock sugar, and black salt.

sentences.zh: 北天竺距雪山，圜抱如璧，南有谷，通為國門。

translations.literal: North India faced the Snow Mountains, encircled round like a jade disk; to the south was a valley serving as the national gate.
translations.idiomatic: North India faced the Snow Mountains, encircled like a jade disk; a southern valley served as the national gate.

sentences.zh: 東天竺際海，與扶南、林邑接。

translations.literal: East India bordered the sea and connected with Funan and Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: East India bordered the sea and connected with Funan and Linyi.

sentences.zh: 西天竺與罽賓、波斯接。

translations.literal: West India connected with Jibin and Persia.
translations.idiomatic: West India connected with Jibin and Persia.

sentences.zh: 中天竺在四天竺之會，都城曰茶镈和羅城，濱迦毗黎河。

translations.literal: Central India lay at the confluence of the four Indias; the capital was called Chaboluoluo City on the Kapila River.
translations.idiomatic: Central India lay at the confluence of the four Indias; the capital was Chaboluoluo City on the Kapila River.

sentences.zh: 有別城數百，皆置長；

translations.literal: There were several hundred separate cities, each with a chief;
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred separate cities each had a chief;

sentences.zh: 別國數十，置王。

translations.literal: several dozen separate states each had a king.
translations.idiomatic: several dozen separate states each had a king.

sentences.zh: 曰舍衛；

translations.literal: One was called Shewei;
translations.idiomatic: One was Shewei;

sentences.zh: 曰迦沒路，開戶皆東嚮；

translations.literal: one was called Kamolu, its gates all facing east;
translations.idiomatic: one was Kamolu, its gates all facing east;

sentences.zh: 曰迦尸，或曰波羅奈，亦曰波羅那斯。

translations.literal: one was called Kashi, also called Varanasi, also called Varanasi.
translations.idiomatic: one was Kashi, also called Varanasi.

sentences.zh: 其畜有稍割牛，黑色，角細，長四尺許，十日一割，不然困且死。

translations.literal: Their livestock included slightly cut cattle, black in color with fine horns four chi long; they were cut every ten days, otherwise they grew distressed and died.
translations.idiomatic: Their livestock included slightly cut cattle—black with fine horns four chi long, cut every ten days lest they sicken and die.

sentences.zh: 人飲其血，或曰壽五百歲，牛壽如之。

translations.literal: People drank their blood; some said they lived five hundred years, and the cattle lived as long.
translations.idiomatic: People drank their blood; some said they lived five hundred years, as did the cattle.

sentences.zh: 中天竺王姓乞利咥氏，亦曰刹利，世有其國，不篡殺。

translations.literal: The king of Central India bore the surname Qilizhi, also called Kshatriya; his family had held the state for generations without usurpation or murder.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Central India bore the surname Qilizhi, also called Kshatriya; his line had ruled for generations without usurpation or murder.

sentences.zh: 土溽熱，稻歲四熟。

translations.literal: The soil was humid and hot; rice ripened four times a year.
translations.idiomatic: The soil was humid and hot; rice ripened four times a year.

sentences.zh: 禾之長者沒橐它。

translations.literal: The tallest grain stalks were hidden by camels.
translations.idiomatic: The tallest grain stalks were hidden by camels.

sentences.zh: 以貝齒為貨。

translations.literal: Shell currency served as money.
translations.idiomatic: Shell currency served as money.

sentences.zh: 有金剛、旃檀、鬱金，與大秦、扶南、交趾相貿易。

translations.literal: There were diamonds, sandalwood, and turmeric, traded with Daqin, Funan, and Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Diamonds, sandalwood, and turmeric were traded with Daqin, Funan, and Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 人富樂，無簿籍，耕王地者乃輸稅。

translations.literal: The people were rich and content; there were no registers; only those who cultivated royal land paid taxes.
translations.idiomatic: The people were rich and content; there were no registers; only royal land cultivators paid taxes.

sentences.zh: 以舐足摩踵為致禮。

translations.literal: Licking the feet and rubbing the heels was the form of respectful greeting.
translations.idiomatic: Licking the feet and rubbing the heels was the form of respectful greeting.

sentences.zh: 家有奇樂倡伎。

translations.literal: Every household had exotic music and performers.
translations.idiomatic: Every household had exotic music and performers.

sentences.zh: 王大臣皆服錦罽，為螺髻於頂，餘發翦使卷。

translations.literal: Kings and ministers all wore brocade rugs; they wore spiral topknots on the crown and cut the remaining hair to curl.
translations.idiomatic: Kings and ministers wore brocade rugs, spiral topknots on the crown, and curled the remaining hair.

sentences.zh: 男子穿耳垂璫，或懸金，耳緩者為上類；

translations.literal: Men pierced their ears and wore ear pendants or suspended gold; loose-hanging ears marked the upper class;
translations.idiomatic: Men pierced their ears with pendants or suspended gold; loose-hanging ears marked the upper class;

sentences.zh: 徒跣，衣重白。

translations.literal: they went barefoot and wore heavy white garments.
translations.idiomatic: they went barefoot in heavy white garments.

sentences.zh: 婦人項飾金、銀、珠纓絡，死者燔骸取灰，建窣堵，或委野中及河，餌鳥獸魚鼈，無喪紀。

translations.literal: Women adorned their necks with gold, silver, and pearl tassels; the dead were cremated and the ashes collected to build stupas, or the body was cast into the wild or into rivers to feed birds, beasts, fish, and turtles; there was no mourning ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Women adorned their necks with gold, silver, and pearl tassels. The dead were cremated and ashes collected for stupas, or bodies cast to wilds or rivers to feed birds and fish; there was no mourning ritual.

sentences.zh: 謀反者幽殺之；

translations.literal: Rebels were secretly executed;
translations.idiomatic: Rebels were secretly executed;

sentences.zh: 小罪贖錢；

translations.literal: minor crimes were redeemed with money;
translations.idiomatic: minor crimes were redeemed with money;

sentences.zh: 不孝者斷手足，劓耳鼻，徙于邊。

translations.literal: the unfilial had hands and feet cut off, nose and ears sliced, and were exiled to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: the unfilial had limbs severed, nose and ears cut, and were exiled to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 有文字，善步曆，學《悉曇章》，妄曰梵天法。

translations.literal: They had writing and were skilled in calendrical calculation, studying the Siddham script, falsely calling it the law of Brahma.
translations.idiomatic: They had writing and calendrical skill, studying Siddham script, falsely calling it Brahma's law.

sentences.zh: 書貝多葉以記事。

translations.literal: They recorded affairs on pattra leaves.
translations.idiomatic: They recorded affairs on pattra leaves.

sentences.zh: 尚浮圖法，不殺生飲酒，國中處處指曰佛故跡也。

translations.literal: They honored the Buddhist law, did not kill or drink wine, and throughout the state every place was pointed out as a trace of the Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: They honored Buddhism, abstained from killing and wine, and every place was pointed out as a trace of the Buddha.

sentences.zh: 信盟誓，傳禁呪，能致龍起雲雨。

translations.literal: They trusted oaths and transmitted forbidden incantations, able to summon dragons and raise clouds and rain.
translations.idiomatic: They trusted oaths and transmitted forbidden incantations, able to summon dragons and rain.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝時，遣裴矩通西域諸國，獨天竺、拂菻不至為恨。

translations.literal: During Emperor Yang of Sui, Pei Ju opened communication with the Western Regions states; only India and Fulin did not come—a regret.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Yang, Pei Ju opened the Western Regions; only India and Fulin did not come—a regret.

sentences.zh: 武德中，國大亂，王尸羅逸多勒兵戰無前，象不弛鞍，士不釋甲，因討四天竺，皆北面臣之。

translations.literal: During Wude the state fell into great turmoil; King Shiluoyiduo led troops invincible in battle, elephants never unharnessed, soldiers never doffing armor; he thereupon campaigned against the four Indias and all submitted facing north.
translations.idiomatic: During Wude the kingdom fell into turmoil. King Shiluoyiduo led invincible troops, elephants never unharnessed, soldiers never doffing armor, and subdued all four Indias.

sentences.zh: 會唐浮屠玄奘至其國，尸羅逸多召見曰：「而國有聖人出，作《秦王破陣樂》，試為我言其為人。」

translations.literal: When the Tang monk Xuanzang reached the state, Shiluoyiduo summoned him and said: "Your state has produced a sage who composed the 'Prince of Qin's Breaking the Battle Array'—try to tell me what kind of man he is.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzang arrived, Shiluoyiduo summoned him: "Your state has produced a sage who composed the 'Prince of Qin's Breaking the Battle Array'—tell me what kind of man he is.

sentences.zh: 玄奘粗言太宗神武，平禍亂，四夷賓服狀。

translations.literal: Xuanzang roughly described Emperor Taizong's martial spirit, pacifying calamity and disorder, and the submission of the four barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzang described Taizong's martial spirit, pacifying disorder and winning the submission of the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 王喜，曰：「我當東面朝之。」，

translations.literal: The king was pleased and said: "I shall face east and pay him homage.
translations.idiomatic: The king was pleased: "I shall face east and pay him homage.

sentences.zh: 自稱摩伽陀王，遣使者上書。

translations.literal: He styled himself King of Magadha and sent envoys with a letter.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself King of Magadha and sent envoys with a letter.

sentences.zh: 帝命雲騎尉梁懷璥持節尉撫，尸羅逸多驚問國人：「自古亦有摩訶震旦使者至吾國乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Cloud Cavalry Commandant Liang Huaijin to go with credentials to console and reassure him; Shiluoyiduo asked his countrymen in astonishment: "From antiquity has a Great Mahachina envoy ever reached our state?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Liang Huaijin to console him. Shiluoyiduo asked in astonishment: "From antiquity has a Great Mahachina envoy ever reached our kingdom?

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「無有。」

translations.literal: All said: "Never."
translations.idiomatic: All said: "Never."

sentences.zh: 戎言中國為摩訶震旦。

translations.literal: Among the barbarians China was called Great Mahachina.
translations.idiomatic: Among the barbarians China was called Great Mahachina.

sentences.zh: 乃出迎，膜拜受詔書，戴之頂，復遣使者隨入朝。

translations.literal: He then went out to welcome them, prostrated himself in worship and received the edict, placed it on his head, and again sent envoys to follow to court.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to welcome them, prostrated and received the edict, placed it on his head, and sent envoys to follow to court.

sentences.zh: 詔衛尉丞李義表報之，大臣郊迎，傾都邑縱觀，道上焚香，尸羅逸多率羣臣東面受詔書，復獻火珠、鬱金、菩提樹。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Guard of the Right Rate Office Chief Administrator Li Yibiao to respond; ministers greeted them in the suburbs; the whole city turned out to watch; incense was burned along the road; Shiluoyiduo led his ministers eastward to receive the edict and again presented fire pearls, turmeric, and bodhi trees.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yibiao was ordered to respond; ministers greeted them in the suburbs and the city turned out to watch. Shiluoyiduo led ministers eastward to receive the edict and presented fire pearls, turmeric, and bodhi trees.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，遣右衛率府長史王玄策使其國，以蔣師仁為副；

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Wang Xuance of the Right Guard Rate Office was dispatched to their state with Jiang Shiren as deputy;
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Wang Xuance was dispatched with Jiang Shiren as deputy;

sentences.zh: 未至，尸羅逸多死，國人亂，其臣那伏帝阿羅那順自立，發兵拒玄策。

translations.literal: before they arrived Shiluoyiduo died, the state fell into turmoil, and his minister Nafudi Arunashun made himself ruler and dispatched troops to resist Xuance.
translations.idiomatic: before arrival Shiluoyiduo died, the kingdom fell into turmoil, and minister Nafudi Arunashun made himself ruler and resisted Xuance.

sentences.zh: 時從騎纔數十，戰不勝，皆沒，遂剽諸國貢物。

translations.literal: At the time the escort numbered only several dozen; they fought without victory and all perished; he then plundered tribute goods of the various states.
translations.idiomatic: The escort numbered only dozens; defeated, all perished; Arunashun plundered tribute goods of various states.

sentences.zh: 玄策挺身奔吐蕃西鄙，檄召鄰國兵。

translations.literal: Xuance fled alone to the Tibetan western frontier and summoned neighboring states' troops by proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: Xuance fled to the Tibetan western frontier and summoned neighboring troops by proclamation.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃以兵千人來，泥婆羅以七千騎來，玄策部分進戰茶鏄和羅城，三日破之，斬首三千級，溺水死萬人。

translations.literal: Tibet came with a thousand troops and Nepal with seven thousand horsemen; Xuance divided forces and advanced to fight at Chazhan Heluo City, breaking it in three days with three thousand heads taken and ten thousand drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet sent a thousand troops and Nepal seven thousand horsemen. Xuance attacked Chazhan Heluo City, breaking it in three days—three thousand heads, ten thousand drowned.

sentences.zh: 阿羅那順委國走，合散兵復陣，師仁禽之，俘斬千計。

translations.literal: Arunashun abandoned the state and fled, gathered scattered troops and re-formed battle lines; Shiren captured him, with captures and killings numbering a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Arunashun fled, rallied scattered troops, and re-formed lines; Shiren captured him, with captures and killings by the thousand.

sentences.zh: 餘衆奉王妻息阻乾陀衛江，師仁擊之，大潰，獲其妃、王子，虜男女萬二千人，雜畜三萬，降城邑五百八十所。

translations.literal: The remaining forces, supporting the queen and crown prince, blocked the Gandaki River; Shiren attacked and routed them utterly, capturing the consort and princes, taking twelve thousand men and women and thirty thousand mixed livestock, and reducing five hundred eighty cities.
translations.idiomatic: Remaining forces supporting the queen and crown prince blocked the Gandaki River; Shiren routed them, capturing consort and princes, twelve thousand people, thirty thousand livestock, and five hundred eighty cities.

sentences.zh: 東天竺王尸鳩摩送牛馬三萬餽軍，及弓、刀、寶纓絡。

translations.literal: The king of East India Shijiumo sent thirty thousand cattle and horses to supply the army, along with bows, blades, and precious tassels.
translations.idiomatic: The king of East India Shijiumo sent thirty thousand cattle and horses to supply the army, along with bows, blades, and precious tassels.

sentences.zh: 迦沒路國獻異物，并上地圖，請老子象。

translations.literal: The Kingdom of Kamolu presented exotic objects and a map, requesting an image of Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: The Kingdom of Kamolu presented exotic objects and a map, requesting an image of Laozi.

sentences.zh: 玄策執阿羅那順獻闕下。

translations.literal: Xuance presented Arunashun at the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Xuance presented Arunashun at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 有司告宗廟，帝曰：「夫人耳目玩聲色，口鼻耽臭味，此敗德之原也。

translations.literal: The relevant office reported to the ancestral temple. The emperor said: "Men's ears and eyes delight in sound and color, mouths and noses indulge in flavors and odors—this is the root of ruined virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office reported to the ancestral temple. The emperor said: "Men's ears and eyes delight in sound and color, mouths and noses indulge in flavors and odors—this is the root of ruined virtue.

sentences.zh: 婆羅門不劫吾使者，寧至俘虜邪？」

translations.literal: Had the Brahmins not robbed our envoys, would they have become captives?
translations.idiomatic: Had the Brahmins not robbed our envoys, would they have become captives?

sentences.zh: 擢玄策朝散大夫。

translations.literal: Xuance was promoted to Gentleman for Promoting Morality.
translations.idiomatic: Xuance was promoted to Gentleman for Promoting Morality.

sentences.zh: 得方士那邏邇娑婆寐，自言壽二百歲，有不死術，帝改館使治丹，命兵部尚書崔敦禮護視。

translations.literal: A Daoist named Naluo'er Sapomi was obtained, who claimed to be two hundred years old and possessed an art of immortality. The emperor lodged him to prepare elixirs and ordered Minister of War Cui Dunli to oversee him.
translations.idiomatic: A Daoist named Naluo'er Sapomi was obtained, who claimed to be two hundred years old and possessed an art of immortality. The emperor lodged him to prepare elixirs and ordered Minister of War Cui Dunli to oversee him.

sentences.zh: 使者馳天下，采怪藥異石，又使者走婆羅門諸國。

translations.literal: Envoys were dispatched throughout the empire to gather strange drugs and exotic stones, and other envoys were sent to the Brahman states.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were dispatched throughout the empire to gather strange drugs and exotic stones, and other envoys were sent to the Brahman states.

sentences.zh: 所謂畔茶法水者，出石臼中，有石象人守之，水有七種色，或熱或冷，能銷草木金鐵，人手入輒爛，以橐它髑髏轉注瓠中。

translations.literal: The so-called Pantea method water came from a stone mortar, guarded by a stone image of a man. The water had seven colors, sometimes hot or cold, and could dissolve plants, metal, and iron. If a hand entered it, it rotted; it was transferred into gourds using camel skulls.
translations.idiomatic: The so-called Pantea method water came from a stone mortar, guarded by a stone image of a man. The water had seven colors, sometimes hot or cold, and could dissolve plants, metal, and iron. If a hand entered it, it rotted; it was transferred into gourds using camel skulls.

sentences.zh: 有樹名咀賴羅，葉如梨，生窮山崖腹，前有巨虺守穴，不可到。

translations.literal: There was a tree called Julailuo, its leaves like pears, growing in the belly of steep mountain cliffs, with a great serpent guarding the cave so it could not be reached.
translations.idiomatic: There was a tree called Julailuo, its leaves like pears, growing in the belly of steep mountain cliffs, with a great serpent guarding the cave so it could not be reached.

sentences.zh: 欲取葉者，以方鏃矢射枝則落，為羣鳥銜去，則又射，乃得之。

translations.literal: To obtain the leaves, one shot the branch with square-headed arrows and it fell; flocks of birds carried it away, so one shot again and only then obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: To obtain the leaves, one shot the branch with square-headed arrows and it fell; flocks of birds carried it away, so one shot again and only then obtained it.

sentences.zh: 其詭譎類如此。

translations.literal: Their deceptions were of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Their deceptions were of this sort.

sentences.zh: 後術不驗，有詔聽還，不能去，死長安。

translations.literal: Later the art proved ineffective; an edict permitted his return, but he could not leave and died in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Later the art proved ineffective; an edict permitted his return, but he could not leave and died in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，廬伽逸多者，東天竺烏茶人，亦以術進，拜懷化大將軍，

translations.literal: During Emperor Gaozong's reign, Luzhi Yiduo of East India, an Udra man, also presented his art and was appointed General of Pacification and Transformation.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Gaozong's reign, Luzhi Yiduo of East India, an Udra man, also presented his art and was appointed General of Pacification and Transformation.

sentences.zh: 五天竺皆來朝。

translations.literal: All five Indias came to court.
translations.idiomatic: All five Indias came to court.

sentences.zh: 開元時，中天竺遣使者三至；

translations.literal: During the Kaiyuan era, Central India sent envoys three times;
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era, Central India sent envoys three times;

sentences.zh: 南天竺一，獻五色能言鳥，乞師討大食、吐蕃，丐名其軍。

translations.literal: South India once, presenting a five-colored talking bird, requesting troops against the Arabs and Tibet, and begging that their army be named.
translations.idiomatic: South India once, presenting a five-colored talking bird, requesting troops against the Arabs and Tibet, and begging that their army be named.

sentences.zh: 玄宗詔賜懷德軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong decreed the name Huai De Army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong decreed the name Huai De Army.

sentences.zh: 使者曰：「蕃夷惟以袍帶為寵。」

translations.literal: The envoy said: "Barbarians regard robes and belts as marks of favor.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said: "Barbarians regard robes and belts as marks of favor.

sentences.zh: 帝以錦袍、金革帶、魚袋並七事賜之；

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed brocade robes, golden leather belts, fish insignia pouches, and seven other items;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bestowed brocade robes, golden leather belts, fish insignia pouches, and seven other items;

sentences.zh: 北天竺一來朝。

translations.literal: North India came to court once.
translations.idiomatic: North India came to court once.

sentences.zh: 摩揭它，一曰摩伽陀，本中天竺屬國。

translations.literal: Magadha, also called Magadha, was originally a dependent state of Central India.
translations.idiomatic: Magadha. Also called Magadha, it was originally a dependent state of Central India.

sentences.zh: 環五千里，土沃宜稼穡，有異稻巨粒，號供大人米。

translations.literal: It encompassed five thousand li with fertile soil suited to crops; there was a special rice with huge grains, called rice for supplying great men.
translations.idiomatic: It encompassed five thousand li with fertile soil suited to crops; there was a special rice with huge grains, called rice for supplying great men.

sentences.zh: 王居拘阇揭羅布羅城，或曰俱蘇摩補羅，曰波咤厘子城，北瀕克伽河。

translations.literal: The king dwelt at Jushejialuoboluo City, also called Jusumobuluo or Bozhalizi City, north on the Ganges River.
translations.idiomatic: The king dwelt at Jushejialuoboluo City, also called Jusumobuluo or Bozhalizi City, north on the Ganges River.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二十一年，始遣使者自通於天子，獻波羅樹，樹類白楊。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Zhenguan, envoys first came of their own accord to the Son of Heaven, presenting bodhi trees resembling white poplars.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Zhenguan, envoys first came of their own accord to the Son of Heaven, presenting bodhi trees resembling white poplars.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣使取熬糖法，即詔揚州上諸蔗，拃沈如其劑，色味愈西域遠甚。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong dispatched envoys to obtain the method of refining sugar; he then ordered sugarcane from Yangzhou processed according to that method, and the color and flavor far surpassed those of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong dispatched envoys to obtain the method of refining sugar; he then ordered Yangzhou sugarcane processed by that method, and the color and flavor far surpassed the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 高宗又遣王玄策至其國摩訶菩提祠立碑焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong again dispatched Wang Xuance to their Mahabodhi Temple to erect a stele.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong again dispatched Wang Xuance to their Mahabodhi Temple to erect a stele.

sentences.zh: 後德宗自制鐘銘，賜那爛陀祠。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Dezong personally composed a bell inscription and bestowed it on the Nalanda Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Dezong personally composed a bell inscription and bestowed it on the Nalanda Temple.

sentences.zh: 又有那揭者，亦屬國也，貞觀二十年，遣使者貢方物。

translations.literal: There was also Najie, likewise a dependent state; in the twentieth year of Zhenguan it sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Najie, likewise a dependent state; in the twentieth year of Zhenguan it sent envoys presenting local products.

sentences.zh: 烏茶烏茶者，一曰烏伏那，亦曰烏萇，直天竺南，地廣五千里，東距勃律六百里，西罽賓四百里。

translations.literal: Udra. Udra, also called Wufuna or Wuchang, lay directly south of India, five thousand li across, six hundred li east to Bolü, four hundred li west to Jibin.
translations.idiomatic: Udra. Also called Wufuna or Wuchang, it lay directly south of India, five thousand li across, six hundred li east to Bolü, four hundred li west to Jibin.

sentences.zh: 山谷相屬，產金、鐵、蒲陶、郁金。

translations.literal: Mountains and valleys succeeded one another; it produced gold, iron, grapes, and turmeric.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains and valleys succeeded one another; it produced gold, iron, grapes, and turmeric.

sentences.zh: 稻歲熟。

translations.literal: Rice ripened each year.
translations.idiomatic: Rice ripened each year.

sentences.zh: 人柔詐，善禁架術。

translations.literal: The people were soft and deceitful and skilled in forbidden arts.
translations.idiomatic: The people were soft and deceitful and skilled in forbidden arts.

sentences.zh: 國無殺刑，抵死者放之窮山。

translations.literal: The state had no death penalty; those deserving death were released in remote mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The state had no death penalty; those deserving death were released in remote mountains.

sentences.zh: 罪有疑，飲以藥，視溲清濁而決輕重。

translations.literal: When guilt was doubtful, the accused drank a drug and judgment of severity or leniency was made by observing whether the urine was clear or turbid.
translations.idiomatic: When guilt was doubtful, the accused drank a drug and judgment of severity or leniency was made by observing whether the urine was clear or turbid.

sentences.zh: 有五城，王居術瞢蘗利城，一曰瞢揭厘城，東北有達麗羅川，即烏萇舊地，

translations.literal: There were five cities; the king dwelt at Shumenglili City, also called Mengjieli City. To the northeast was Daliluo River, the former territory of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: There were five cities; the king dwelt at Shumenglili City, also called Mengjieli City. To the northeast was Daliluo River, the former territory of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 其王達摩因陀訶斯遣使者獻龍腦香，璽書優答。

translations.literal: King Damo Yintuosi sent envoys presenting dragon-brain incense; an imperial edict responded graciously.
translations.idiomatic: King Damo Yintuosi sent envoys presenting dragon-brain incense; an imperial edict responded graciously.

sentences.zh: 大食與烏萇東鄙接，開元中數誘之，其王與骨咄、俱位二王不肯臣，玄宗命使者冊為王。

translations.literal: The Arabs bordered Udra's eastern frontier; in the Kaiyuan era they repeatedly incited it, but its king and the kings of Gudu and Juwei refused to submit; Emperor Xuanzong ordered envoys to invest them as kings.
translations.idiomatic: The Arabs bordered Udra's eastern frontier; in the Kaiyuan era they repeatedly incited it, but its king and the kings of Gudu and Juwei refused to submit; Emperor Xuanzong ordered envoys to invest them as kings.

sentences.zh: 章求拔國，或曰章揭拔，本西羌種。

translations.literal: The Kingdom of Zhangqiuba, also called Zhangjieba, was originally a branch of the Western Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangqiuba. Also called Zhangjieba, it was originally a branch of the Western Qiang.

sentences.zh: 居悉立西南四山中，後徙山西，與東天竺接。

translations.literal: It dwelt in the four mountains southwest of Sili, later moving west of the mountains to connect with East India.
translations.idiomatic: It dwelt in the four mountains southwest of Sili, later moving west of the mountains to connect with East India.

sentences.zh: 衣服略相類，因附之。

translations.literal: Clothing was somewhat similar, and for this reason it attached itself to India.
translations.idiomatic: Clothing was somewhat similar, and for this reason it attached itself to India.

sentences.zh: 地袤八九百里，勝兵二千人。

translations.literal: The territory measured eight or nine hundred li; effective fighting forces numbered two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The territory measured eight or nine hundred li; it could field two thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 無城郭，好鈔暴，商旅患之。

translations.literal: There were no walled cities; they loved raiding, and merchants suffered from them.
translations.idiomatic: There were no walled cities; they loved raiding, and merchants suffered from them.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二十年，其王羅利多菩伽因悉立國遣使者入朝。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Zhenguan, King Luoliduopojia sent envoys to court through the Kingdom of Sili.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Zhenguan, King Luoliduopojia sent envoys to court through the Kingdom of Sili.

sentences.zh: 玄策之討中天竺，發兵來赴，有功，由是職貢不絕。

translations.literal: When Xuance campaigned against Central India, they dispatched troops to assist and rendered service; tribute thereafter never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuance campaigned against Central India, they dispatched troops to assist; tribute thereafter never ceased.

sentences.zh: 悉立當吐蕃西南，戶五萬，城邑多旁澗溪。

translations.literal: Sili lay southwest of Tibet with fifty thousand households; many walled cities stood beside streams and ravines.
translations.idiomatic: Sili lay southwest of Tibet with fifty thousand households; many walled cities stood beside streams and ravines.

sentences.zh: 男子繒束頭，衣氈褐。

translations.literal: Men bound their heads with silk and wore felt and coarse wool.
translations.idiomatic: Men bound their heads with silk and wore felt and coarse wool.

sentences.zh: 婦人辮發，短裙。

translations.literal: Women braided their hair and wore short skirts.
translations.idiomatic: Women braided their hair and wore short skirts.

sentences.zh: 昏姻不以財聘。

translations.literal: Marriage did not rely on bride-price.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage did not rely on bride-price.

sentences.zh: 其谷宜粳稻、麥、豆。

translations.literal: Their grains suited rice, wheat, and beans.
translations.idiomatic: Their grains suited rice, wheat, and beans.

sentences.zh: 死者葬於野，不封樹，喪制為黑衣，滿年而除。

translations.literal: The dead were buried in the wild without mounds or trees; mourning garments were black and removed after a full year.
translations.idiomatic: The dead were buried in the wild without mounds or trees; mourning garments were black and removed after a full year.

sentences.zh: 刑有刖、劓。

translations.literal: Punishments included cutting off feet and slicing noses.
translations.idiomatic: Punishments included cutting off feet and slicing noses.

sentences.zh: 常羈屬吐蕃。

translations.literal: They were regularly bound subjects of Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: They were regularly bound subjects of Tibet.

sentences.zh: 罽賓罽賓，隋漕國也，居蔥嶺南，距京師萬二千里而贏，南距舍衛三千里。

translations.literal: Jibin. Jibin was the Sui Kingdom of Caoguo, south of the Congling Pass, twelve thousand li from the capital with surplus, three thousand li south to Shewei.
translations.idiomatic: Jibin. The Sui Kingdom of Caoguo, south of the Congling Pass, twelve thousand li from the capital with surplus, three thousand li south to Shewei.

sentences.zh: 王居脩鮮城，常役屬大月氏。

translations.literal: The king dwelt at Xiuxian City and was regularly subject to the Greater Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: The king dwelt at Xiuxian City and was regularly subject to the Greater Yuezhi.

sentences.zh: 地暑濕，人乘象，俗治浮屠法，

translations.literal: The land was hot and humid; people rode elephants and honored the Buddhist law by custom.
translations.idiomatic: The land was hot and humid; people rode elephants and honored the Buddhist law by custom.

sentences.zh: 遣使貢寶帶、金鎖、水精盞、頗黎狀若酸棗。

translations.literal: Envoys presented jeweled belts, gold locks, crystal cups, and glass resembling sour jujubes.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys presented jeweled belts, gold locks, crystal cups, and glass resembling sour jujubes.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中獻名馬。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan they presented famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan they presented famous horses.

sentences.zh: 太宗詔大臣曰：「朕始即位，或言天子欲耀兵，振伏四夷，惟魏徵勸我脩文德，安中夏；

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong told his ministers: "When I first ascended the throne, some said the Son of Heaven wished to display military might and awe the four barbarians; only Wei Zheng urged me to cultivate civil virtue and pacify the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong told his ministers: "When I first ascended the throne, some said the Son of Heaven wished to display military might; only Wei Zheng urged me to cultivate civil virtue and pacify the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 中夏安，遠人伏矣。

translations.literal: When the Central Plains are pacified, distant peoples submit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Central Plains are pacified, distant peoples submit.

sentences.zh: 今天下大安，四夷君長皆來獻，此徵力也。」

translations.literal: Now the empire is greatly at peace and chieftains of the four barbarians all come to present tribute—this is Zheng's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Now the empire is greatly at peace and chieftains of the four quarters all come with tribute—this is Zheng's achievement.

sentences.zh: 遣果毅何處羅拔等厚賫賜其國，並撫尉天竺。

translations.literal: Fruit-and-Courage He Chuluobo and others were dispatched with rich gifts to their state and to console India.
translations.idiomatic: Fruit-and-Courage He Chuluobo and others were dispatched with rich gifts to Jibin and to console India.

sentences.zh: 處羅拔至罽賓，王東向稽首再拜，仍遣人導護使者至天竺。

translations.literal: Chuluobo reached Jibin; the king bowed eastward twice and again sent men to guide and escort the envoy to India.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluobo reached Jibin; the king bowed eastward twice and again sent men to guide the envoy to India.

sentences.zh: 十六年，獻褥特鼠，喙尖尾赤，能食蛇，螫者嗅且尿，瘡即愈。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year they presented the mattress rat, with pointed snout and red tail, able to eat snakes; when bitten, smelling its urine healed the wound.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year they presented the mattress rat, with pointed snout and red tail, able to eat snakes; when bitten, smelling its urine healed the wound.

sentences.zh: 國人共傳王始祖曰馨孽，至曷擷支傳十二世，

translations.literal: The people commonly transmitted that their royal founder was called Xinnie, passing through twelve generations to Yijiezhi.
translations.idiomatic: The people commonly transmitted that their royal founder was called Xinnie, passing through twelve generations to Yijiezhi.

sentences.zh: 以其地為脩鮮都督府。

translations.literal: Their territory was made the Xiuxian Military Governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Their territory was made the Xiuxian Military Governorship.

sentences.zh: 龍朔初，拜其王脩鮮等十一州諸軍事、脩鮮都督，

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longshuo, their king was appointed military governor of Xiuxian and eleven other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longshuo, their king was appointed military governor of Xiuxian and eleven other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 遣使獻天文及秘方奇藥，天子冊其王為葛邏達支特勒。

translations.literal: Envoys presented astronomical knowledge and secret recipes for strange drugs; the Son of Heaven enfeoffed their king as Tejin Geluodazhi.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys presented astronomical knowledge and secret recipes for strange drugs; the Son of Heaven enfeoffed their king as Tejin Geluodazhi.

sentences.zh: 後烏散特勒灑年老，請以子拂菻罽婆嗣，聽之。

translations.literal: Later King Wusan Telesa grew old and requested that his son Fulin Jipo succeed; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Later King Wusan Telesa grew old and requested that his son Fulin Jipo succeed; permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 天寶四載，冊其子勃匐準為襲罽賓及烏萇國王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianbao, his son Bofuzhun was invested as successor king of Jibin and Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianbao, his son Bofuzhun was invested as successor king of Jibin and Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 乾元初使者朝貢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyuan envoys came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qianyuan envoys came with tribute.

sentences.zh: Category:印度

translations.literal: Category: India
translations.idiomatic: Category: India

sentences.zh: ◎西域下康國康者，一曰薩末鞬，亦曰颯秣建，元魏所謂悉斤者。

translations.literal: Western Regions (lower section): Kang. Kang, also called Samarkand, also called Sadijian, was what Northern Wei called Sijin.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Regions, lower section: Kang. Also called Samarkand or Sadijian, what Northern Wei called Sijin.

sentences.zh: 其南距史百五十里，西北距西曹百餘里，東南屬米百里，北中曹五十里。

translations.literal: South it was one hundred fifty li from Shi; northwest one hundred plus li from West Cao; southeast it belonged to Mi a hundred li; north it was fifty li from Central Cao.
translations.idiomatic: South it was one hundred fifty li from Shi; northwest one hundred plus li from West Cao; southeast it belonged to Mi a hundred li; north fifty li from Central Cao.

sentences.zh: 在那密水南，大城三十，小堡三百。

translations.literal: It lay south of the Namich River with thirty great cities and three hundred small fortresses.
translations.idiomatic: It lay south of the Namich River with thirty great cities and three hundred small fortresses.

sentences.zh: 君姓溫，本月氏人。

translations.literal: The ruler bore the surname Wen and was originally a Yuezhi man.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler bore the surname Wen and was originally a Yuezhi man.

sentences.zh: 始居祁連北昭武城，為突厥所破，稍南依蔥嶺，即有其地。

translations.literal: At first they dwelt at Zhaowu City north of the Qilian Mountains; broken by the Turks, they moved gradually south relying on the Congling Pass and then possessed this land.
translations.idiomatic: At first they dwelt at Zhaowu City north of the Qilian Mountains; broken by the Turks, they moved south along the Congling Pass and possessed this land.

sentences.zh: 枝庶分王，曰安，曰曹，曰石，曰米，曰何，曰火尋，曰戊地，曰史，世謂「九姓」，皆氏昭武。

translations.literal: Branch descendants divided into kings: An, Cao, Shi, Mi, He, Huoxun, Wudi, and Shi—the so-called Nine Surnames—all of the Zhaowu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Branch descendants divided into kings: An, Cao, Shi, Mi, He, Huoxun, Wudi, and Shi—the Nine Surnames—all of the Zhaowu clan.

sentences.zh: 土沃宜禾，出善馬，兵強諸國。

translations.literal: The soil was fertile and suited to grain; it produced fine horses and its army was strongest among the states.
translations.idiomatic: The soil was fertile and suited to grain; it produced fine horses and its army was strongest among the states.

sentences.zh: 人嗜酒，好歌舞於道。

translations.literal: The people loved wine and enjoyed singing and dancing in the streets.
translations.idiomatic: The people loved wine and enjoyed singing and dancing in the streets.

sentences.zh: 王帽氈，飾金雜寶。

translations.literal: The king's cap was felt, adorned with gold and assorted treasures.
translations.idiomatic: The king's cap was felt, adorned with gold and assorted treasures.

sentences.zh: 女子盤髻，蒙黑巾，綴金花。

translations.literal: Women wore looped topknots, covered with black cloth and adorned with golden flowers.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore looped topknots, covered with black cloth and adorned with golden flowers.

sentences.zh: 生兒以石蜜啖之，置膠於掌，欲長而甘言，持缶若黏雲。

translations.literal: At birth children were fed rock sugar; glue was placed in the palm, wishing that as they grew they would speak sweet words and hold jars as if sticking to clouds.
translations.idiomatic: At birth children were fed rock sugar; glue was placed in the palm, wishing sweet speech and hands that held jars as if sticking to clouds.

sentences.zh: 習旁行書。

translations.literal: They practiced horizontal writing.
translations.idiomatic: They practiced horizontal writing.

sentences.zh: 善商賈，好利，丈夫年二十，去傍國，利所在無不至。

translations.literal: They were skilled merchants who loved profit; at twenty husbands left for neighboring states and went wherever profit led.
translations.idiomatic: They were skilled merchants who loved profit; at twenty husbands left for neighboring states and went wherever profit led.

sentences.zh: 以十二月為歲首，尚浮圖法，祠祅神，出機巧技。

translations.literal: They took the twelfth month as the start of the year, honored the Buddhist law, worshipped the Zoroastrian god, and produced ingenious crafts.
translations.idiomatic: They took the twelfth month as the start of the year, honored Buddhism, worshipped the Zoroastrian god, and produced ingenious crafts.

sentences.zh: 十一月鼓舞乞寒，以水交潑為樂。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month they danced begging for cold and took mutual water-splashing as amusement.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month they danced begging for cold and took mutual water-splashing as amusement.

sentences.zh: 隋時，其王屈木支娶西突厥女，遂臣突厥。

translations.literal: During the Sui dynasty their king Qumuzhi married a Western Turk woman and thereupon became a subject of the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui dynasty their king Qumuzhi married a Western Turk woman and thereupon became a subject of the Turks.

sentences.zh: 武德十年，始遣使來獻。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Wude envoys first came to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Wude envoys first came to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 貞觀五年，遂請臣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguan they then requested to become subjects.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhenguan they then requested to become subjects.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「朕惡取虛名，害百姓；

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said: "I hate taking empty names and harming the common people;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said: "I hate taking empty names and harming the common people;

sentences.zh: 且康臣我，緩急當同其憂。

translations.literal: and if Kang becomes my subject, in urgency I should share their troubles.
translations.idiomatic: and if Kang becomes my subject, in urgency I should share their troubles.

sentences.zh: 師行萬里，寧朕誌邪？」

translations.literal: An army marching ten thousand li—would that suit my intent?
translations.idiomatic: An army marching ten thousand li—would that suit my intent?

sentences.zh: 卻不受。

translations.literal: He declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: He declined to accept.

sentences.zh: 俄又遣使獻師子獸，帝珍其遠，命秘書監虞世南作賦。

translations.literal: Soon they again sent envoys presenting lion beasts; the emperor treasured their distant journey and ordered Secretariat Director Yu Shinan to compose a rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they again sent envoys presenting lions; the emperor treasured their distant journey and ordered Yu Shinan to compose a rhapsody.

sentences.zh: 自是歲入貢，致金桃、銀桃，詔令植苑中。

translations.literal: Thereafter tribute came yearly, presenting golden peaches and silver peaches; an edict ordered them planted in the imperial park.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute came yearly, presenting golden peaches and silver peaches; an edict ordered them planted in the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 高宗永徽時，以其地為康居都督府，即授其王拂呼縵為都督。

translations.literal: During the Yonghui era of Emperor Gaozong their territory was made the Kangju Military Governorship and their king Fuhu Man was appointed military governor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui era their territory was made the Kangju Military Governorship and King Fuhu Man was appointed military governor.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天中，以大首領篤娑缽提為王。

translations.literal: During Wansui Tongtian, the great chieftain Dusuoti was made king.
translations.idiomatic: During Wansui Tongtian, the great chieftain Dusuoti was made king.

sentences.zh: 死，子泥涅師師立。

translations.literal: When he died his son Nieshi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his son Nieshi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 死，國人立突昏為王。

translations.literal: When he died the people established Tuhun as king.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the people established Tuhun as king.

sentences.zh: 開元初，貢鎖子鎧、水精杯、碼瓶、駝鳥卵及越諾、侏儒、胡旋女子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan they presented chain-mail armor, crystal cups, agate bottles, ostrich eggs, Yuenuo, dwarfs, and Hu-spinning girls.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyuan they presented chain-mail armor, crystal cups, agate bottles, ostrich eggs, Yuenuo, dwarfs, and Hu-spinning girls.

sentences.zh: 其王烏勒伽與大食亟戰不勝，來乞師，天子不許。

translations.literal: Their king Wulejia fought repeatedly with the Arabs without victory and came begging for troops; the Son of Heaven refused.
translations.idiomatic: King Wulejia fought repeatedly with the Arabs without victory and begged for troops; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 久之，請封其子咄曷為曹王，默啜為米王，詔許。

translations.literal: After a long time he requested enfeoffment of his son Duoha as King of Cao and Moruo as King of Mi; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he requested enfeoffment of his son Duoha as King of Cao and Moruo as King of Mi; an edict granted it.

sentences.zh: 烏勒伽死，遣使立咄曷，封欽化王，以其母可敦為郡夫人。

translations.literal: When Wulejia died, envoys were dispatched to establish Duoha; he was enfeoffed as King of Qinhua and his mother Keden as Lady of the Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Wulejia died, envoys established Duoha as King of Qinhua and his mother Keden as Lady of the Commandery.

sentences.zh: 安國安者，一曰布豁，又曰捕喝，元魏謂忸蜜者。

translations.literal: An. An, also called Buohuo, also called Buhe, was what Northern Wei called Niumi.
translations.idiomatic: An. Also called Buohuo or Buhe, what Northern Wei called Niumi.

sentences.zh: 東北至東安，西南至畢，皆百里所。

translations.literal: Northeast to East An and southwest to Bi were each about a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Northeast to East An and southwest to Bi were each about a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 西瀕烏滸河，治阿濫謐城，即康居小君長罽王故地。

translations.literal: West on the Wuhu River it governed Alianmi City, the former territory of the Lesser Lord of Kangju, King Ji.
translations.idiomatic: West on the Wuhu River it governed Alianmi City, the former territory of the lesser Kangju lord King Ji.

sentences.zh: 大城四十，小堡千餘。

translations.literal: Forty great cities and more than a thousand small fortresses.
translations.idiomatic: Forty great cities and more than a thousand small fortresses.

sentences.zh: 募勇健者為柘羯。

translations.literal: Brave and strong men were recruited as zhejie.
translations.idiomatic: Brave and strong men were recruited as zhejie.

sentences.zh: 柘羯，猶中國言戰士也。

translations.literal: Zhejie means warriors in Chinese speech.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejie means warriors in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 武德時，遣使入朝。

translations.literal: During Wude envoys came to court.
translations.idiomatic: During Wude envoys came to court.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，獻方物，太宗厚尉其使曰：「西突厥已降，商旅可行矣。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan they presented local products; Emperor Taizong richly consoled their envoy, saying: "The Western Turks have already submitted; merchants may travel.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguan they presented local products; Emperor Taizong consoled their envoy: "The Western Turks have submitted; merchants may travel.

sentences.zh: 諸胡大悅。

translations.literal: All the Hu were greatly pleased."
translations.idiomatic: All the Hu were greatly pleased."

sentences.zh: 其王訶陵迦又獻名馬，自言一姓相承二十二世雲。

translations.literal: Their king Helingjia again presented famous horses, stating that one surname had succeeded for twenty-two generations.
translations.idiomatic: King Helingjia again presented famous horses, stating one surname had succeeded for twenty-two generations.

sentences.zh: 是歲，東安國亦入獻，言子姓相承十世云。

translations.literal: That year East An also came with tribute, stating ten generations of succession.
translations.idiomatic: That year East An also came with tribute, stating ten generations of succession.

sentences.zh: 東安東安，或曰小國，曰喝汗，在那密水之陽，東距何二百里許，西南至大安四百里。

translations.literal: East An, also called a small state or Hehan, lay on the south bank of the Namich River, two hundred li east to He and four hundred li southwest to Great An.
translations.idiomatic: East An, also called Hehan, lay on the south bank of the Namich River, two hundred li east to He and four hundred li southwest to Great An.

sentences.zh: 治喝汗城，亦曰斤。

translations.literal: It governed Hehan City, also called Jin.
translations.idiomatic: It governed Hehan City, also called Jin.

sentences.zh: 大城二十，小堡百。

translations.literal: Twenty great cities and a hundred small fortresses.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty great cities and a hundred small fortresses.

sentences.zh: 顯慶時，以阿濫為安息州，即以其王昭武殺為刺史；

translations.literal: During Xianqing, Alian was made Anxi Prefecture and their king Zhaowu Sha was appointed prefect;
translations.idiomatic: During Xianqing, Alian was made Anxi Prefecture and King Zhaowu Sha was appointed prefect;

sentences.zh: 斤為木鹿州，以其王昭武閉息為刺史。

translations.literal: Jin was made Mulu Prefecture and their king Zhaowu Bixi was appointed prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was made Mulu Prefecture and King Zhaowu Bixi was appointed prefect.

sentences.zh: 開元十四年，其王篤薩波提遣弟阿悉爛達拂耽發黎來朝，納馬豹。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kaiyuan their king Dusaboti sent his younger brother Asilandafodanlai to court presenting horses and leopards.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Kaiyuan King Dusaboti sent his brother Asilandafodanlai to court with horses and leopards.

sentences.zh: 後八年，獻波斯█婁二，拂菻繡氍球一，郁金香、石蜜等，其妻可敦獻柘辟大氍球二，繡氍球一，丐賜袍帶、鎧仗及可敦袿䙱裝澤。

translations.literal: Eight years later they presented Persian carpets, Fulin embroidered felts, tulips, rock sugar, and the queen presented large felts and embroidered felts, begging robes, belts, armor, and queenly garments.
translations.idiomatic: Eight years later they presented Persian carpets, Fulin felts, tulips, and rock sugar; the queen presented felts and begged robes, belts, armor, and queenly garments.

sentences.zh: 東曹東曹，或曰率都沙那，蘇對沙那，劫布呾那，蘇都識匿，凡四名。

translations.literal: East Cao, also called Shudushana, Sudushana, Jiebudana, or Sudushini—four names in all.
translations.idiomatic: East Cao, also called Shudushana, Sudushana, Jiebudana, or Sudushini—four names in all.

sentences.zh: 居波悉山之陰，漢貳師城地也。

translations.literal: It dwelt on the northern slopes of Mount Boxi, the land of Han General Li's City.
translations.idiomatic: It dwelt on the northern slopes of Mount Boxi, the land of Han General Li's City.

sentences.zh: 東北距俱戰提二百里，北至石，西至康，東北寧遠，皆四百里許，南至吐火羅五百里。

translations.literal: Northeast two hundred li to Juzhanti, north to Shi, west to Kang, northeast to Ningyuan—all about four hundred li; south five hundred li to Tuhuoluo.
translations.idiomatic: Northeast two hundred li to Juzhanti, north to Shi, west to Kang, northeast to Ningyuan—about four hundred li each; south five hundred li to Tuhuoluo.

sentences.zh: 有野叉城，城有巨窟，嚴以關鑰，歲再祭，人向窟立，中即煙出，先觸者死。

translations.literal: There was Yecha City with a great cave sealed with locks; twice yearly they sacrificed, and people stood facing the cave; smoke issued from within and whoever touched it first died.
translations.idiomatic: There was Yecha City with a great cave sealed with locks; twice yearly they sacrificed. Smoke issued from the cave and whoever touched it first died.

sentences.zh: 武德中，與康同遣使入朝。

translations.literal: During Wude they sent envoys to court together with Kang.
translations.idiomatic: During Wude they sent envoys to court together with Kang.

sentences.zh: 其使曰：「本國以臣為健兒，聞秦王神武，欲隸麾下。」

translations.literal: Their envoy said: "Our state made me a strong warrior; hearing Prince of Qin's divine martial prowess, I wished to serve under his banner.
translations.idiomatic: Their envoy said: "Our state made me a warrior; hearing Prince of Qin's divine prowess, I wished to serve under his banner.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 西曹西曹者，隋時曹也，南接史及波覽，治瑟底痕城。

translations.literal: West Cao was Cao in Sui times, south connecting with Shi and Bolan, governing Sedihén City.
translations.idiomatic: West Cao was Cao in Sui times, south connecting with Shi and Bolan, governing Sedihén City.

sentences.zh: 東北越於底城有得悉神祠，國人事之。

translations.literal: Northeast beyond Yudi City was the Deshen Shrine, which the state worshipped.
translations.idiomatic: Northeast beyond Yudi City was the Deshen Shrine, which the state worshipped.

sentences.zh: 有金具器，款其左曰：「漢時天子所賜。」

translations.literal: There was a gold vessel with an inscription on the left: "Bestowed by the Son of Heaven of Han.
translations.idiomatic: There was a gold vessel inscribed: "Bestowed by the Son of Heaven of Han.

sentences.zh: 武德中入朝。

translations.literal: During Wude they came to court.
translations.idiomatic: During Wude they came to court.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年，王哥邏仆羅遣使者獻方物，詔封懷德王，即上言：「祖考以來，奉天可汗，願同唐人受調發，佐天子征討。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao King Geluopuluo sent envoys presenting local products; an edict enfeoffed him King of Huai De, and he memorialized: "From our ancestors we have served the Heavenly Kagan and wish like Tang people to accept mobilization and assist the Son of Heaven in campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianbao King Geluopuluo sent envoys; he was enfeoffed King of Huai De and memorialized willingness to accept Tang mobilization.

sentences.zh: 十一載，東曹王設阿忽與安王請擊黑衣大食，玄宗尉之，不聽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year East Cao King Sheahu and the King of An requested to attack the Black-robed Arabs; Emperor Xuanzong consoled them but refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year East Cao King Sheahu and the King of An requested to attack the Black-robed Arabs; Xuanzong refused.

sentences.zh: 中曹中曹者，居西曹東，康之北。

translations.literal: Central Cao lay east of West Cao and north of Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Central Cao lay east of West Cao and north of Kang.

sentences.zh: 王治迦底真城。

translations.literal: The king governed Jiadizhen City.
translations.idiomatic: The king governed Jiadizhen City.

sentences.zh: 其人長大，工戰鬥。

translations.literal: The people were tall and skilled in fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The people were tall and skilled in fighting.

sentences.zh: 柘支石，或曰柘支，曰柘折，曰赭時，漢大宛北鄙也。

translations.literal: Shi, also called Shizhi or Zheshi, was the northern frontier of Han Greater Fergana.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, also called Shizhi or Zheshi, was the northern frontier of Han Greater Fergana.

sentences.zh: 去京師九千里。

translations.literal: Nine thousand li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Nine thousand li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 東北距西突厥，西北波臘，南二百里所抵俱戰提，西南五百里康也。

translations.literal: Northeast to the Western Turks, northwest to Bola, south two hundred li to Juzhanti, southwest five hundred li to Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Northeast to the Western Turks, northwest to Bola, south two hundred li to Juzhanti, southwest five hundred li to Kang.

sentences.zh: 圓千餘里，右涯素葉河。

translations.literal: About a thousand li round, bounded on the right by the Suyab River.
translations.idiomatic: About a thousand li round, bounded on the right by the Suyab River.

sentences.zh: 王姓石，治柘折城，故康居小王窳匿城地。

translations.literal: The king bore the surname Shi and governed Shizhi City, the former territory of the Lesser Lord of Kangju, Yuni.
translations.idiomatic: The king bore the surname Shi and governed Shizhi City, the former lesser Kangju lord Yuni's territory.

sentences.zh: 西南有藥殺水，入中國謂之真珠河，亦曰質河。

translations.literal: Southwest was the Yash River, called Pearl River in China, also called Quality River.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest was the Yash River, called Pearl River in China, also Quality River.

sentences.zh: 東南有大山，生瑟瑟。

translations.literal: Southeast were great mountains producing sese.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast were great mountains producing sese.

sentences.zh: 俗善戰，多良馬。

translations.literal: By custom they were skilled in warfare and had many fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they were skilled in warfare and had many fine horses.

sentences.zh: 隋大業初，西突厥殺其王，以特勒匐職統其國。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sui Daye the Western Turks killed their king and had Teli Fuzhi rule the state.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Sui Daye the Western Turks killed their king and had Teli Fuzhi rule the state.

sentences.zh: 武德、貞觀間，數獻方物。

translations.literal: During Wude and Zhenguan they repeatedly presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: During Wude and Zhenguan they repeatedly presented local products.

sentences.zh: 顯慶三年，以瞰羯城為大宛都督府，授其王瞰土屯攝舍提於屈昭穆都督。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianqing, Kanjie City was made the Dayuan Military Governorship and their king Kan Tutun Sheti was appointed military governor of Quzhaomu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianqing, Kanjie City became the Dayuan Military Governorship; King Kan Tutun Sheti was appointed military governor.

sentences.zh: 開元初，封其君莫賀咄吐屯，有功，為石國王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan their lord Mohedu Tutun, having rendered service, was made King of Shi.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyuan Lord Mohedu Tutun, having rendered service, was made King of Shi.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，又冊順義王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was again invested as King of Shunyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was again invested as King of Shunyi.

sentences.zh: 明年，王伊捺吐屯屈勒上言：「今突厥已屬天可汗，惟大食為諸國患，請討之。」

translations.literal: The next year King Yinatutun Qule memorialized: "Now the Turks belong to the Heavenly Kagan; only the Arabs are the affliction of the states—please campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: The next year King Yinatutun Qule memorialized: "The Turks now belong to the Heavenly Kagan; only the Arabs afflict the states—please campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 天子不許。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven refused.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，封王子那俱車鼻施為懷化王，賜鐵券。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao his prince Najuchabis was enfeoffed King of Huaihua and granted an iron certificate.
