translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao Prince Najuchabis was enfeoffed King of Huaihua and granted an iron certificate.

sentences.zh: 久之，安西節度使高仙芝劾其無蕃臣禮，請討之。

translations.literal: After a long time Anxi Military Governor Gao Xianzhi impeached them for lacking vassal ritual and requested a campaign.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time Anxi Military Governor Gao Xianzhi impeached them for lacking vassal ritual and requested a campaign.

sentences.zh: 王約降，仙芝遣使者護送至開遠門，俘以獻，斬闕下，於是西域皆怨。

translations.literal: The king agreed to surrender; Xianzhi sent envoys to escort him to Kaiyuan Gate, captured and presented him, and beheaded him below the palace; thereafter all the Western Regions resented this.
translations.idiomatic: The king agreed to surrender; Xianzhi had him captured and beheaded below the palace; thereafter all the Western Regions resented this.

sentences.zh: 王子走大食乞兵，攻怛邏斯城，敗仙芝軍，自是臣大食。

translations.literal: The prince fled to the Arabs begging for troops, attacked Talas City, defeated Xianzhi's army, and thereafter became subjects of the Arabs.
translations.idiomatic: The prince fled to the Arabs, attacked Talas, defeated Xianzhi, and thereafter became Arab subjects.

sentences.zh: 寶應時，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: During Baoying envoys came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During Baoying envoys came with tribute.

sentences.zh: 碎葉有碎葉者，出安西西北千里所，得勃達嶺，南抵上國，北突騎施南鄙也，西南直蔥嶺贏二千里。

translations.literal: Suyab. Suyab lay a thousand li northwest of Anxi beyond Boda Ridge, south reaching the upper state and north bordering the southern frontier of the Turgesh.
translations.idiomatic: Suyab lay a thousand li northwest of Anxi beyond Boda Ridge, south to the upper state and north bordering the Turgesh.

sentences.zh: 水南流者經中國入於海，北流者經胡入於海。

translations.literal: Waters flowing south passed through China into the sea; those flowing north passed through the Hu into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Waters flowing south reached China and the sea; those flowing north reached the Hu lands and the sea.

sentences.zh: 北三日行度雪海，春夏常雨雪。

translations.literal: Northward three days' travel crossed the Snow Sea; in spring and summer there was always rain and snow.
translations.idiomatic: Northward three days crossed the Snow Sea; in spring and summer there was always rain and snow.

sentences.zh: 繇勃達嶺北行贏千里，得細葉川。

translations.literal: From Boda Ridge northward beyond a thousand li one reached Xiyechuan.
translations.idiomatic: From Boda Ridge northward beyond a thousand li lay Xiyechuan.

sentences.zh: 東曰熱海，地寒不凍。

translations.literal: East was Hot Sea, where the land was cold but did not freeze.
translations.idiomatic: East was Hot Sea, cold yet unfrozen.

sentences.zh: 西有碎葉城，天寶七載，北庭節度使王正見伐安西，毀之。

translations.literal: West was Suyab City; in the seventh year of Tianbao Beiting Military Governor Wang Zhengjian campaigning in Anxi destroyed it.
translations.idiomatic: West was Suyab City; in the seventh year of Tianbao Wang Zhengjian destroyed it campaigning in Anxi.

sentences.zh: 川長千里，有異姓突厥兵數萬，耕者皆擐甲，相掠為奴婢。

translations.literal: The river valley was a thousand li long with tens of thousands of foreign Turk warriors; cultivators all wore armor and plundered one another as slaves.
translations.idiomatic: The valley was a thousand li with tens of thousands of foreign Turk warriors; cultivators wore armor and enslaved one another.

sentences.zh: 西屬怛邏斯城，石常分兵鎮之。

translations.literal: West it belonged to Talas City, which Shi often garrisoned with divided troops.
translations.idiomatic: West it belonged to Talas City, which Shi often garrisoned.

sentences.zh: 自此抵西海矣。

translations.literal: From here one reached the Western Sea.
translations.idiomatic: From here one reached the Western Sea.

sentences.zh: 三月訖九月，未嘗雨，人以雪水溉田。

translations.literal: From the third month through the ninth month it never rained; people irrigated fields with meltwater.
translations.idiomatic: From the third through the ninth month it never rained; fields were irrigated with meltwater.

sentences.zh: 怖捍石東南千餘里，有怖捍者，山四環之，地膏腴，多馬羊。

translations.literal: More than a thousand li southeast of Buhan was Buhan, ringed by mountains with rich soil and many horses and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand li southeast of Buhan lay Buhan, ringed by mountains, rich in horses and sheep.

sentences.zh: 西千里距堵利瑟那，東臨葉葉水，水出蔥嶺北原，色濁，西北流入大磧。

translations.literal: A thousand li west to Tulisena, east on the Yeye River; the river issued from the northern plain of the Congling Pass, its color turbid, flowing northwest into the great desert.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand li west to Tulisena, east on the Yeye River issuing from the northern Congling plain, turbid, flowing northwest into the desert.

sentences.zh: 無水草，望大山，尋遺胔，知所指，五百餘里即康也。

translations.literal: Without water or fodder, one gazed at great mountains and sought abandoned corpses to know the direction; five hundred li farther was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Without water or fodder, one followed abandoned corpses as guides; five hundred li farther was Kang.

sentences.zh: 彌末米，或曰彌末，曰彌秣賀。

translations.literal: Mi, also called Mimo or Mimohé.
translations.idiomatic: Mi, also called Mimo or Mimohé.

sentences.zh: 北百里距康。

translations.literal: A hundred li north of Kang.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred li north of Kang.

sentences.zh: 其君治缽息德城，永徽時為大食所破。

translations.literal: Its lord governed Boxide City; during Yonghui it was broken by the Arabs.
translations.idiomatic: Its lord governed Boxide City; during Yonghui it was broken by the Arabs.

sentences.zh: 顯慶三年，以其地為南謐州，授其君昭武開拙為刺史，自是朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianqing its territory was made Nanmi Prefecture and its lord Zhaowu Kaizhuo was appointed prefect; tribute thereafter never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianqing its territory became Nanmi Prefecture; Lord Zhaowu Kaizhuo was appointed prefect; tribute never ceased.

sentences.zh: 開元時，獻璧、舞筵、師子、胡旋女。

translations.literal: During Kaiyuan they presented jade, dance mats, lions, and Hu-spinning girls.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan they presented jade, dance mats, lions, and Hu-spinning girls.

sentences.zh: 十八年，大首領末野門來朝。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the great chieftain Moyemen came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year great chieftain Moyemen came to court.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，封其君為恭順王，母可敦郡夫人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao their lord was enfeoffed King of Gongshun and the queen Lady of the Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao their lord was enfeoffed King of Gongshun and the queen Lady of the Commandery.

sentences.zh: 屈霜你迦何，或曰屈霜你迦，曰貴霜匿，即康居小王附墨城故地。

translations.literal: He, also called Queshuonijia or Guishuangni, was the former territory of the Lesser Lord of Kangju, Fumo City.
translations.idiomatic: He, also called Queshuonijia or Guishuangni, was the former lesser Kangju lord Fumo City's territory.

sentences.zh: 城左有重樓，北繪中華古帝，東突厥、婆羅門，西波斯、拂菻等諸王，其君旦詣拜則退。

translations.literal: Left of the city was a multi-storied tower; on the north were painted ancient Chinese emperors, Eastern Turks, and Brahmins; on the west Persians and Fulin kings; the lord visited each morning to bow and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Left of the city was a tower painted with Chinese emperors, Turks, Brahmins, Persians, and Fulin kings; the lord bowed each morning and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十五年，遣使者入朝。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenguan envoys came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Zhenguan envoys came to court.

sentences.zh: 永徽時上言：「聞唐出師西討，願輸糧於軍。」

translations.literal: During Yonghui they memorialized: "Hearing Tang is campaigning westward, we wish to supply grain to the army.
translations.idiomatic: During Yonghui they memorialized willingness to supply grain to the Tang army campaigning westward.

sentences.zh: 俄以其地為貴霜州，授其君昭武婆達地刺史。

translations.literal: Soon their territory was made Guishuang Prefecture and their lord Zhaowu Bodadi was appointed prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Soon their territory became Guishuang Prefecture; Lord Zhaowu Bodadi was appointed prefect.

sentences.zh: 遣使者缽底失入謝。

translations.literal: Envoy Bodi sent came to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy Bodi sent came to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 火尋火尋，或曰貨利習彌，曰過利，居烏滸水之陽。

translations.literal: Huoxun, also called Huoliximi or Guoli, lay on the south bank of the Wuhu River.
translations.idiomatic: Huoxun, also called Huoliximi or Guoli, lay on the south bank of the Wuhu River.

sentences.zh: 東南六百里距戊地，西南與波斯接，西北抵突厥曷薩，乃康居小王奧城故地。

translations.literal: Six hundred li southeast to Wudi, southwest connecting with Persia, northwest reaching the Turk Yisa—it was the former Lesser Lord of Kangju Aocheng's territory.
translations.idiomatic: Six hundred li southeast to Wudi, southwest to Persia, northwest to Turk Yisa—former lesser Kangju lord Aocheng's territory.

sentences.zh: 其君治急多颶遮城。

translations.literal: Its lord governed Jiduohui City.
translations.idiomatic: Its lord governed Jiduohui City.

sentences.zh: 諸胡惟其國有車牛，商賈乘以行諸國。

translations.literal: Among the Hu only this state had ox-carts, which merchants rode to travel among the states.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Hu only this state had ox-carts for merchants traveling among the states.

sentences.zh: 天寶十載，君稍施芬遣使者朝，獻黑鹽。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianbao Lord Shaoshifen sent envoys to court presenting black salt.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tianbao Lord Shaoshifen sent envoys presenting black salt.

sentences.zh: 寶應時復入朝。

translations.literal: During Baoying they again came to court.
translations.idiomatic: During Baoying they again came to court.

sentences.zh: 羯霜那史，或曰佉沙，曰羯霜那，居獨莫水南康居小王蘇薤城故地。

translations.literal: Shi, also called Qiasha or Jieshuangna, was the former Lesser Lord of Kangju Suoxie City's territory on the south bank of the Dumo River.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, also called Qiasha or Jieshuangna, was the former lesser Kangju lord Suoxie City's territory on the south bank of the Dumo River.

sentences.zh: 西百五十里距那色波，北二百里屬米，南四百里吐火羅也。

translations.literal: A hundred fifty li west to Nashebo, two hundred li north belonging to Mi, four hundred li south to Tuhuoluo.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred fifty li west to Nashebo, two hundred li north to Mi, four hundred li south to Tuhuoluo.

sentences.zh: 有鐵門山，左右巉峭，石色如鐵，為關以限二國，以金錮闔。

translations.literal: There was Iron Gate Mountain with steep cliffs on both sides, stone colored like iron, serving as a pass limiting the two states, its gate bound with gold.
translations.idiomatic: Iron Gate Mountain had steep iron-colored cliffs serving as a pass between two states, its gate bound with gold.

sentences.zh: 城有神祠，每祭必千羊，用兵類先禱乃行。

translations.literal: The city had a divine shrine; each sacrifice required a thousand sheep; before military action they prayed first.
translations.idiomatic: The city had a divine shrine requiring a thousand sheep per sacrifice; armies prayed before marching.

sentences.zh: 國有城五百。

translations.literal: The state had five hundred cities.
translations.idiomatic: The state had five hundred cities.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，其君狄遮始通中國，號最強盛，築乞史城，地方數千里。

translations.literal: During Sui Daye its lord Dizhe first communicated with China, said to be strongest, and built Qishi City over several thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: During Sui Daye Lord Dizhe first communicated with China, built Qishi City, and was strongest over several thousand li.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十六年，君沙瑟畢獻方物。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhenguan Lord Shasebi presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Zhenguan Lord Shasebi presented local products.

sentences.zh: 顯慶時，以其地為佉沙州，授君昭武失阿喝刺史。

translations.literal: During Xianqing their territory was made Qiasha Prefecture and Lord Zhaowu Shiahe was appointed prefect.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianqing their territory became Qiasha Prefecture; Lord Zhaowu Shiahe was appointed prefect.

sentences.zh: 開元十五年，君忽必多獻舞女、文豹。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kaiyuan Lord Hubiduo presented dancing girls and literary leopards.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Kaiyuan Lord Hubiduo presented dancing girls and literary leopards.

sentences.zh: 後君長數死、立，然首領時時入朝。

translations.literal: Later lords frequently died and were replaced, yet chieftains regularly came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Later lords frequently died and were replaced, yet chieftains regularly came to court.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，詔改史為來威國。

translations.literal: During Tianbao an edict changed Shi to the Kingdom of Laiwei.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao an edict changed Shi to the Kingdom of Laiwei.

sentences.zh: 那色波那色波，亦曰小史，蓋為史所役屬。

translations.literal: Nashebo, also called Lesser Shi, was made subject by Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Nashebo, also called Lesser Shi, was subject to Shi.

sentences.zh: 居吐火羅故地，東厄蔥嶺，西接波剌斯，南雪山。

translations.literal: It lay in former Tuhuoluo territory, east bounded by the Congling Pass, west connecting with Persia, south by the Snow Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: It lay in former Tuhuoluo territory, east bounded by the Congling Pass, west to Persia, south by the Snow Mountains.

sentences.zh: 呾蜜種循縛芻水北有呾蜜種，亦自國，東西六百里所。

translations.literal: North of the Fuchu River on the north bank was the Damimi tribe, also a state in itself, six hundred li east to west.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Fuchu River was the Damimi tribe, also a state, six hundred li east to west.

sentences.zh: 又東逾四種，有鑊沙者，廣三百里，長五百里，東界骨咄，接蔥嶺有十八種。

translations.literal: Farther east beyond four tribes was Huosha, three hundred li wide and five hundred li long, east bordering Gudu, connecting with eighteen tribes at the Congling Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Farther east was Huosha, three hundred by five hundred li, east bordering Gudu, connecting eighteen Congling tribes.

sentences.zh: 南有揭職，稍大，幅員準千里，陵阜連屬，多菽麥，氣寒烈。

translations.literal: South was Jiezhi, somewhat larger, about a thousand li across, with linked hills, much beans and wheat, and a harsh cold climate.
translations.idiomatic: South was Jiezhi, about a thousand li across with linked hills, beans and wheat, and harsh cold.

sentences.zh: 東南抵雪山六百里，道吐火羅，又逾五種至婆羅睹邏。

translations.literal: Six hundred li southeast to the Snow Mountains led to Tuhuoluo, then beyond five tribes to Boluoduo.
translations.idiomatic: Six hundred li southeast to the Snow Mountains led to Tuhuoluo, then beyond five tribes to Boluoduo.

sentences.zh: 北逾山行六百里，得烏萇種。

translations.literal: Six hundred li north over mountains reached the Wuchang tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Six hundred li north over mountains reached the Wuchang tribe.

sentences.zh: 東北行二百里至河波羅水，水西南流，春夏涸凍。

translations.literal: Two hundred li northeast reached the Heluo River; its waters flowed southwest and dried and froze in spring and summer.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred li northeast reached the Heluo River flowing southwest, drying and freezing in spring and summer.

sentences.zh: 北歷十二種有婆羅吸摩補羅，最大種，綿地四千里，山周其外，土沃，產鍮、水精。

translations.literal: North through twelve tribes was Boluoximobuluo, the largest tribe, four thousand li across, mountains encircling it, rich soil, producing brass and crystal.
translations.idiomatic: North through twelve tribes was Boluoximobuluo, four thousand li across, mountain-encircled, producing brass and crystal.

sentences.zh: 北大雪山，即東女也。

translations.literal: North was the great Snow Mountain—that is, the Eastern Women.
translations.idiomatic: North was the great Snow Mountain—the Eastern Women.

sentences.zh: 歷十九種得摩揭陀。

translations.literal: Through nineteen tribes one reached Magadha.
translations.idiomatic: Through nineteen tribes one reached Magadha.

sentences.zh: 又東過四種，逾大河，有迦摩縷波，皆阪險，地接西南夷，其人類蠻獠。

translations.literal: Four tribes farther east beyond a great river was Kamoluobo, all steep slopes bordering the southwestern barbarians, people like Man and Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Four tribes east beyond a great river was Kamoluobo, steep and bordering southwestern barbarians.

sentences.zh: 行二月，叩蜀南邊，其東南野象群暴，故戰用象軍。

translations.literal: Traveling two months reached the southern border of Shu; wild elephants rampaged in the southeast, so they fought with elephant armies.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling two months reached Shu’s southern border; they fought with elephant armies against rampaging wild elephants.

sentences.zh: 又南歷三十二種有狼揭羅者，地大數千里，其君治窣菟黎濕伐羅城。

translations.literal: Thirty-two tribes farther south was Langjieluo, several thousand li across; its lord governed Suoyulishifaluo City.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-two tribes south was Langjieluo, several thousand li across, capital at Suoyulishifaluo City.

sentences.zh: 西北即波剌斯，傳言廣萬里，王治蘇剌薩儻那城。

translations.literal: Northwest was Persia, said to span ten thousand li; the king governed Sulasahenna City.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest was Persia, said to span ten thousand li, capital at Sulasahenna City.

sentences.zh: 土溫溽，引水為田，人富饒。

translations.literal: The soil was warm and humid; water was drawn for fields; the people were rich.
translations.idiomatic: The soil was warm and humid; irrigated fields made the people rich.

sentences.zh: 出金、銀、水精。

translations.literal: It produced gold, silver, and crystal.
translations.idiomatic: It produced gold, silver, and crystal.

sentences.zh: 多工巧，織錦、褐、氍毹。

translations.literal: Many were skilled craftsmen, weaving brocade, felt, and felts.
translations.idiomatic: Many were skilled weavers of brocade and felt.

sentences.zh: 產善馬、橐它。

translations.literal: It produced fine horses and camels.
translations.idiomatic: It produced fine horses and camels.

sentences.zh: 人服錦氎。

translations.literal: People wore brocade felts.
translations.idiomatic: People wore brocade felts.

sentences.zh: 賦稅，口出四銀錢，又以交易。

translations.literal: Taxation was four silver coins per person, with trade besides.
translations.idiomatic: Taxation was four silver coins per person, with trade besides.

sentences.zh: 西北距拂菻，西南際海島，有西女種，皆女子，多珍貨，附拂菻，拂菻君長歲遣男子配焉。

translations.literal: Northwest to Fulin, southwest to sea islands, was the Western Women tribe—all women with many treasures, attached to Fulin, whose lord sent men yearly to mate with them.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest to Fulin, southwest to sea islands, was the Western Women tribe attached to Fulin, whose lord sent men yearly to mate with them.

sentences.zh: 俗產男不舉。

translations.literal: By custom male children were not raised.
translations.idiomatic: By custom male children were not raised.

sentences.zh: 又有臂、多、勢、羅四種，西北逾大山廣川，歷小城聚，行二千里即謝也。

translations.literal: Also the four tribes Bi, Duo, Shi, and Luo; northwest beyond great mountains and broad rivers, traveling two thousand li, was Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Also Bi, Duo, Shi, and Luo; northwest beyond mountains and rivers, two thousand li, was Xie.

sentences.zh: 北五百里有弗栗恃薩儻那，地橫二千里，縱千里。

translations.literal: Five hundred li north was Fulishisahenna, two thousand li across and a thousand li long.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred li north was Fulishisahenna, two thousand by a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 其君突厥種，治護那城。

translations.literal: Its lord was of Turkic stock and governed Huna City.
translations.idiomatic: Its Turkic lord governed Huna City.

sentences.zh: 東北大雪山，盛夏常凍，鑿冰乃可度。

translations.literal: Northeast was the great Snow Mountain, frozen even in midsummer; one chiseled ice to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Northeast was the great Snow Mountain, frozen even in midsummer.

sentences.zh: 下有安呾羅縛者，地三千里；

translations.literal: Below was Andaluofu, three thousand li across;
translations.idiomatic: Below was Andaluofu, three thousand li across;

sentences.zh: 西北逾嶺四百里有闊悉多；

translations.literal: four hundred li northwest was Kuoxiduo;
translations.idiomatic: four hundred li northwest was Kuoxiduo;

sentences.zh: 西北三百里有活種，大二千里。

translations.literal: three hundred li northwest was the Huo tribe, two thousand li across.
translations.idiomatic: three hundred li northwest was the Huo tribe, two thousand li across.

sentences.zh: 此三種皆居吐火羅故地，臣於突厥，君亦突厥種，主鐵門南諸戎，遷徙不常。

translations.literal: These three tribes all dwelt in former Tuhuoluo territory, subject to the Turks; their lords were also Turkic, ruling the various tribes south of Iron Gate, migrating without fixed abode.
translations.idiomatic: These three tribes dwelt in former Tuhuoluo territory, subject to Turks, migrating without fixed abode.

sentences.zh: 東又有七種，東南峽道險甚，無慮三百里，得俱蘭。

translations.literal: East were seven tribes; the southeastern pass was extremely dangerous, presumably three hundred li, reaching Julan.
translations.idiomatic: East were seven tribes; the southeastern pass was extremely dangerous, reaching Julan.

sentences.zh: 東北山行五百里，即護密，北識匿也。

translations.literal: Five hundred li northeast over mountains was Humi, also called Shini.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred li northeast over mountains was Humi, also Shini.

sentences.zh: 南有商彌，地大二千里而贏，多蒲陶。

translations.literal: South was Shangmi, more than two thousand li across with many grapes.
translations.idiomatic: South was Shangmi, more than two thousand li with many grapes.

sentences.zh: 生雌黃，鑿石乃得。

translations.literal: Orpiment was mined from stone.
translations.idiomatic: Orpiment was mined from stone.

sentences.zh: 東北逾山七百里，至波謎羅川，東西千里，南北百里，春夏雨雪。

translations.literal: Seven hundred li northeast over mountains was Boluoluo Valley, a thousand li east to west and a hundred north to south, with rain and snow in spring and summer.
translations.idiomatic: Seven hundred li northeast was Boluoluo Valley, snowing in spring and summer.

sentences.zh: 南有缽露種，多紫金。

translations.literal: South was the Bolu tribe with much purple gold.
translations.idiomatic: South was the Bolu tribe with much purple gold.

sentences.zh: 行五百里有盤陀。

translations.literal: Five hundred li farther was Pantuo.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred li farther was Pantuo.

sentences.zh: 東行八百里出蔥嶺，又八百里至烏鎩，環千里，出白、、青三種玉。

translations.literal: Eight hundred li east out of the Congling Pass, then eight hundred li to Wusa, a thousand li round, producing white, green, and blue jade.
translations.idiomatic: Eight hundred li east out of the Congling Pass, then eight hundred li to Wusa, producing three kinds of jade.

sentences.zh: 君長世臣盤陀。

translations.literal: The lords generation after generation served Pantuo.
translations.idiomatic: The lords generation after generation served Pantuo.

sentences.zh: 北徑磧，曠野五百里，得疏勒。

translations.literal: North through the desert, five hundred li of open wilderness, one reached Kashgar.
translations.idiomatic: North through five hundred li of desert one reached Kashgar.

sentences.zh: 東南五百里濟徙多水，逾大沙嶺，有斫句迦種，或曰沮渠，地千里。

translations.literal: Five hundred li southeast crossed the Tidu River over a great sand ridge to the Zhuqujia tribe, also called Juqu, a thousand li across.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred li southeast crossed the Tidu River to the Zhuqujia tribe, a thousand li across.

sentences.zh: 東逾領八百里，即於闐也，東有媲摩川。

translations.literal: Eight hundred li east over a ridge was Khotan, east of which was the Pimo River.
translations.idiomatic: Eight hundred li east over a ridge was Khotan, east of which was the Pimo River.

sentences.zh: 度磧行二百里，得尼壤城，在大澤中，地墊洳，蘆荒茂，行者鑿道趣城通於闐，而於闐以為東關。

translations.literal: Crossing the desert two hundred li reached Nirang City in a great marsh with lush reeds; travelers cut a path to the city connecting to Khotan, which regarded it as the eastern gate.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the desert two hundred li reached Nirang City in a great marsh, Khotan's eastern gate.

sentences.zh: 又東行入大流沙，人行無跡，故往返輒迷，聚遣骸以識道。

translations.literal: Farther east one entered the Great Drifting Sands; travelers left no tracks and often lost their way, gathering bones to mark the route.
translations.idiomatic: Farther east lay the Great Drifting Sands where travelers left no tracks and marked routes with bones.

sentences.zh: 無水草，多熱風，觸人及六畜皆迷仆。

translations.literal: Without water or fodder, hot winds struck people and livestock and all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Without water or fodder, hot winds struck people and livestock.

sentences.zh: 行四百里至故都邏。

translations.literal: Traveling four hundred li reached old Duluo.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling four hundred li reached old Duluo.

sentences.zh: 又六百里至故折摩馱那，古且末也。

translations.literal: Six hundred li farther reached old Zhemotuona, ancient Qiemo.
translations.idiomatic: Six hundred li farther reached old Zhemotuona, ancient Qiemo.

sentences.zh: 又千里至故納縛波，古樓蘭也。

translations.literal: A thousand li farther reached old Nazhabo, ancient Loulan.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand li farther reached old Nazhabo, ancient Loulan.

sentences.zh: 自呾蜜以下，諸種相與群聚，華人皆以國名之，故未嘗與唐通，傳記雜詭，不可得而考，然其地與諸國連屬，粗序其名云。

translations.literal: From Damimi downward the various tribes gathered together; Chinese all named them by state, so they had never communicated with Tang and records are confused and cannot be verified; yet their lands connect with the various states, and their names are roughly ordered here.
translations.idiomatic: From Damimi downward tribes gathered; records are confused, yet their lands connect with neighboring states and names are roughly ordered here.

sentences.zh: 寧遠寧遠者，本拔汗那，或曰汗，元魏時謂破洛那。

translations.literal: Ningyuan was originally Bahanna, also called Han, what Northern Wei called Poluona.
translations.idiomatic: Ningyuan was originally Bahanna, also called Han, what Northern Wei called Poluona.

sentences.zh: 去京師八千里。

translations.literal: Eight thousand li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Eight thousand li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 居西城，在真珠河之北。

translations.literal: It dwelt in the western city on the north bank of the Pearl River.
translations.idiomatic: It dwelt in the western city on the north bank of the Pearl River.

sentences.zh: 有大城六，小城百。

translations.literal: Six great cities and a hundred small ones.
translations.idiomatic: Six great cities and a hundred small ones.

sentences.zh: 人多壽。

translations.literal: People often lived long.
translations.idiomatic: People often lived long.

sentences.zh: 其王自魏、晉相承不絕。

translations.literal: Their kings succeeded uninterrupted from Wei and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Their kings succeeded uninterrupted from Wei and Jin.

sentences.zh: 每元日，王及首領判二朋，朋出一人被甲鬥，眾以瓦石相之，有死者止，以卜歲善惡。

translations.literal: Each New Year the king and chieftains divided into two groups; each group sent one man in armor to fight; the crowd pelted them with tiles and stones; when one died they stopped, divining the year's fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Each New Year the king and chieftains divided into two groups for armed combat; when one died they stopped, divining the year's fortune.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，王契為西突厥瞰莫賀咄所殺，阿瑟那鼠匿奪其城。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan King Qi was killed by the Western Turk Khan Mohemodu; Ashina Shuni seized his city.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan King Qi was killed by Western Turk Khan Mohemodu; Ashina Shuni seized his city.

sentences.zh: 鼠匿死，子遏波之立契兄子阿了參為王，治呼悶城；

translations.literal: When Shuni died his son Ebo established Qi's brother's son Alcan as king, governing Humen City;
translations.idiomatic: When Shuni died his son Ebo established Qi's nephew Alcan as king at Humen City;

sentences.zh: 遏波之治渴塞城。

translations.literal: Ebo governed Kesai City.
translations.idiomatic: Ebo governed Kesai City.

sentences.zh: 顯慶初，遏波之遣使朝貢，高宗厚慰諭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianqing Ebo sent envoys with tribute; Emperor Gaozong richly consoled them.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianqing Ebo sent envoys; Emperor Gaozong richly consoled them.

sentences.zh: 三年，以渴塞城為休循州都督，授阿了參刺史，自是歲朝貢。

translations.literal: In the third year Kesai City was made Xiuxun Military Governorship and Alcan was appointed prefect; tribute came yearly thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Kesai City became Xiuxun Military Governorship; Alcan was appointed prefect; tribute came yearly.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元二十七年，王阿悉爛達幹助平吐火仙，冊拜奉化王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Kaiyuan King Asilandagan helped pacify Tuhuoxian and was invested King of Fenghua.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Kaiyuan King Asilandagan helped pacify Tuhuoxian and was invested King of Fenghua.

sentences.zh: 天寶三載，改其國號寧遠，帝以外家姓賜其王曰竇，又封宗室女為和義公主降之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianbao its state name was changed to Ningyuan; the emperor granted the imperial maternal surname Dou to its king and enfeoffed an imperial clanswoman as Princess of Heyi to marry him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianbao its name became Ningyuan; the emperor granted the surname Dou and enfeoffed Princess of Heyi to marry its king.

sentences.zh: 十三載，王忠節遣子薛裕朝，請留宿衛，習華禮，聽之，授左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year King Zhongjie sent his son Xue Yu to court requesting to remain as palace guard and learn Chinese ritual; permission was granted and he was appointed Left Martial Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year King Zhongjie sent his son Xue Yu to remain as palace guard; he was appointed Left Martial Guard General.

sentences.zh: 其事唐最謹。

translations.literal: Their service to Tang was the most diligent.
translations.idiomatic: Their service to Tang was the most diligent.

sentences.zh: 大勃律大勃律，或曰布露。

translations.literal: Greater Bolü, also called Bulu.
translations.idiomatic: Greater Bolü, also called Bulu.

sentences.zh: 直吐蕃西，與小勃律接，西鄰北天竺、烏萇。

translations.literal: Directly west of Tibet, connecting with Lesser Bolü, west neighboring North India and Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Directly west of Tibet, connecting with Lesser Bolü, west to North India and Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 地宜郁金。

translations.literal: The soil suited turmeric.
translations.idiomatic: The soil suited turmeric.

sentences.zh: 役屬吐蕃。

translations.literal: Subject to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Subject to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天逮開元時，三遣使者朝，故冊其君蘇弗舍利支離泥為王。

translations.literal: From Wansui Tongtian through Kaiyuan they sent envoys to court three times; therefore their lord Sufu Shelizhini was invested king.
translations.idiomatic: From Wansui Tongtian through Kaiyuan they sent envoys three times; Lord Sufu Shelizhini was invested king.

sentences.zh: 死，又冊蘇麟陀逸之嗣王。

translations.literal: When he died Sulin Tuoyizhi was again invested successor king.
translations.idiomatic: When he died Sulin Tuoyizhi was invested successor king.

sentences.zh: 凡再遣大首領貢方物。

translations.literal: Twice they sent great chieftains presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: Twice they sent great chieftains with tribute.

sentences.zh: 小勃律去京師九千里而贏，東少南三千里距吐蕃贊普牙，東八百里屬烏萇，東南三百里大勃律，南五百里個失蜜，北五百里當護密之娑勒城。

translations.literal: Lesser Bolü lay nine thousand li from the capital with surplus; three thousand li southeast to the Tibetan king's camp, eight hundred li east belonging to Wuchang, three hundred li southeast to Greater Bolü, five hundred li south to Geshimi, five hundred li north to Sule City of Humi.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser Bolü lay nine thousand li from the capital; three thousand li southeast to the Tibetan camp, connecting Greater Bolü, Geshimi, and Humi.

sentences.zh: 王居孽多城，臨娑夷水。

translations.literal: The king dwelt at Nieduo City on the Sayi River.
translations.idiomatic: The king dwelt at Nieduo City on the Sayi River.

sentences.zh: 其西山顛有大城曰迦布羅。

translations.literal: On its western mountain peak was a great city called Jiabolu.
translations.idiomatic: On its western peak was a great city called Jiabolu.

sentences.zh: 開元初，王沒謹忙來朝，玄宗以兒子畜之，以其地為綏遠軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan King Mojinmang came to court; Emperor Xuanzong treated him like a son and made his land the Suiyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyuan King Mojinmang came to court; Xuanzong made his land the Suiyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 國迫吐蕃，數為所困。

translations.literal: The state was pressed by Tibet and repeatedly harassed.
translations.idiomatic: The state was pressed by Tibet and repeatedly harassed.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃曰：「我非謀爾國，假道攻四鎮爾。」

translations.literal: Tibet said: "We do not covet your state but borrow the route to attack the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet said: "We borrow your route to attack the Four Garrisons, not covet your state.

sentences.zh: 久之，吐蕃奪其九城，沒謹忙求救北庭，節度使張孝嵩遣疏勒副使張思禮率銳兵四千倍道往，沒謹忙因出兵，大破吐蕃，殺其眾數萬，復九城。

translations.literal: After a long time Tibet seized nine of its cities.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time Tibet seized nine of its cities.

sentences.zh: 詔冊為小勃律王；

translations.literal: Mojinmang begged Beiting for rescue; Deputy Military Governor Zhang Sixi dispatched Kashgar Deputy Commissioner Zhang Sili with four thousand crack troops by forced march;
translations.idiomatic: Mojinmang begged Beiting for rescue; Zhang Sixi dispatched Zhang Sili with four thousand crack troops;

sentences.zh: 遣大首領察卓那斯摩沒勝入謝。

translations.literal: Mojinmang thereupon led troops and greatly defeated Tibet, killing tens of thousands and recovering nine cities.
translations.idiomatic: Mojinmang led troops, defeated Tibet, killing tens of thousands and recovering nine cities.

sentences.zh: 沒謹忙死，子難泥立。

translations.literal: An edict invested him King of Lesser Bolü;
translations.idiomatic: An edict invested him King of Lesser Bolü;

sentences.zh: 死，兄麻來兮立。

translations.literal: Great chieftain Chazhuonasimosheng was dispatched to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Great chieftain Chazhuonasimosheng was dispatched to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 死，蘇失利之立，為吐蕃陰誘，妻以女，故西北二十餘國皆臣吐蕃，貢獻不入。

translations.literal: When Mojinmang died his son Nanni succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Mojinmang died his son Nanni succeeded.

sentences.zh: 安西都護三討之無功。

translations.literal: When he died his elder brother Malaiqi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his elder brother Malaiqi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 天寶六載，詔副都護高仙芝伐之。

translations.literal: When he died Sushilizhi succeeded; secretly incited by Tibet and given a daughter in marriage, more than twenty states of the northwest all became Tibetan subjects and tribute ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When he died Sushilizhi succeeded; incited by Tibet and given a daughter in marriage, more than twenty northwestern states became Tibetan subjects.

sentences.zh: 前遣將軍席元慶馳千騎見蘇失利之曰：「請假道趨大勃律。」

translations.literal: The Anxi Protector campaigned three times without success.
translations.idiomatic: The Anxi Protector campaigned three times without success.

sentences.zh: 城中大酋五六，皆吐蕃腹心。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianbao an edict ordered Deputy Protector Gao Xianzhi to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianbao Deputy Protector Gao Xianzhi was ordered to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 仙芝約元慶：「吾兵到，必走山。

translations.literal: First General Xi Yuanqing was dispatched with a thousand horsemen to tell Sushilizhi: "We request passage to Greater Bolü.
translations.idiomatic: First Xi Yuanqing was dispatched to tell Sushilizhi: "We request passage to Greater Bolü.

sentences.zh: 出詔書召慰，賜繒彩。

translations.literal: Five or six great chiefs in the city were all Tibetan confidants.
translations.idiomatic: Five or six great chiefs in the city were Tibetan confidants.

sentences.zh: 縛酋領待我。」

translations.literal: Xianzhi agreed with Yuanqing: "When our troops arrive they will surely flee to the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi agreed with Yuanqing: "When our troops arrive they will flee to the mountains.

sentences.zh: 元慶如約。

translations.literal: Issue an edict summoning and consoling them and bestow silk.
translations.idiomatic: Issue an edict summoning them and bestow silk.

sentences.zh: 蘇失利之挾妻走，不得其處。

translations.literal: Bind the chiefs and wait for me."
translations.idiomatic: Bind the chiefs and wait for me."

sentences.zh: 仙芝至，斬為吐蕃者，斷娑夷橋。

translations.literal: Yuanqing did as agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing did as agreed.

sentences.zh: 是暮，吐蕃至，不能救。

translations.literal: Sushilizhi fled with his wife and could not be found.
translations.idiomatic: Sushilizhi fled with his wife and could not be found.

sentences.zh: 仙芝約王降，遂平其國。

translations.literal: When Xianzhi arrived he beheaded those who were for Tibet and cut the Sayi Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhi arrived he beheaded Tibetan partisans and cut the Sayi Bridge.

sentences.zh: 於是拂菻、大食諸胡七十二國皆震恐，鹹歸附。

translations.literal: That evening Tibet arrived but could not rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: That evening Tibet arrived but could not rescue them.

sentences.zh: 執小勃律王及妻歸京師，詔改其國號歸仁，置歸仁軍，募千人鎮之。

translations.literal: Xianzhi persuaded the king to surrender and thus pacified the state.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi persuaded the king to surrender and pacified the state.

sentences.zh: 帝赦蘇失利之不誅，授右威衛將軍，賜紫袍、黃金帶，使宿衛。

translations.literal: Thereupon Fulin, the Arabs, and seventy-two Hu states all trembled in fear and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Fulin, the Arabs, and seventy-two Hu states all trembled and submitted.

sentences.zh: 吐火羅吐火羅，或曰土豁羅，曰睹貨邏，元魏謂吐呼羅者。

translations.literal: Tuhuoluo, also called Tuhuoluo, also called Duhuoluo, was what Northern Wei called Tuhulu.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhuoluo, also called Duhuoluo, was what Northern Wei called Tuhulu.

sentences.zh: 居蔥嶺西，烏滸河之南，古大夏地。

translations.literal: It lay west of the Congling Pass, south of the Wuhu River, the ancient land of Greater Daxia.
translations.idiomatic: It lay west of the Congling Pass, south of the Wuhu River, ancient Greater Daxia.

sentences.zh: 與挹怛雜處。

translations.literal: It mixed with the Yeda.
translations.idiomatic: It mixed with the Yeda.

sentences.zh: 勝兵十萬。

translations.literal: Effective fighting forces numbered one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: It could field one hundred thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 國土著，少女多男。

translations.literal: The state was settled; girls were many and boys few.
translations.idiomatic: The state was settled; girls outnumbered boys.

sentences.zh: 北有頗黎山，其陽穴中有神馬，國人遊牧牝於側，生駒輒汗血。

translations.literal: North was the Poli Mountain; in its sunny cave was a divine horse; the people pastured mares nearby and foals born were blood-sweating.
translations.idiomatic: North was Poli Mountain with a divine horse cave; foals pastured nearby were blood-sweating.

sentences.zh: 其王號「葉護」。

translations.literal: Their king was titled Yehu.
translations.idiomatic: Their king was titled Yehu.

sentences.zh: 武德、貞觀時再入獻。

translations.literal: During Wude and Zhenguan they came twice with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During Wude and Zhenguan they came twice with tribute.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年，獻大鳥，高七尺，色黑，足類橐駝，翅而行，日三百里，能啖鐵，俗謂駝鳥。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui they presented a great bird seven chi tall, black, with feet like a camel, wing-walking three hundred li a day, able to eat iron—popularly called ostrich.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yonghui they presented a great black bird seven chi tall with camel-like feet, wing-walking three hundred li a day—an ostrich.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，以其阿緩城為月氏都督府，析小城為二十四州，授王阿史那都督。

translations.literal: During Xianqing their Ahuancheng was made the Yuezhi Military Governorship, dividing small cities into twenty-four prefectures; King Ashina was appointed military governor.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianqing Ahuancheng became the Yuezhi Military Governorship of twenty-four prefectures; King Ashina was appointed military governor.

sentences.zh: 後二年，遣子來朝，俄又獻碼硇鐙樹，高三尺。

translations.literal: Two years later his son came to court and soon they again presented an agate lamp tree three chi tall.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later his son came to court and they presented an agate lamp tree three chi tall.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，王那都泥利遣弟仆羅入朝，留宿衛。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong King Nadunili sent his younger brother Poluo to court to remain as palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenlong King Nadunili sent his brother Poluo to remain as palace guard.

sentences.zh: 開元、天寶間數獻馬、█婁、異藥、乾陀婆羅二百品、紅碧玻黎，乃冊其君骨咄祿頓達度為吐火羅葉護、挹怛王。

translations.literal: During Kaiyuan and Tianbao they repeatedly presented horses, carpets, strange drugs, and two hundred items of Gandharan goods and red-green glass; their lord Gutulu Dundadu was then invested Tuhuoluo Yehu and Yeda King.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan and Tianbao they repeatedly presented horses, carpets, and glass; Lord Gutulu Dundadu was invested Tuhuoluo Yehu and Yeda King.

sentences.zh: 其後，鄰胡羯師謀引吐蕃攻吐火羅，於是葉護失裏忙伽羅丐安西兵助討，帝為出師破之。

translations.literal: Later neighboring Hu Jieshi plotted to incite Tibet to attack Tuhuoluo; Yehu Shilimangaluo begged Anxi troops to help suppress them and the emperor dispatched an army that broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jieshi incited Tibet against Tuhuoluo; Yehu Shilimangaluo begged Anxi troops and the emperor dispatched an army that broke them.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，與西域九國發兵為天子討賊，肅宗詔隸朔方行營。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyuan, together with nine Western Regions states they dispatched troops to campaign against rebels for the Son of Heaven; Emperor Suzong ordered them attached to the Shuofang camp.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qianyuan, with nine Western Regions states they dispatched troops for the emperor; Suzong ordered them attached to the Shuofang camp.

sentences.zh: 挹怛國挹怛國，漢大月氏之種。

translations.literal: The Kingdom of Yeda. Yeda was the stock of Han Greater Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yeda. The stock of Han Greater Yuezhi.

sentences.zh: 大月氏為烏孫所奪，西過大宛，擊大夏臣之。

translations.literal: Greater Yuezhi was displaced by Wusun, passed west beyond Greater Fergana, attacked and made Greater Daxia subject.
translations.idiomatic: Greater Yuezhi was displaced by Wusun, passed west, attacked and subjugated Greater Daxia.

sentences.zh: 治藍氏城。

translations.literal: They governed Lanzhi City.
translations.idiomatic: They governed Lanzhi City.

sentences.zh: 大夏即吐火羅也。

translations.literal: Greater Daxia was Tuhuoluo.
translations.idiomatic: Greater Daxia was Tuhuoluo.

sentences.zh: 嚈噠，王姓也，後裔以姓為國，訛為挹怛，亦曰挹闐。

translations.literal: Yanda was a royal surname; descendants took the surname as the state, corrupted to Yeda, also called Yitian.
translations.idiomatic: Yanda was a royal surname; descendants took it as the state name, corrupted to Yeda, also Yitian.

sentences.zh: 俗類突厥，天寶中遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Customs resembled the Turks; during Tianbao envoys came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Customs resembled the Turks; during Tianbao envoys came with tribute.

sentences.zh: 俱蘭俱蘭，或曰俱羅弩，曰屈浪挐，與吐火羅接，環地三千里，南大雪山，北俱魯河。

translations.literal: Julan, also called Jululuo or Qulangna, connected with Tuhuoluo, three thousand li round, south of the great Snow Mountain, north of the Julu River.
translations.idiomatic: Julan, connecting with Tuhuoluo, three thousand li round, south of the Snow Mountains, north of the Julu River.

sentences.zh: 出金精，琢石取之。

translations.literal: It produced gold essence mined from stone.
translations.idiomatic: It produced gold essence mined from stone.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二十年，其王忽提婆遣使者來獻，書辭類浮屠語。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Zhenguan their king Huti sent envoys with tribute; the letter resembled Buddhist language.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Zhenguan King Huti sent envoys; the letter resembled Buddhist language.

sentences.zh: 劫劫者，居蔥嶺中，西及南距賒彌，西北挹怛也。

translations.literal: Jiejie lay in the Congling Pass, west and south bordering Shemi, northwest to Yeda.
translations.idiomatic: Jiejie lay in the Congling Pass, west and south to Shemi, northwest to Yeda.

sentences.zh: 去京師萬二千里。

translations.literal: Twelve thousand li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve thousand li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 氣常熱，有稻、麥、粟、豆。

translations.literal: The climate was constantly hot; there were rice, wheat, millet, and beans.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was constantly hot; there were rice, wheat, millet, and beans.

sentences.zh: 畜羊馬。

translations.literal: Sheep and horses were raised.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep and horses were raised.

sentences.zh: 俗死棄於山。

translations.literal: By custom the dead were abandoned on mountains.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the dead were abandoned on mountains.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，遣使者獻寶帶、玻黎、水精杯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude envoys presented jeweled belts, glass, and crystal cups.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wude envoys presented jeweled belts, glass, and crystal cups.

sentences.zh: 越底延越底延者，南三千里距天竺，西北千里至賒彌，東北五千里至瓜州，居辛頭水之北。

translations.literal: Yuediyan lay three thousand li south of India, a thousand li northwest to Shemi, five thousand li northeast to Guazhou, north of the Sindhu River.
translations.idiomatic: Yuediyan lay three thousand li south of India, northwest to Shemi, northeast to Guazhou, north of the Sindhu River.

sentences.zh: 其法不殺人，重罪流，輕罪放。

translations.literal: By their law they did not kill; serious crimes meant exile, light crimes release.
translations.idiomatic: By their law they did not kill; serious crimes meant exile, light crimes release.

sentences.zh: 無租稅。

translations.literal: There were no taxes.
translations.idiomatic: There were no taxes.

sentences.zh: 俗翦發，被錦袍，貧者白氎。

translations.literal: By custom they cut their hair and wore brocade robes; the poor wore white felt.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they cut their hair and wore brocade robes; the poor wore white felt.

sentences.zh: 自澡潔。

translations.literal: They bathed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They bathed themselves.

sentences.zh: 氣溫，多稻、米、石蜜。

translations.literal: The climate was warm with much rice and rock sugar.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was warm with much rice and rock sugar.

sentences.zh: 谢䫻谢䫻居吐火羅西南，本曰漕矩咤，或曰漕矩，顯慶時謂訶達羅支，武後改今號。

translations.literal: Xieju lay southwest of Tuhuoluo, originally called Caojuzha, also Caoju; during Xianqing called Hedaluozhi, Empress Wu changed to the present name.
translations.idiomatic: Xieju lay southwest of Tuhuoluo, originally Caojuzha; Empress Wu changed to the present name.

sentences.zh: 東距罽賓，東北帆延，皆四百里。

translations.literal: East four hundred li to Jibin, northeast four hundred li to Fanyan.
translations.idiomatic: East four hundred li to Jibin, northeast four hundred li to Fanyan.

sentences.zh: 南婆羅門，西波斯，北護時健。

translations.literal: South to Brahmana, west to Persia, north to Hushijian.
translations.idiomatic: South to Brahmana, west to Persia, north to Hushijian.

sentences.zh: 其王居鶴悉那城，地七千里，亦治阿娑你城。

translations.literal: Its king dwelt at Hexina City, seven thousand li across, also governing Asuni City.
translations.idiomatic: Its king dwelt at Hexina City, seven thousand li across, also governing Asuni City.

sentences.zh: 多郁金、瞿草。

translations.literal: Much turmeric and qu grass.
translations.idiomatic: Much turmeric and qu grass.

sentences.zh: 瀵泉灌田。

translations.literal: Spring-fed streams irrigated fields.
translations.idiomatic: Spring-fed streams irrigated fields.

sentences.zh: 國中有突厥、罽賓、吐火羅種人雜居，罽賓取其子弟持兵以禦大食。

translations.literal: In the state Turks, Jibin, and Tuhuoluo peoples lived mixed; Jibin took their young men as armed guards against the Arabs.
translations.idiomatic: Turks, Jibin, and Tuhuoluo lived mixed; Jibin took their young men as guards against the Arabs.

sentences.zh: 景雲初，遣使朝貢，後遂臣罽賓。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingyun envoys came with tribute and later became subject to Jibin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingyun envoys came and later they became subject to Jibin.

sentences.zh: 開元八年，天子冊葛達羅支頡利發誓屈爾為王。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kaiyuan the Son of Heaven invested Gedaluozhi Feli Faqie'er as king.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Kaiyuan Gedaluozhi Feli Faqie'er was invested king.

sentences.zh: 至天寶中數朝獻。

translations.literal: Until Tianbao they repeatedly came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Until Tianbao they repeatedly came to court.

sentences.zh: 帆延帆延者，或曰望衍，曰梵衍那。

translations.literal: Fanyan, also called Wangyan or Fanyanna.
translations.idiomatic: Fanyan, also called Wangyan or Fanyanna.

sentences.zh: 居斯卑莫運山之旁，西北與護時健接，東南距罽賓，西南訶達羅支，與吐火羅連境。

translations.literal: It lay beside Mount Sibimoyun, northwest connecting with Hushijian, southeast four hundred li to Jibin, southwest to Xiedaluozhi, bordering Tuhuoluo.
translations.idiomatic: It lay beside Mount Sibimoyun, connecting Hushijian, Jibin, Xiedaluozhi, and Tuhuoluo.

sentences.zh: 地寒，人穴處。

translations.literal: The land was cold; people dwelt in caves.
translations.idiomatic: The land was cold; people dwelt in caves.

sentences.zh: 王治羅爛城，有大城四五。

translations.literal: The king governed Llan City with four or five great cities.
translations.idiomatic: The king governed Llan City with four or five great cities.

sentences.zh: 水北流入烏滸河。

translations.literal: Water flowed north into the Wuhu River.
translations.idiomatic: Water flowed north into the Wuhu River.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，遣使者入朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan envoys came to court.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguan envoys came to court.

sentences.zh: 顯慶三年，以羅爛城為寫鳳都督府，縛時城為悉萬州，授王寫鳳州都督，管內五州諸軍事，自是朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianqing, Llan City was made Xiefeng Military Governorship and Fushi City was Siwan Prefecture; the king was appointed Xiefeng military governor over five prefectures and all military affairs; tribute thereafter never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianqing, Llan City became Xiefeng Military Governorship; the king was appointed military governor over five prefectures; tribute never ceased.

sentences.zh: 石汗那石汗那，或曰斫汗那。

translations.literal: Shihanna, also called Zhanhanna.
translations.idiomatic: Shihanna, also called Zhanhanna.

sentences.zh: 自縛底野南入雪山，行四百里得帆延，東臨烏滸河。

translations.literal: From Fudiye south into the Snow Mountains, traveling four hundred li reached Fanyan, east on the Wuhu River.
translations.idiomatic: From Fudiye south into the Snow Mountains, four hundred li reached Fanyan, east on the Wuhu River.

sentences.zh: 多赤豹。

translations.literal: Many red leopards.
translations.idiomatic: Many red leopards.

sentences.zh: 開元、天寶中，一再朝獻。

translations.literal: During Kaiyuan and Tianbao they came to court once or twice with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan and Tianbao they came once or twice with tribute.

sentences.zh: 識匿識匿，或曰屍棄尼，曰瑟匿。

translations.literal: Shini, also called Shiqini or Seni.
translations.idiomatic: Shini, also called Shiqini or Seni.

sentences.zh: 東南直京師九千里，東五百里距蔥嶺守捉所，南三百里屬護蜜，西北五百里抵俱蜜。

translations.literal: Southeast directly nine thousand li from the capital, five hundred li east to the Congling garrison, three hundred li south belonging to Humi, five hundred li northwest to Jumi.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast nine thousand li from the capital, east to the Congling garrison, south to Humi, northwest to Jumi.

sentences.zh: 初治苦汗城，後散居山谷。

translations.literal: At first they governed Kuhan City, later scattered in mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: At first they governed Kuhan City, later scattered in valleys.

sentences.zh: 有大谷五，酋長自為治，謂之五識匿。

translations.literal: There were five great valleys; chieftains each governed themselves, called the Five Shini.
translations.idiomatic: Five great valleys; chieftains each governed themselves—the Five Shini.

sentences.zh: 地二千里，無五谷。

translations.literal: The land was two thousand li across without the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand li across without the five grains.

sentences.zh: 人喜攻剽，劫商賈。

translations.literal: People loved raiding and plundered merchants.
translations.idiomatic: People loved raiding and plundered merchants.

sentences.zh: 播蜜川四谷稍不用王號令。

translations.literal: The four valleys of Bomichuan slightly did not use the king's orders.
translations.idiomatic: The four valleys of Bomichuan slightly ignored the king's orders.

sentences.zh: 俗窟室。

translations.literal: By custom they dwelt in cave houses.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they dwelt in cave houses.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二十年，與似沒、役槃二國使者偕來朝。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Zhenguan envoys of Simo and Yipan came to court together.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Zhenguan envoys of Simo and Yipan came together.

sentences.zh: 開元十二年，授王布遮波資金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kaiyuan King Buzhebo was appointed Golden Guard Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Kaiyuan King Buzhebo was appointed Golden Guard Grand General.

sentences.zh: 天寶六載，王跌失伽延從討勃律戰死，擢其子都督、左武衛將軍，給祿居藩。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianbao King Dieshijiayan died campaigning against Bolü; his son was promoted military governor and Left Martial Guard General with stipend while residing at the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianbao King Dieshijiayan died campaigning against Bolü; his son was promoted military governor and Left Martial Guard General.

sentences.zh: 似沒似沒者，北接石。

translations.literal: Simo lay north connecting with Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Simo lay north connecting with Shi.

sentences.zh: 土俗與康同。

translations.literal: Customs and soil resembled Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Customs and soil resembled Kang.

sentences.zh: 役槃，亦與康鄰。

translations.literal: Yipan also bordered Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Yipan also bordered Kang.

sentences.zh: 出良馬。

translations.literal: It produced fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: It produced fine horses.

sentences.zh: 俱蜜俱蜜者，治山中。

translations.literal: Jumi was governed in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Jumi was governed in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 在吐火羅東北，南臨黑河。

translations.literal: Northeast of Tuhuoluo, south on the Black River.
translations.idiomatic: Northeast of Tuhuoluo, south on the Black River.

sentences.zh: 其王突厥延陀種。

translations.literal: Its king was of Turkic Yantuo stock.
translations.idiomatic: Its king was of Turkic Yantuo stock.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十六年，遣使者入朝。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhenguan envoys came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Zhenguan envoys came to court.

sentences.zh: 開元中，獻胡旋舞女，其王那羅延頗言為大食暴賦，天子但尉遣而已。

translations.literal: During Kaiyuan they presented Hu-spinning dancing girls; King Naluoyan complained greatly of Arab exactions; the Son of Heaven only consoled and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan they presented Hu-spinning dancing girls; King Naluoyan complained of Arab exactions; the emperor only consoled him.

sentences.zh: 天寶時，王伊悉爛俟斤又獻馬。

translations.literal: During Tianbao King Yixilanhoujin again presented horses.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao King Yixilanhoujin again presented horses.

sentences.zh: 護蜜護蜜者，或曰達摩悉鐵帝，曰鑊侃，元魏所謂缽和者，亦吐火羅故地。

translations.literal: Humi, also called Damoxitiedi or Huokan, was what Northern Wei called Bohe—also former Tuhuoluo territory.
translations.idiomatic: Humi, also called Damoxitiedi or Huokan, was Northern Wei's Bohe—former Tuhuoluo territory.

sentences.zh: 東南直京師九千里而贏，橫千六百里，縱狹才四五里。

translations.literal: Southeast directly nine thousand li from the capital with surplus, sixteen hundred li across, only four or five li wide north to south.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast nine thousand li from the capital, sixteen hundred by four or five li.

sentences.zh: 王居塞迦審城，北臨烏滸河。

translations.literal: The king dwelt at Saikashen City, north on the Wuhu River.
translations.idiomatic: The king dwelt at Saikashen City, north on the Wuhu River.

sentences.zh: 地寒洹，堆阜曲折，沙石流漫。

translations.literal: The land was cold and damp with winding heaps and mounds; sand and stones flowed spread.
translations.idiomatic: Cold and damp with winding mounds; sand and stones spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 有豆、麥，宜木果，出善馬。

translations.literal: There were beans and wheat, suited to tree fruits, and fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: Beans, wheat, tree fruits, and fine horses.

sentences.zh: 人碧瞳。

translations.literal: People had green eyes.
translations.idiomatic: People had green eyes.

sentences.zh: 顯慶時以地為鳥飛州，王沙缽羅頡利發為刺史。

translations.literal: During Xianqing the territory was made Wufei Prefecture and King Shaboluolilifa was appointed prefect.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianqing the territory became Wufei Prefecture; King Shaboluolilifa was appointed prefect.

sentences.zh: 地當四鎮入吐火羅道，故役屬吐蕃。

translations.literal: The land lay on the Four Garrisons route into Tuhuoluo, hence subject to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: It lay on the Four Garrisons route into Tuhuoluo, hence subject to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 開元八年，冊其王羅旅伊陀骨咄祿多毗勒莫賀達摩薩爾為王。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kaiyuan their king Luolüyituoguduliduolimohedamosier was invested king.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Kaiyuan their king was invested.

sentences.zh: 十六年，與米首領米忽汗同獻方物。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, together with Mi chieftain Mihuhan, they presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, with Mi chieftain Mihuhan, they presented local products.

sentences.zh: 明年，大酋烏鶻達幹復朝。

translations.literal: The next year great chieftain Wugudagan again came to court.
translations.idiomatic: The next year great chieftain Wugudagan came to court.

sentences.zh: 王死，冊其從弟護真檀嗣王。

translations.literal: When the king died his younger cousin Huzhen was invested successor king.
translations.idiomatic: When the king died his cousin Huzhen was invested successor king.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，身入朝，宴內殿，拜左金吾衛將軍，賜紫袍、金帶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he came in person to court, was feasted in the inner palace, appointed Left Golden Guard General, and granted a purple robe and golden belt.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he came in person, was feasted in the inner palace, and appointed Left Golden Guard General.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，王子頡吉匐請絕吐蕃，賜鐵券。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao the prince Jiejifu requested to break with Tibet and was granted an iron certificate.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao Prince Jiejifu requested to break with Tibet and was granted an iron certificate.

sentences.zh: 八載，真檀來朝，請宿衛，詔可。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Huzhen came to court requesting to remain as guard; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Huzhen came requesting to remain as guard; permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 授右武衛將軍，久乃遣。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Martial Guard General and sent home only after a long time.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Martial Guard General and sent home only after a long time.

sentences.zh: 又遣首領朝貢。

translations.literal: Chieftains again came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Chieftains again came with tribute.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年，王紇設伊俱鼻施來朝，賜氏李。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan King Heshe Yijubishi came to court and was granted the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianyuan King Heshe Yijubishi came to court and was granted the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 個失蜜個失蜜，或曰迦濕彌邏。

translations.literal: Geshimi, also called Jiashimiluo.
translations.idiomatic: Geshimi, also called Jiashimiluo.

sentences.zh: 北距勃律五百里，環地四千里，山回繚之，它國無能攻伐。

translations.literal: Five hundred li north of Bolü, four thousand li round, mountains encircling it; no other state could attack it.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred li north of Bolü, four thousand li round, mountain-encircled and impregnable.

sentences.zh: 王治撥邏勿邏布邏城，西瀕彌那悉多大河。

translations.literal: The king governed Boluoboluo City, west on the Minasiddha Great River.
translations.idiomatic: The king governed Boluoboluo City, west on the Minasiddha Great River.

sentences.zh: 地宜稼。

translations.literal: The soil suited crops.
translations.idiomatic: The soil suited crops.

sentences.zh: 多雪不風。

translations.literal: Much snow, little wind.
translations.idiomatic: Much snow, little wind.

sentences.zh: 出火珠、郁金、龍種馬。

translations.literal: It produced fire pearls, turmeric, and dragon-seed horses.
translations.idiomatic: It produced fire pearls, turmeric, and dragon-seed horses.

sentences.zh: 俗毛褐。

translations.literal: By custom they wore wool and felt.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they wore wool and felt.

sentences.zh: 世傳地本龍池，龍徙水竭，故往居之。

translations.literal: Tradition held the land was originally a dragon pool; when the dragon moved the water dried, hence they went to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition held the land was a dragon pool; when the dragon moved and the water dried, they settled there.

sentences.zh: 開元初，遣使者朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan envoys came to court.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyuan envoys came to court.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔冊其王真陀羅秘利為王；

translations.literal: In the eighth year an edict invested their king Zhentuoluomili as king;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year their king Zhentuoluomili was invested king;

sentences.zh: 間獻胡藥。

translations.literal: from time to time they presented Hu drugs.
translations.idiomatic: from time to time they presented Hu drugs.

sentences.zh: 天木死，弟木多筆立，遣使者物理多來朝，且言：「有國以來，並臣天可汗，受調發。

translations.literal: When King Tianmu died his younger brother Moduobi succeeded; envoys Wuliduo came to court, stating: "Since our state was founded we have all served the Heavenly Kagan and accepted mobilization.
translations.idiomatic: When King Tianmu died his brother Moduobi succeeded; envoy Wuliduo stated they had always served the Heavenly Kagan.

sentences.zh: 國有象、馬、步三種兵，臣身與中天竺王厄吐蕃五大道，禁出入，戰輒勝。

translations.literal: The state had elephant, horse, and infantry armies; I personally with the Central India king blocked the five great Tibetan routes, forbidding passage, and always won in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The state had elephant, horse, and infantry armies; I with the Central India king blocked five Tibetan routes and always won.

sentences.zh: 有如天可汗兵至勃律者，雖眾二十萬，能輸糧以助。

translations.literal: If Heavenly Kagan troops reach Bolü, though two hundred thousand strong, we can supply grain to assist.
translations.idiomatic: If Heavenly Kagan troops reach Bolü, even two hundred thousand, we can supply grain.

sentences.zh: 又國有摩訶波多磨龍池，願為天可汗營祠。」

translations.literal: Also the state has the Mahabodhi Dragon Pool; we wish to build a shrine for the Heavenly Kagan.
translations.idiomatic: Also we have the Mahabodhi Dragon Pool and wish to build a shrine for the Heavenly Kagan.

sentences.zh: 因丐王冊，鴻臚譯以聞。

translations.literal: He therefore begged investiture as king; the Court of Ceremonies translated and reported.
translations.idiomatic: He begged investiture as king; the Court of Ceremonies translated and reported.

sentences.zh: 詔內物理多宴中殿，賜賚優備，冊木多筆為王，自是職貢有常。

translations.literal: An edict feasted Wuliduo in the middle hall with lavish gifts and invested Moduobi as king; tribute thereafter was regular.
translations.idiomatic: Wuliduo was feasted in the middle hall and Moduobi was invested king; tribute became regular.

sentences.zh: 其役屬五種，亦名國。

translations.literal: Its subject five tribes were also called states.
translations.idiomatic: Its five subject tribes were also called states.

sentences.zh: 所謂呾叉始羅者，地二千里，有都城。

translations.literal: The so-called Dachashiluo had two thousand li of territory with a capital city.
translations.idiomatic: Dachashiluo had two thousand li with a capital city.

sentences.zh: 東南餘七百里得僧訶補羅，地三千餘里，亦治都城。

translations.literal: Seven hundred li southeast reached Senghebula, three thousand plus li with a capital city.
translations.idiomatic: Seven hundred li southeast was Senghebula, three thousand plus li with a capital.

sentences.zh: 東南山行五百里得烏剌屍，地二千里，有都城。

translations.literal: Five hundred li southeast by mountain road reached Wulashi, two thousand li with a capital city.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred li southeast by mountain road was Wulashi, two thousand li with a capital.

sentences.zh: 宜稼穡。

translations.literal: Suited to crops.
translations.idiomatic: Suited to crops.

sentences.zh: 東南限山千里即個失蜜。

translations.literal: A thousand li southeast bounded by mountains was Geshimi.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand li southeast bounded by mountains was Geshimi.

sentences.zh: 西南行險七百里得半笯蹉，地二千里。

translations.literal: Seven hundred li southwest by dangerous route reached Bannacuo, two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Seven hundred li southwest by dangerous route was Bannacuo, two thousand li.

sentences.zh: 又得曷邏阇補羅者，其大四千里，有都城，多山阜，人驍勇。

translations.literal: Also Heluojianbula, four thousand li across with a capital, many hills, and fierce warriors.
translations.idiomatic: Also Heluojianbula, four thousand li with a capital and fierce warriors.

sentences.zh: 五種皆無君長雲。

translations.literal: All five tribes had no rulers, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: All five tribes had no rulers, it is said.

sentences.zh: 骨咄骨咄，或曰珂咄羅。

translations.literal: Gudu. Gudu, also called Kedouluo.
translations.idiomatic: Gudu. Also called Kedouluo.

sentences.zh: 廣長皆千里。

translations.literal: Both length and width were a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Both length and width were a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 王治思助建城。

translations.literal: The king governed Sizhujian City.
translations.idiomatic: The king governed Sizhujian City.

sentences.zh: 多良馬、赤豹。

translations.literal: Many fine horses and red leopards.
translations.idiomatic: Many fine horses and red leopards.

sentences.zh: 有四大鹽山，山出烏鹽。

translations.literal: There were four great salt mountains producing black salt.
translations.idiomatic: Four great salt mountains produced black salt.

sentences.zh: 開元十七年，王俟斤遣子骨都施來朝。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kaiyuan King Houjin sent his son Gudushi to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Kaiyuan King Houjin sent his son Gudushi to court.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，王頡利發獻女樂，又遣大首領多博勒達幹朝貢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year King Felifa presented female musicians and sent great chieftain Duoboledagan with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year King Felifa presented female musicians and sent great chieftain Duoboledagan with tribute.

sentences.zh: 天寶十一載，冊其王羅全節為葉護。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianbao their king Luoquanjie was invested Yehu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Tianbao King Luoquanjie was invested Yehu.

sentences.zh: 蘇毗蘇毗，本西羌族，為吐蕃所並，號孫波，在諸部最大。

translations.literal: Supi. Supi was originally a Western Qiang tribe, annexed by Tibet and styled Sunbo; among the tribes it was largest.
translations.idiomatic: Supi. Originally a Western Qiang tribe annexed by Tibet as Sunbo; largest among the tribes.

sentences.zh: 東與多彌接，西距鶻莽硤，戶三萬。

translations.literal: East it connected with Duomi, west bordered Gumangxia, thirty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: East to Duomi, west to Gumangxia, thirty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，王沒陵贊欲舉國內附，為吐蕃所殺。

translations.literal: During Tianbao King Molingzan wished to lead the entire state to submit inward but was killed by Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao King Molingzan wished to submit inward but was killed by Tibet.

sentences.zh: 子悉諾率首領奔隴右，節度使哥舒翰護送闕下，玄宗厚禮之。

translations.literal: His son Sinuo led chieftains to flee to Longyou; Military Governor Geshu Han escorted them to court and Emperor Xuanzong treated them generously.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sinuo fled to Longyou; Geshu Han escorted them to court and Xuanzong treated them generously.

sentences.zh: 多彌多彌，亦西羌族，役屬吐蕃，號難磨。

translations.literal: Duomi was also a Western Qiang tribe, subject to Tibet, styled Nanmo.
translations.idiomatic: Duomi was also Western Qiang, subject to Tibet, styled Nanmo.

sentences.zh: 濱犁牛河，土多黃金。

translations.literal: Bordering the Plough Ox River, the soil had much gold.
translations.idiomatic: Bordering the Plough Ox River, the soil had much gold.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年，遣使者朝貢，賜遣之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan envoys came with tribute and were sent home with gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenguan envoys came with tribute and were sent home with gifts.

sentences.zh: 伊吾城伊吾城者，漢宜禾都尉所治。

translations.literal: Yiwu City was where the Han Yihai Colonel was stationed.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwu City was where the Han Yihai Colonel was stationed.

sentences.zh: 商胡雜居，勝兵千，附鐵勒。

translations.literal: Merchants of many states lived mixed; effective fighting forces a thousand, attached to the Tiele.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants lived mixed; a thousand warriors, attached to the Tiele.

sentences.zh: 人驍悍，土良沃。

translations.literal: The people were fierce; the soil was fertile.
translations.idiomatic: The people were fierce; the soil was fertile.

sentences.zh: 隋末內屬，置伊吾郡。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui it submitted inward and Yiwu Commandery was established.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Sui it submitted and Yiwu Commandery was established.

sentences.zh: 天下亂，復臣突厥。

translations.literal: When the empire fell into turmoil it again became subject to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: When the empire fell into turmoil it again became subject to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年，城酋來朝。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan the city chieftain came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenguan the city chieftain came to court.

sentences.zh: 頡利滅，舉七城降，列其地為西伊州。

translations.literal: When Jieli fell seven cities submitted and their lands were organized as West Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Jieli fell seven cities submitted and their lands became West Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 師子師子，居西南海中，延袤二千餘里。

translations.literal: Shizi lay in the southwestern sea, more than two thousand li in length.
translations.idiomatic: Shizi lay in the southwestern sea, more than two thousand li long.

sentences.zh: 有棱伽山，多奇寶，以寶置洲上，商舶償直輒取去。

translations.literal: There was Mount Lengjia with many strange treasures; treasures were placed on the islet and merchant ships paid price and took them away.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Lengjia had strange treasures placed on an islet for merchant ships to buy.

sentences.zh: 後鄰國人稍往居之。

translations.literal: Later people of neighboring states gradually went to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Later neighboring peoples gradually settled there.

sentences.zh: 能馴養師子，因以名國。

translations.literal: They could tame lions, hence the state name.
translations.idiomatic: They could tame lions, hence the state name.

sentences.zh: 總章三年，遣使者來朝。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zongzhang envoys came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zongzhang envoys came to court.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，王屍羅迷迦再遣使獻大珠、鈿金、寶瓔、象齒、白氎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao King Shiluomijia again sent envoys presenting great pearls, inlaid gold, jeweled tassels, ivory, and white felt.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao King Shiluomijia sent great pearls, inlaid gold, jeweled tassels, ivory, and white felt.

sentences.zh: 波斯波斯，居達遏水西，距京師萬五千里而贏。

translations.literal: Persia lay west of the Dada River, fifteen thousand li from the capital with surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Persia lay west of the Dada River, fifteen thousand li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 東與吐火羅、康接，北鄰突厥可薩部，西南皆瀕海，西北贏四千里，拂菻也。

translations.literal: East it connected with Tuhuoluo and Kang, north neighbored the Turk Khasar tribe, southwest all bordered the sea, northwest four thousand li with surplus to Fulin.
translations.idiomatic: East to Tuhuoluo and Kang, north to Turk Khasar, southwest to the sea, northwest to Fulin.

sentences.zh: 人數十萬，其先波斯匿王，大月氏別裔，王因以姓，又為國號。

translations.literal: People numbered several hundred thousand; their ancestor was King Bosini of the Greater Yuezhi branch; the king took it as surname and also as state name.
translations.idiomatic: People numbered several hundred thousand; their ancestor was King Bosini of the Greater Yuezhi branch.

sentences.zh: 治二城，有大城十餘。

translations.literal: They governed two cities with more than ten great cities.
translations.idiomatic: They governed two cities with more than ten great cities.

sentences.zh: 俗尊右下左，祠天地日月水火。

translations.literal: By custom they honored the right and lowered the left, worshipping heaven, earth, sun, moon, fire, and water.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they honored the right over the left, worshipping heaven, earth, sun, moon, fire, and water.

sentences.zh: 祠夕，以麝揉蘇，澤耏顏鼻耳。

translations.literal: At evening sacrifice they rubbed musk and applied it to face, nose, and ears.
translations.idiomatic: At evening sacrifice they rubbed musk on face, nose, and ears.

sentences.zh: 西域諸胡受其法，以祠祅。

translations.literal: Various Hu of the Western Regions received their method to worship the Zoroastrian god.
translations.idiomatic: Various Hu received their method to worship the Zoroastrian god.

sentences.zh: 拜必交股。

translations.literal: In bowing they always crossed their legs.
translations.idiomatic: In bowing they always crossed their legs.

sentences.zh: 俗徒跣，丈夫祝髮，衣不剖襟，青白為巾帔，緣以錦。

translations.literal: By custom they went barefoot; husbands shaved their heads and wore garments without split fronts, green and white as turban and cape, edged with brocade.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they went barefoot; men shaved their heads in uncut-front garments with brocade-edged turbans.

sentences.zh: 婦辮發著後。

translations.literal: Women braided their hair behind.
translations.idiomatic: Women braided their hair behind.

sentences.zh: 戰乘象，一象士百人，負則盡殺。

translations.literal: In battle they rode elephants; one elephant soldier had a hundred men; if he fled all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: In battle they rode elephants; one elephant soldier had a hundred men; if he fled all were killed.

sentences.zh: 斷罪不為文書，決於廷。

translations.literal: Judgment of crimes did not use documents but was decided in court.
translations.idiomatic: Crimes were decided in court without documents.

sentences.zh: 叛者鐵灼其舌，瘡白為直，黑為曲。

translations.literal: Rebels had their tongues iron-burned; white scar meant straight, black meant crooked.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels had their tongues iron-burned; white scar meant straight, black crooked.

sentences.zh: 刑有髡、鉗、刖、劓，小罪耏，或系木於頸，以時月而置。

translations.literal: Punishments included shaving, shackling, cutting feet, and slicing nose; minor crimes meant whipping or wooden collars around the neck for set months.
translations.idiomatic: Punishments included shaving, shackling, amputation, and slicing nose; minor crimes meant whipping or wooden collars.

sentences.zh: 劫盜囚終老，偷者輸銀錢。

translations.literal: Robbers and bandits were imprisoned until old age; thieves paid silver coins.
translations.idiomatic: Robbers were imprisoned for life; thieves paid silver.

sentences.zh: 凡死，棄於山，服閱月除。

translations.literal: For death the body was abandoned on mountains; mourning garments were removed after a month.
translations.idiomatic: The dead were abandoned on mountains; mourning ended after a month.

sentences.zh: 氣常熱，地夷漫，知耕種畜牧。

translations.literal: The climate was constantly hot; the land was level and wide; they knew cultivation and herding.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was hot; the land level; they farmed and herded.

sentences.zh: 有鷲鳥，能啖羊。

translations.literal: There were vulture birds able to eat sheep.
translations.idiomatic: There were vulture birds able to eat sheep.

sentences.zh: 多善犬、█婁、大驢。

translations.literal: Many fine dogs, carpets, and great donkeys.
translations.idiomatic: Many fine dogs, carpets, and great donkeys.

sentences.zh: 產珊瑚，高不三尺。

translations.literal: Coral was produced, no more than three chi high.
translations.idiomatic: Coral was produced, no more than three chi high.

sentences.zh: 隋末，西突厥葉護可汗討殘其國，殺王庫薩和，其子施利立，葉護使部帥監統。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui the Western Turk Khan Yehu campaigned against and destroyed their state, killing King Kusahe; his son Shili succeeded and Yehu had a tribal commander supervise.
translations.idiomatic: At Sui's end Western Turk Khan Yehu destroyed their state, killing King Kusahe; his son Shili succeeded under Turk supervision.

sentences.zh: 施利死，遂不肯臣。

translations.literal: When Shili died they refused to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Shili died they refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 立庫薩和女為王，突厥又殺之。

translations.literal: Kusahe's daughter was established as queen; the Turks killed her again.
translations.idiomatic: Kusahe's daughter was made queen; the Turks killed her again.

sentences.zh: 施利之子單羯方奔拂菻，國人迎立之，是為伊怛支。

translations.literal: Shili's son Danjiefang fled to Fulin; the people welcomed and established him—this was Yidizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shili's son Danjiefang fled to Fulin and was established as Yidizhi.

sentences.zh: 死，兄子伊嗣俟立。

translations.literal: When he died his elder brother's son Yisiqi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his nephew Yisiqi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十二年，遣使者沒似半朝貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhenguan envoys Mosiban came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhenguan envoy Mosiban came with tribute.

sentences.zh: 又獻活褥蛇，狀類鼠，色正青，長九寸，能捕穴鼠。

translations.literal: They also presented the living mattress snake, shaped like a rat, pure green, nine cun long, able to catch burrowing rats.
translations.idiomatic: They also presented the living mattress snake, rat-shaped, green, nine cun long, catching burrowing rats.

sentences.zh: 伊嗣俟不君，為大酋所逐，奔吐火羅，半道，大食擊殺之。

translations.literal: Yisiqi misruled and was driven out by great chieftains; fleeing to Tuhuoluo, halfway the Arabs struck and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yisiqi misruled, was driven out, fled to Tuhuoluo, and was killed by the Arabs en route.

sentences.zh: 子卑路斯入吐火羅以免。

translations.literal: His son Beilusi entered Tuhuoluo to escape.
translations.idiomatic: His son Beilusi entered Tuhuoluo to escape.

sentences.zh: 遣使者告難，高宗以遠不可師，謝遣。

translations.literal: Envoys reported their distress; Emperor Gaozong, finding the distance too great for troops, declined and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys reported distress; Gaozong declined troops and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 會大食解而去，吐火羅以兵納之。

translations.literal: When the Arabs withdrew, Tuhuoluo brought troops to install him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Arabs withdrew, Tuhuoluo installed him with troops.

sentences.zh: 龍朔初，又訴為大食所侵，是時天子方遣使者到西域分置州縣，以疾陵城為波斯都督府，即拜卑路斯為都督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longshuo they again complained of Arab invasion; the Son of Heaven was then dispatching envoys to the Western Regions to establish prefectures and counties; Jiling City was made the Persian Military Governorship and Beilusi was appointed military governor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longshuo they again complained of Arabs; Jiling City became the Persian Military Governorship and Beilusi was appointed military governor.

sentences.zh: 俄為大食所滅。

translations.literal: Soon they were destroyed by the Arabs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they were destroyed by the Arabs.

sentences.zh: 雖不能國，咸亨中猶入朝，授右武衛將軍，死。

translations.literal: Though they could not preserve the state, during Xianheng they still came to court; Beilusi was appointed Right Martial Guard General and died.
translations.idiomatic: Though the state fell, during Xianheng Beilusi still came to court as Right Martial Guard General and died.
