sentences.zh: 始，其子泥涅師為質，調露元年，詔裴行儉將兵護還，將復王其國。

translations.literal: At first his son Nieshi was kept as hostage; in the first year of Tiaolu an edict ordered Pei Xingjian to lead troops to escort him back and restore him as king.
translations.idiomatic: His son Nieshi was hostage; in the first year of Tiaolu Pei Xingjian was ordered to restore him as king.

sentences.zh: 以道遠，至安西碎葉，行儉還。

translations.literal: Because the route was far, reaching Suyab in Anxi, Xingjian returned.
translations.idiomatic: The route was far; reaching Suyab in Anxi, Xingjian returned.

sentences.zh: 泥涅師因客吐火羅二十年，部落益離散。

translations.literal: Nieshi then sojourned in Tuhuoluo twenty years and the tribes scattered further.
translations.idiomatic: Nieshi sojourned in Tuhuoluo twenty years as tribes scattered further.

sentences.zh: 景龍初，復來朝，授左威衛將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jinglong he again came to court and was appointed Left Martial Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jinglong he again came to court as Left Martial Guard General.

sentences.zh: 病死，西部獨存。

translations.literal: He died of illness; only the western part remained.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness; only the western part remained.

sentences.zh: 開元、天寶間，遣使者十輩獻碼床、火毛繡舞筵。

translations.literal: During Kaiyuan and Tianbao envoys came ten times presenting agate beds and fire-fur embroidered dance mats.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan and Tianbao envoys came ten times with agate beds and fire-fur dance mats.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，從大食襲廣州，焚倉庫廬舍，浮海走。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyuan, following the Arabs they raided Guangzhou, burned granaries and buildings, and fled by sea.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qianyuan they followed the Arabs raiding Guangzhou, then fled by sea.

sentences.zh: 大歷時復來獻。

translations.literal: During the Dali era they again came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali era they again came with tribute.

sentences.zh: 又有陀拔斯單者，或曰陀拔薩憚。

translations.literal: Also Tuobasidanzhe, also called Tuobasadanzhe.
translations.idiomatic: Also Tuobasidanzhe, also Tuobasadanzhe.

sentences.zh: 其國三面阻山，北瀕小海。

translations.literal: The state was blocked by mountains on three sides and bordered a small sea on the north.
translations.idiomatic: Blocked by mountains on three sides, north bordered a small sea.

sentences.zh: 居婆裏城，世為波斯東大將。

translations.literal: It dwelt at Bolil City; generation after generation served as Persia's eastern great general.
translations.idiomatic: It dwelt at Bolil City, generations serving as Persia's eastern great general.

sentences.zh: 波斯滅，不肯臣大食。

translations.literal: When Persia fell they refused to submit to the Arabs.
translations.idiomatic: When Persia fell they refused Arab submission.

sentences.zh: 天寶五載，王忽魯汗遣使入朝，封為歸信王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianbao King Huluhann sent envoys to court and was enfeoffed King of Guixin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianbao King Huluhann was enfeoffed King of Guixin.

sentences.zh: 後八年，遣子自會羅來朝，拜右武衛員外中郎將，賜紫袍、金魚，留宿衛。

translations.literal: Eight years later his son Ziluoluo came to court, appointed Right Martial Guard External Lieutenant General, granted purple robe and golden fish, remaining as palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Eight years later his son Ziluoluo came to court as Right Martial Guard External Lieutenant General and palace guard.

sentences.zh: 為黑衣大食所滅。

translations.literal: They were destroyed by the Black-robed Arabs.
translations.idiomatic: They were destroyed by the Black-robed Arabs.

sentences.zh: 貞觀後，遠小國君遣使者來朝獻，有司未嘗參考本末者，今附之左方。

translations.literal: After Zhenguan, distant small-state rulers sent envoys to court with tribute whom the offices had never referenced from beginning to end; they are appended here on the left.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhenguan, distant small-state envoys never fully documented are appended here.

sentences.zh: 曰火辭彌，與波斯接。

translations.literal: Called Huocimi, connecting with Persia.
translations.idiomatic: Called Huocimi, connecting with Persia.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十八年，與摩羅遊使者偕朝。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Zhenguan they came to court together with envoys of Moluoyou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Zhenguan they came with envoys of Moluoyou.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，有健達王獻佛土菜，莖五葉，赤華紫須。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year King Jianda presented Buddha-soil vegetable with five-leaf stems and red flowers with purple filaments.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year King Jianda presented Buddha-soil vegetable with five-leaf stems and red flowers.

sentences.zh: 龍朔元年，多福王難婆修強宜說遣使者來朝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longshuo King Duofuwang Nanpoxiuqiangyishuo sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longshuo King Nanpoxiuqiangyishuo sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 總章元年，有末陀提王，開元五年，有習阿薩般王安殺，並遣使者朝貢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zongzhang there was King Moditi; in the fifth year of Kaiyuan there was King Xi'asaban Ansha—all sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zongzhang King Moditi; in the fifth year of Kaiyuan King Ansha—all sent envoys.

sentences.zh: 七年，訶毗施王捺塞因吐火羅大酋羅摩獻師子、五色鸚鵡。

translations.literal: In the seventh year King Nase of Hepishi presented lions and five-colored parrots through the great chieftain of Tuhuoluo, Luomo.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year King Nase presented lions and five-colored parrots through Tuhuoluo chieftain Luomo.

sentences.zh: 天寶時來朝者，曰俱爛那，曰舍摩，曰威遠，曰蘇吉利發屋蘭，曰蘇利悉單，曰建城，曰新城，曰俱位，凡八國。

translations.literal: Those who came during Tianbao were Julanna, Shemo, Weiyuan, Sulixidan Wulan, Sulixidan, Jiancheng, Xincheng, and Juwei—eight states in all.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbao visitors included Julanna, Shemo, Weiyuan, and five others—eight states in all.

sentences.zh: 俱位俱位，或曰商彌。

translations.literal: Juwei, also called Shangmi.
translations.idiomatic: Juwei, also called Shangmi.

sentences.zh: 治阿賒師多城，在大雪山、勃律河北。

translations.literal: It governed Asheduoduo City on the great Snow Mountain north of the Bolü River.
translations.idiomatic: It governed Asheduoduo City on the great Snow Mountain north of the Bolü River.

sentences.zh: 地寒，有五谷、蒲陶、若榴，冬窟室。

translations.literal: The land was cold with the five grains, grapes, and pomegranates; in winter they dwelt in cave houses.
translations.idiomatic: Cold land with grains, grapes, and pomegranates; winter cave dwellings.

sentences.zh: 國人常助小勃律為中國候。

translations.literal: The people often assisted Lesser Bolü as scouts for China.
translations.idiomatic: The people often assisted Lesser Bolü as scouts for China.

sentences.zh: 新城之國，在石東北贏百里。

translations.literal: The state of Xincheng lay a hundred plus li northeast of Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Xincheng lay a hundred plus li northeast of Shi.

sentences.zh: 有弩室羯城，亦曰新城，曰小石國城，後為葛邏祿所並。

translations.literal: There was Nushijie City, also called Xincheng or Lesser Shi City, later annexed by the Qarluk.
translations.idiomatic: Nushijie City, also Xincheng or Lesser Shi City, later annexed by the Qarluk.

sentences.zh: 拂菻拂菻，古大秦也，居西海上，一曰海西國。

translations.literal: Fulin. Fulin was ancient Daqin, dwelling on the Western Sea, also called the Kingdom West of the Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Fulin. Ancient Daqin, on the Western Sea, also the Kingdom West of the Sea.

sentences.zh: 去京師四萬里，在苫西，北直突厥可薩部，西瀕海，有遲散城，東南接波斯。

translations.literal: Forty thousand li from the capital, in Shanxi, north directly to the Turk Khasar tribe, west bordering the sea, with Chisan City; southeast connecting with Persia.
translations.idiomatic: Forty thousand li from the capital, west of Shan, north to Turk Khasar, west to the sea, southeast to Persia.

sentences.zh: 地方萬里，城四百，勝兵百萬。

translations.literal: The territory ten thousand li square with four hundred cities and a million effective warriors.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand li square with four hundred cities and a million warriors.

sentences.zh: 十里一亭，三亭一置。

translations.literal: Every ten li a pavilion, every three pavilions a post station.
translations.idiomatic: Every ten li a pavilion, every three pavilions a post station.

sentences.zh: 臣役小國數十，以名通者曰澤散，曰驢分。

translations.literal: It made subjects of several dozen small states; those known by name included Zesan and Lufen.
translations.idiomatic: It subject several dozen small states including Zesan and Lufen.

sentences.zh: 澤散直東北，不得其道裏。

translations.literal: Zesan lay directly northeast; the route li could not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Zesan lay northeast; exact distance unknown.

sentences.zh: 東度海二千里至驢分國。

translations.literal: East across the sea two thousand li reached the Kingdom of Lufen.
translations.idiomatic: East across the sea two thousand li lay Lufen.

sentences.zh: 重石為都城，廣八十里，東門高二十丈，扣以黃金。

translations.literal: Heavy stones formed the capital city, eighty li wide; the east gate twenty zhang high, struck with gold.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy stones formed the capital, eighty li wide; the east gate twenty zhang high, gilded.

sentences.zh: 王宮有三襲門，皆飾異寶。

translations.literal: The royal palace had three layered gates, all adorned with exotic treasures.
translations.idiomatic: The royal palace had three layered gates adorned with exotic treasures.

sentences.zh: 中門中有金巨稱一，作金人立，其端屬十二丸，率時改一丸落。

translations.literal: In the middle gate was a great golden scale with a golden man standing at its end connected to twelve balls; one ball dropped each hour.
translations.idiomatic: In the middle gate a golden scale with a golden man and twelve balls dropping one each hour.

sentences.zh: 以瑟瑟為殿柱，水精、琉璃為棁，香木梁，黃金為地，象牙闔。

translations.literal: Sese formed hall pillars; crystal and glass were rafters; fragrant wood beams; gold floors; ivory doors.
translations.idiomatic: Sese hall pillars, crystal and glass rafters, fragrant wood beams, gold floors, ivory doors.

sentences.zh: 有貴臣十二共治國。

translations.literal: Twelve noble ministers jointly governed the state.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve noble ministers jointly governed the state.

sentences.zh: 王出，一人挈囊以從，有訟書投囊中，還省枉直。

translations.literal: When the king went out, one man carried a bag; lawsuits written and thrown in were examined upon return for right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: When the king went out, one man carried a bag for lawsuit petitions examined upon return.

sentences.zh: 國有大災異，輒廢王更立賢者。

translations.literal: When the state suffered great calamities or anomalies, the king was deposed and a worthy man newly established.
translations.idiomatic: Great calamities meant deposing the king and establishing a worthy successor.

sentences.zh: 王冠如鳥翼，綴珠。

translations.literal: The king's crown was like bird wings adorned with pearls.
translations.idiomatic: The king's crown was like bird wings adorned with pearls.

sentences.zh: 衣錦繡，前無襟。

translations.literal: He wore brocade with no front opening.
translations.idiomatic: He wore brocade with no front opening.

sentences.zh: 坐金蘤榻，側有鳥如鵝，綠毛，上食有毒輒鳴。

translations.literal: He sat on a golden flower couch; beside him was a bird like a goose with green feathers that cried when poison was served.
translations.idiomatic: He sat on a golden flower couch beside a green goose-like bird that cried at poison.

sentences.zh: 無陶瓦，屑白石塈屋，堅潤如玉。

translations.literal: There was no pottery tile; crushed white stone plastered houses, hard and smooth as jade.
translations.idiomatic: No pottery tile; crushed white stone houses hard and smooth as jade.

sentences.zh: 盛暑引水上，流氣為風。

translations.literal: In great summer water was drawn above and flowing air became wind.
translations.idiomatic: In great summer water was drawn above and flowing air became wind.

sentences.zh: 男子翦發、衣繡，右袒而帔，乘輜軿白蓋小車，出入建旌旗，擊鼓。

translations.literal: Men cut their hair and wore brocade, baring the right side with a cape, riding small covered white-canopied carriages; going out they raised banners and beat drums.
translations.idiomatic: Men cut hair, wore brocade baring the right side, rode small covered carriages with banners and drums.

sentences.zh: 婦人錦巾。

translations.literal: Women wore brocade kerchiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore brocade kerchiefs.

sentences.zh: 家訾億萬者為上官。

translations.literal: Households worth hundreds of millions were upper officials.
translations.idiomatic: Households worth hundreds of millions were upper officials.

sentences.zh: 俗喜酒，嗜乾餅。

translations.literal: By custom they loved wine and dried cakes.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they loved wine and dried cakes.

sentences.zh: 多幻人，能發火於顏，手為江湖，口幡毛舉，足墮珠玉。

translations.literal: Many illusionists could emit fire from the face, make rivers and lakes with the hand, raise banners from the mouth, and drop pearls and jade from the feet.
translations.idiomatic: Many illusionists performed fire, water, banner, and pearl tricks.

sentences.zh: 有善醫能開腦出蟲以愈目眚。

translations.literal: There were skilled physicians able to open the skull and remove worms to cure eye blindness.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled physicians opened skulls removing worms to cure blindness.

sentences.zh: 土多金、銀、夜光璧、明月珠、大貝、車渠、碼、木難、孔翠、虎魄。

translations.literal: The soil had much gold, silver, luminous jade, moon pearls, great shells, chequ, agate, munai, kongque, and amber.
translations.idiomatic: The soil had gold, silver, luminous jade, moon pearls, shells, chequ, agate, munai, kongque, and amber.

sentences.zh: 織水羊毛為布，曰海西布。

translations.literal: They wove water-sheep wool into cloth called sea-west cloth.
translations.idiomatic: They wove water-sheep wool into sea-west cloth.

sentences.zh: 海中有珊瑚洲，海人乘大舶，墮鐵網水底。

translations.literal: In the sea was Coral Isle; seafolk rode great ships and dropped iron nets to the bottom.
translations.idiomatic: In the sea was Coral Isle; seafolk dropped iron nets from great ships.

sentences.zh: 珊瑚初生磐石上，白如菌，一歲而黃，三歲赤，枝格交錯，高三四尺。

translations.literal: Coral first grew on rocks white as fungus; in one year yellow, in three red, branches interlacing three or four chi high.
translations.idiomatic: Coral grew on rocks white as fungus, yellow in one year, red in three, branches three or four chi high.

sentences.zh: 鐵發其根，系網舶上，絞而出之，失時不敢即腐。

translations.literal: Iron was sent to the roots, nets tied to the ship, winched out; missing the time it rotted at once.
translations.idiomatic: Iron reached the roots, nets winched out; missing the time it rotted.

sentences.zh: 西海有市，貿易不相見，置直物旁，名鬼市。

translations.literal: In the Western Sea was a market where trade occurred without seeing one another; goods were placed with prices—a ghost market.
translations.idiomatic: In the Western Sea was a ghost market trading without meeting.

sentences.zh: 有獸名，大如狗，獷惡而力。

translations.literal: There was a beast called , large as a dog, fierce and strong.
translations.idiomatic: There was a fierce beast large as a dog.

sentences.zh: 北邑有羊，生土中，臍屬地，割必死，俗介馬而走，擊鼓以驚之，羔臍絕，即逐水草，不能群，

translations.literal: In the northern region were sheep born from the soil with navels attached to earth; cutting meant death; by custom they rode horses to drive them, beating drums to startle them; lambs broke the navel and followed grass and water, unable to flock.
translations.idiomatic: Northern sheep were born from soil with earth-attached navels; cutting killed them; drums startled lambs to break free.

sentences.zh: 王波多力遣使獻赤玻黎、綠金精，下詔答賚。

translations.literal: King Boduoli sent envoys presenting red glass and green gold essence; an edict responded with gifts.
translations.idiomatic: King Boduoli sent red glass and green gold essence; an edict responded with gifts.

sentences.zh: 大食稍強，遣大將軍摩拽伐之，拂菻約和，遂臣屬。

translations.literal: The Arabs grew somewhat stronger; a great general was dispatched to campaign against them; Fulin made peace and thereupon became a subject state.
translations.idiomatic: The Arabs grew stronger; Fulin made peace and became a subject state.

sentences.zh: 乾封至大足，再朝獻，

translations.literal: From Qianfeng through Dazu they came twice with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: From Qianfeng through Dazu they came twice with tribute.

sentences.zh: 因吐火羅大酋獻師子、羚羊。

translations.literal: Through the great chieftain of Tuhuoluo they presented lions and antelope.
translations.idiomatic: Through Tuhuoluo's great chieftain they presented lions and antelope.

sentences.zh: 自拂菻西南度磧二千里，有國曰磨鄰，曰老勃薩。

translations.literal: Southwest of Fulin crossing the desert two thousand li were the states of Molin and Laobosa.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest of Fulin two thousand li across the desert were Molin and Laobosa.

sentences.zh: 其人黑而性悍。

translations.literal: The people were black and fierce by nature.
translations.idiomatic: The people were black and fierce.

sentences.zh: 地瘴癘，無草木五谷，飼馬以槁魚，人食鶻莽。

translations.literal: The land had miasma without plants or the five grains; horses were fed dried fish and people ate qu mang.
translations.idiomatic: Miasmic land without crops; horses fed dried fish, people ate qu mang.

sentences.zh: 鶻莽，波斯棗也。

translations.literal: Qu mang was Persian jujube.
translations.idiomatic: Qu mang was Persian jujube.

sentences.zh: 不恥烝報，於夷狄最甚，號曰「尋」。

translations.literal: They did not shame themselves for incest; among the barbarians they were the worst, styled "Xun."
translations.idiomatic: They did not shame incest; among barbarians the worst, styled Xun.

sentences.zh: 其君臣七日一休，不出納交易，飲以窮夜。

translations.literal: Ruler and ministers rested one day in seven without conducting transactions, drinking through the night.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and ministers rested one day in seven, drinking through the night.

sentences.zh: 大食大食，本波斯地。

translations.literal: The Arabs. The Arabs were originally Persian lands.
translations.idiomatic: The Arabs. Originally Persian lands.

sentences.zh: 男子鼻高，黑而髯。

translations.literal: Men had high noses, were black and bearded.
translations.idiomatic: Men had high noses, were black and bearded.

sentences.zh: 女子白皙，出輒鄣面。

translations.literal: Women were fair-skinned and veiled their faces when going out.
translations.idiomatic: Women were fair-skinned and veiled when going out.

sentences.zh: 日五拜天神。

translations.literal: Five times daily they worshipped the heavenly god.
translations.idiomatic: Five times daily they worshipped the heavenly god.

sentences.zh: 銀帶，佩銀刀，不飲酒舉樂。

translations.literal: Silver belts, silver knives at the waist, no wine or music.
translations.idiomatic: Silver belts and knives, no wine or music.

sentences.zh: 有禮堂容數百人，率七日，王高坐為下說曰：「死敵者生天上，殺敵受福。」

translations.literal: There was a ritual hall holding several hundred men; every seven days the king sat high and preached below: "Those who die fighting enemies live in heaven; killing enemies receive blessing.
translations.idiomatic: A ritual hall held hundreds; every seven days the king preached that dying fighting enemies meant heaven.

sentences.zh: 故俗勇於鬥。

translations.literal: Hence by custom they were brave in battle."
translations.idiomatic: Hence by custom they were brave in battle."

sentences.zh: 土饒礫不可耕，獵而食肉。

translations.literal: The soil was stony and could not be plowed; they hunted and ate meat.
translations.idiomatic: Stony soil could not be plowed; they hunted and ate meat.

sentences.zh: 刻石蜜為廬如輿狀，歲獻貴人。

translations.literal: Rock sugar was carved into hut-like dwellings like palanquins and presented yearly to nobles.
translations.idiomatic: Rock sugar was carved into hut-like dwellings presented yearly to nobles.

sentences.zh: 蒲陶大者如雞卵。

translations.literal: Grapes as large as chicken eggs.
translations.idiomatic: Grapes as large as chicken eggs.

sentences.zh: 有千里馬，傳為龍種。

translations.literal: There were thousand-li horses, transmitted as dragon seed.
translations.idiomatic: There were thousand-li horses, transmitted as dragon seed.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，有波斯國人牧於俱紛摩地那山，有獸言曰：「山西三穴，有利兵，黑石而白文，得之者王。」

translations.literal: During Sui Daye a Persian herded at Mount Junfenmodina; a beast spoke: "Three caves west of the mountain contain profitable weapons—black stone with white markings; whoever obtains it becomes king.
translations.idiomatic: During Sui Daye a Persian herder heard a beast speak of black stone with white markings west of the mountain.

sentences.zh: 走視，如言。

translations.literal: He went to look—it was as said.
translations.idiomatic: He went to look—it was as said.

sentences.zh: 石文言當反，乃詭眾裒亡命於恒曷水，劫商旅，保西鄙自王，移黑石寶之。

translations.literal: The stone's text said he should rebel; he then deceived the crowd gathering fugitives at the Hengyi River, robbing merchants, protecting the western frontier and making himself king, moving the black stone to treasure it.
translations.idiomatic: The stone said rebel; he gathered fugitives at the Hengyi River, robbed merchants, and made himself king.

sentences.zh: 國人往討之，皆大敗還，於是遂強。

translations.literal: The state sent troops to attack; all were greatly defeated and retreated; thus they grew strong.
translations.idiomatic: State troops were defeated; thus they grew strong.

sentences.zh: 滅波斯，破拂菻，始有粟麥倉庾。

translations.literal: They destroyed Persia, broke Fulin, and first had granaries of millet and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: They destroyed Persia, broke Fulin, and first had millet and wheat granaries.

sentences.zh: 南侵婆羅門，並諸國，勝兵至四十萬。

translations.literal: South they invaded Brahmana and all states; effective warriors reached four hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: South they invaded Brahmana; warriors reached four hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 康、石皆往臣之。

translations.literal: Kang and Shi all went to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Kang and Shi all submitted.

sentences.zh: 其地廣萬里，東距突騎施。

translations.literal: Their land ten thousand li square, east bordering the Turgesh.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand li square, east bordering the Turgesh.

sentences.zh: 西南屬海。

translations.literal: Southwest belonged to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest belonged to the sea.

sentences.zh: 海中有撥拔力種，無所附屬。

translations.literal: In the sea was the Baboli tribe, belonging to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: In the sea was the Baboli tribe, belonging to nothing.

sentences.zh: 不生五谷，食肉，刺牛血和乳飲之。

translations.literal: They produced no five grains; they ate meat, piercing cattle blood mixed with milk to drink.
translations.idiomatic: No five grains; they ate meat and drank cattle blood mixed with milk.

sentences.zh: 俗無衣服，以羊皮自蔽。

translations.literal: By custom there were no clothes; sheepskin covered them.
translations.idiomatic: No clothes by custom; sheepskin covered them.

sentences.zh: 婦人明皙而麗。

translations.literal: Women were fair and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Women were fair and beautiful.

sentences.zh: 多象牙及阿末香，波斯賈人欲往市，必數千人納氎镵血誓，乃交易。

translations.literal: Much ivory and aloeswood; Persian merchants wishing to trade had to swear by thousands with felt, blood, and weapons before trading.
translations.idiomatic: Much ivory and aloeswood; Persian merchants swore by thousands before trading.

sentences.zh: 兵多牙角，而有弓、矢、鎧、槊，士至二十萬，數為大食所破略。

translations.literal: Warriors mostly used ivory horns with bows, arrows, armor, and spears; troops reached two hundred thousand, repeatedly plundered by the Arabs.
translations.idiomatic: Warriors used ivory horns with bows and spears; two hundred thousand troops, repeatedly plundered by Arabs.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年，大食王豃密莫末𧸐始遣使者朝貢，自言王大食氏，有國三十四年，傳二世。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui the Arab king Yinmimomo first sent envoys with tribute, stating his royal Arab clan had ruled thirty-four years over two generations.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yonghui the Arab king first sent envoys, stating thirty-four years over two generations.

sentences.zh: 開元初，復遣使獻馬、鈿帶，謁見不拜，有司將劾之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan envoys again came presenting horses and inlaid belts; they bowed without kneeling and the office was about to impeach them.
translations.idiomatic: At Kaiyuan envoys came without kneeling; officials were about to impeach them.

sentences.zh: 中書令張說謂殊俗慕義，不可置於罪。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Yue said exotic peoples admiring righteousness should not be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Yue said exotic peoples admiring righteousness should not be punished.

sentences.zh: 玄宗赦之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 使者又來，辭曰：「國人止拜天，見王無拜也。」

translations.literal: Envoys came again, stating: "Our people worship only heaven; seeing the king requires no bow.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys stated their people worshipped only heaven and bowed to no king.

sentences.zh: 有司切責，乃拜。

translations.literal: The office sternly reproached them and they then bowed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials sternly reproached them and they bowed.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遣使蘇黎滿獻方物，拜果毅，賜緋袍、帶。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year envoy Suliman presented local products, appointed Fruit-and-Courage, granted crimson robe and belt.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year envoy Suliman was appointed Fruit-and-Courage with crimson robe and belt.

sentences.zh: 或曰大食族中有孤列種，世酋長，號白衣大食。

translations.literal: Some say among the Arab tribes was the Guli tribe, hereditary chieftains, styled White-robed Arabs.
translations.idiomatic: Some say the Guli tribe were hereditary chieftains styled White-robed Arabs.

sentences.zh: 種有二姓，一曰盆尼末換，二曰奚深。

translations.literal: The tribe had two surnames: one Penimohuan, one Xishen.
translations.idiomatic: The tribe had two surnames: Penimohuan and Xishen.

sentences.zh: 有摩訶末者，勇而智，眾立為王。

translations.literal: There was Mohemo, brave and wise, whom the crowd established as king.
translations.idiomatic: Mohemo, brave and wise, was established as king.

sentences.zh: 辟地三千里，克夏臘城。

translations.literal: He opened territory three thousand li and captured Xiala City.
translations.idiomatic: He opened territory three thousand li and captured Xiala City.

sentences.zh: 傳十四世，至末換，殺兄伊疾自王，下怨其忍。

translations.literal: Passing fourteen generations to Mohuan, he killed his elder brother Yiji and made himself king; the lower classes resented his cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen generations to Mohuan, who killed his brother Yiji; the lower classes resented his cruelty.

sentences.zh: 有呼羅珊木鹿人並波悉林將討之，徇眾曰：「助我者，皆黑衣。」

translations.literal: A Merv man Bin Bosenlin would campaign against him, proclaiming to the crowd: "Help me and all wear black.
translations.idiomatic: Bin Bosenlin of Merv proclaimed: "Help me and all wear black.

sentences.zh: 俄而眾數萬，即殺末換，求奚深種孫阿蒲羅拔為王，更號黑衣大食。

translations.literal: Soon tens of thousands gathered; Mohuan was killed and the Xishen clan's descendant Apuluoba was sought as king, changing the title to Black-robed Arabs.
translations.idiomatic: Mohuan was killed and Apuluoba of the Xishen clan was made king—the Black-robed Arabs.

sentences.zh: 蒲羅死，弟阿蒲恭拂立。

translations.literal: When Puluo died his younger brother Apugongfu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Puluo died his brother Apugongfu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 至德初，遣使者朝貢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide envoys came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhide envoys came with tribute.

sentences.zh: 代宗取其兵平兩京。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong used their troops to pacify the two capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong used their troops to pacify the two capitals.

sentences.zh: 阿蒲恭拂死，子迷地立。

translations.literal: When Apugongfu died his son Midi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Apugongfu died his son Midi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 死，弟訶論立。

translations.literal: When he died his younger brother Helun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his brother Helun succeeded.

sentences.zh: 貞元時，與吐蕃相攻，吐蕃歲西師，故鮮盜邊。

translations.literal: During the Zhenyuan era they fought with Tibet; Tibet sent western troops yearly, hence they frequently raided the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenyuan they fought Tibet; Tibetan western troops enabled frequent frontier raids.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遣使者含嵯、烏雞、沙北三人朝，皆拜中郎將，賚遣之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year envoys Hancuo, Wuji, and Shabei came to court; all were appointed Lieutenant Generals and sent home with gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year envoys Hancuo, Wuji, and Shabei were appointed Lieutenant Generals and sent home with gifts.

sentences.zh: 傳言其國西南二千里山谷間，有木生花如人首，與語輒笑，則落。

translations.literal: Tradition held two thousand li southwest in a mountain valley was a tree bearing flowers like human heads; speaking to them made them laugh and fall.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition held a tree two thousand li southwest bore human-headed flowers that fell when spoken to.

sentences.zh: 東有末祿，小國也。

translations.literal: East was Molu, a small state.
translations.idiomatic: East was Molu, a small state.

sentences.zh: 治城郭，多木姓，以五月為歲首，以畫缸相獻。

translations.literal: They governed walled cities; many bore the surname Mu; they took the fifth month as year start and exchanged painted jars as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: They governed walled cities; many surnamed Mu; fifth month as year start; painted jars as gifts.

sentences.zh: 有尋支瓜，大者十人食乃盡。

translations.literal: There was the Xunzhi melon; ten men ate before it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: There was the Xunzhi melon requiring ten men to finish.

sentences.zh: 蔬有顆蔥、葛藍、軍達、茇薤。

translations.literal: Vegetables included kecong, gelan, junda, and bixie.
translations.idiomatic: Vegetables included kecong, gelan, junda, and bixie.

sentences.zh: 大食之西有苫者，亦自國。

translations.literal: West of the Arabs was Shan, also an independent state.
translations.idiomatic: West of the Arabs was Shan, also independent.

sentences.zh: 北距突厥可薩部，地數千里。

translations.literal: North bordering the Turk Khasar tribe, several thousand li across.
translations.idiomatic: North bordering Turk Khasar, several thousand li across.

sentences.zh: 有五節度，勝兵萬人。

translations.literal: Five military governorships; ten thousand effective warriors.
translations.idiomatic: Five military governorships; ten thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 土多禾。

translations.literal: The soil had much grain.
translations.idiomatic: The soil had much grain.

sentences.zh: 有大川，東流入亞俱羅。

translations.literal: There was a great river flowing east into Yajuluo.
translations.idiomatic: A great river flowed east into Yajuluo.

sentences.zh: 商賈往來相望雲。

translations.literal: Merchants came and went in unbroken succession.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants came and went in unbroken succession.

sentences.zh: 自大食西十五日行，得都盤，西距羅利支十五日行；

translations.literal: Fifteen days' travel west of the Arabs reached Dupan; west twenty-five days to Luolizhi;
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen days west of the Arabs was Dupan; west twenty-five days to Luolizhi;

sentences.zh: 南即大食，二十五日行；

translations.literal: south was the Arabs, twenty-five days;
translations.idiomatic: south the Arabs, twenty-five days;

sentences.zh: 北勃達，一月行。

translations.literal: north Boda, one month's travel.
translations.idiomatic: north Boda, one month.

sentences.zh: 勃達之東距大食二月行；

translations.literal: East of Boda two months to the Arabs;
translations.idiomatic: East of Boda two months to the Arabs;

sentences.zh: 西抵岐蘭二十日行；

translations.literal: west to Qilan twenty days;
translations.idiomatic: west to Qilan twenty days;

sentences.zh: 南都盤，北大食，皆一月行。

translations.literal: south Dupan, north the Arabs—all one month.
translations.idiomatic: south Dupan, north the Arabs—one month each.

sentences.zh: 岐蘭之東南二十日行，得阿沒，或曰阿昧；

translations.literal: Twenty days southeast of Qilan was Amei, also Ami;
translations.idiomatic: Twenty days southeast of Qilan was Amei;

sentences.zh: 東南距陀拔斯十五日行；

translations.literal: southeast fifteen days to Tuobasi;
translations.idiomatic: southeast fifteen days to Tuobasi;

sentences.zh: 南沙蘭，一月行；

translations.literal: south Shalan, one month;
translations.idiomatic: south Shalan, one month;

sentences.zh: 北距海二日行。

translations.literal: north two days to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: north two days to the sea.

sentences.zh: 居你訶溫多城，宜馬羊，俗柔寬，故大食常遊牧於此。

translations.literal: They dwelt at Nihewenduo City, suited to horses and sheep; by custom gentle and tolerant, hence the Arabs often pastured there.
translations.idiomatic: At Nihewenduo City, suited to horses and sheep; gentle by custom, hence Arab pasturage.

sentences.zh: 沙蘭東距羅利支，北恒滿，皆二十日行；

translations.literal: Shalan east to Luolizhi, north Hengman—all twenty days;
translations.idiomatic: Shalan east to Luolizhi, north Hengman—twenty days;

sentences.zh: 西即大食，二十五日行。

translations.literal: west the Arabs, twenty-five days.
translations.idiomatic: west the Arabs, twenty-five days.

sentences.zh: 羅利支東距都盤，北陀拔斯，皆十五日行；

translations.literal: Luolizhi east to Dupan, north Tuobasi—fifteen days each;
translations.idiomatic: Luolizhi east to Dupan, north Tuobasi—fifteen days;

sentences.zh: 西沙蘭，二十日行；

translations.literal: west Shalan, twenty days;
translations.idiomatic: west Shalan, twenty days;

sentences.zh: 南大食，二十五日行。

translations.literal: south the Arabs, twenty-five days.
translations.idiomatic: south the Arabs, twenty-five days.

sentences.zh: 怛滿怛滿，或曰怛沒，東陀拔斯，南大食，皆一月行；

translations.literal: Hengman, also Hengmo, east to Tuobasi, south the Arabs—one month each;
translations.idiomatic: Hengman, east to Tuobasi, south the Arabs—one month;

sentences.zh: 北岐蘭，二十日行；

translations.literal: north Qilan, twenty days;
translations.idiomatic: north Qilan, twenty days;

sentences.zh: 西即大食，一月行。

translations.literal: west the Arabs, one month.
translations.idiomatic: west the Arabs, one month.

sentences.zh: 居烏滸河北平川中。

translations.literal: It lay in the flat lands north of the Wuhu River.
translations.idiomatic: It lay in flat lands north of the Wuhu River.

sentences.zh: 獸多師子。

translations.literal: Beasts were mostly lions.
translations.idiomatic: Beasts were mostly lions.

sentences.zh: 西北與史接，以鐵關為限。

translations.literal: Northwest connected with Shi, limited by Iron Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest connected with Shi, limited by Iron Pass.

sentences.zh: 天寶六載，都盤等六國皆遣使者入朝，乃封都盤王謀思健摩訶延曰順化王，勃達王摩俱澀斯曰守義王，阿沒王俱那胡設曰恭信王，沙蘭王卑路斯威曰順禮王，羅利支王伊思俱習曰義寧王，怛滿王謝沒曰奉順王。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianbao Dupan and six other states all sent envoys to court; Dupan King Mousijianmoheyan was enfeoffed King of Shunhua, Boda King Mojushensi King of Shouyi, Amei King Junahu King of Gongxin, Shalan King Beiluwei King of Shunli, Luolizhi King Yisijuxi King of Yining, and Hengman King Xiemei King of Fengshun.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianbao six states sent envoys; their kings were enfeoffed with various titles.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：西方之戎，古未嘗通中國，至漢始載烏孫諸國。

translations.literal: Commentary: Western barbarians had never communicated with China from antiquity; only from Han were Wusun and various states first recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Western barbarians rarely reached China before Han records of Wusun and others.

sentences.zh: 後以名字見者浸多。

translations.literal: Later those known by name gradually increased.
translations.idiomatic: Later those known by name gradually increased.

sentences.zh: 唐興，以次脩貢，蓋百餘，皆冒萬里而至，亦已勤矣！

translations.literal: When Tang rose they came in succession with tribute—more than a hundred—all braving ten thousand li to arrive; this was indeed diligence!
translations.idiomatic: When Tang rose more than a hundred came in succession with tribute across ten thousand li—indeed diligence!

sentences.zh: 然中國有報贈、冊吊、程糧、傳驛之費，東至高麗，南至真臘，西至波斯、吐蕃、堅昆，北至突厥、契丹、靺鞨，謂之「八蕃」，其外謂之「絕域」，視地遠近而給費。

translations.literal: Yet China had return gifts, investiture condolences, provision costs, and relay expenses; east to Goguryeo, south to Zhenla, west to Persia, Tibet, and Kirghiz, north to Turks, Khitan, and Mohe—the so-called Eight Barbarians; beyond them the Utterly Remote, fees given according to distance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet China paid return gifts and relay costs to the Eight Barbarians and the Utterly Remote by distance.

sentences.zh: 開元盛時，稅西域商胡以供四鎮，出北道者納賦輪臺。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan's prosperity, Western Regions merchant taxes supplied the Four Garrisons; those on the northern route paid at Luntai.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan's prosperity, Western Regions merchant taxes supplied the Four Garrisons; the northern route paid at Luntai.

sentences.zh: 地廣則費倍，此盛王之鑒也。

translations.literal: Wide territory meant doubled expense—this is the mirror of a flourishing king.
translations.idiomatic: Wide territory meant doubled expense—a mirror for flourishing kings.

sentences.zh: Category:歐洲

translations.literal: Category: Europe
translations.idiomatic: Category: Europe
